# THE GRAIL
### A field guide to browser MUGEN

The knowledge base behind **Energy's WebMUGEN**, a browser port of the
open-source [Ikemen GO](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO)
fighting-game engine, and its Mod Studio. Written for three readers at once:

- **Players** who want to fight, locally and online.
- **Modders** adding characters, stages, music and screenpacks.
- **Developers** building on this fork or porting MUGEN content anywhere.

Part IV is a reference for the **H-MUGEN compatibility model**: the
giver/receiver standard, the pair-animation registries, detection rules and
the mechanics behind the famous breakages.

Every rule here was measured in real files or reproduced in a real engine.
Where a number is a tuned default rather than a universal law, it says so;
where something is a heuristic, it says that too. The history of how each
finding was made lives in the project's DEVLOG, not here.

*Maintained by **energy.jp** (Discord). Powered by the open-source Ikemen GO
engine. Characters and stages are fan-made community content; all rights to
original works belong to their respective owners.*

# Part I — The player's FAQ

## Getting started

**Do I need to download or install anything?**
No. The engine is compiled to WebAssembly and runs in the browser tab. The website only hands over files.

**Why is the first load big?**
The first visit downloads the engine (~17 MB) plus all game data; the boot page shows live progress. Everything is cached after that — later visits are fast, and updates re-download only what changed. `Ctrl+F5` forces a full fresh download.

**Controls:**

| | Move | Punches (X/Y/Z) | Kicks (A/B/C) | Start |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | `W A S D` | `I O P` | `K L ;` | `Enter` |
| **P2** | Arrow keys | Numpad `4 5 6` | Numpad `1 2 3` | Numpad `Enter` |

`Alt+Enter` toggles fullscreen. All bindings are remappable in the in-game Options. Two players on one keyboard is the default local-versus setup.

Press `F1` at any time for the in-game info box; it also opens automatically on first boot.

**Do controllers work?**
Yes — plug in an Xbox-style pad before the page loads. First pad detected is P1, second is P2; keyboard stays active alongside. The config screen shows familiar labels (A/B/X/Y/LB/RB/LT/RT); triggers appearing as "axes" is normal. Default pad layout puts heavy punch on RB and heavy kick on RT.

**Controller is dead, or controls the wrong player.**
Some USB devices (microphones, wheels) falsely enumerate as gamepads and can steal a player slot. Real pads are ranked first automatically; unplugging odd USB hardware is a valid fix. Each detected device logs one console line (`[gamepad N] id= ...`) — the fastest way to check what the browser sees as plugged in.

**No sound until a key is pressed.**
Browsers block audio until the first input. Any keypress resumes it.

## The boot page

- **Online netcode — Rollback / Delay.** Rollback is the default: zero input delay, with the engine re-simulating on late inputs. Delay is the fallback for a connection that stays choppy under rollback. Both players must pick the same mode — a mismatch is refused with a clear message.
- **Picture — 480p / 720p (1280×720).** A real performance trade, not a quality slider: 720p draws over twice the pixels of 480p on the same single thread. **480p keeps the screenpack's shape:** 854×480 when the active screenpack is widescreen, 640×480 only when the pack itself is 4:3. The reason is that the engine letterboxes a FIGHT to its stage but never a menu — a menu takes the window's shape — so a widescreen pack in a 640×480 window loses a sixth of its width off each side: menu items, names, the title. Every screenpack the project ships is widescreen, the stock `ikemen1` one included, so a plain 640×480 option cut the menus of every build. The shape comes from the active motif's `[Info] localcoord` (MUGEN's default 320,240 when absent; widescreen = wider than 1.4:1), read after the player's own theme pick, which can change it. The stored choice is still named `4:3` so returning players keep their pick. No netplay effect: builds ship `FightAspectWidth/Height = -1`, which compares the stage's shape, not the picture's. Offline setting; changing it reloads. **The first visit to an unpacked build gets it too** (2026-10-12): the shipped `save/config.ini` the boot page fetches is kept in the file system it hands the engine, so every patch (theme, `[Common]`, rules, netcode, the picture size) lands in it. Read into a local only, a first visit had nothing to patch and the engine fetched the server's own file: 854×480 while the boot page said 720p. Test: `tools/test-picture-shape.js`, which also boots the unpacked page and a packed export in headless Chrome and measures each canvas.
- **Build ID.** A fingerprint of everything that affects a match: shipped content, every mod added in this browser, and the active theme. For online play it must match the opponent's — the quick eyeball check that both sides loaded the same game.
- **The version.** The page's title carries the bundle's `siteVersion`, and so does the game's F1 box ("Welcome to <title>! (<version>)"). Every build that sets one stamps it into the screenpack's `[Infobox Text]` (`vfslib.js`), public builds included (tools/test-site-version.js). The Build ID hashes paths and sizes, never bytes, so a version of the same length leaves it as it was.
- **Compare with a friend** (under the Build ID line). **Copy mine** puts one chat-pasteable line on the clipboard: Build ID, Engine, Netcode, Upload stamp and three part hashes. The other player pastes it into the box on their boot page and presses **Check**; the page prints one verdict per iron rule — content, engine, netcode, theme — and, when both lines carry the parts, names which half moved: the upload (a different version of the site), the mods (something added or changed in the Studio) or the theme. The plain `Build ID: …` line from a loading screen works too. Local: nothing is fetched or sent. A Check before the engine has finished downloading says so instead of "same".

**Power-user URL parameters:** `?gogc=N` (garbage-collector headroom, for A/B-testing stutter on weak machines) and `?signal=` (use a different lobby server). One `?` per URL — chain the rest with `&`. The boot page also forwards `?p1=&p2=&p2ai=&stage=` to the engine's quick-match command line, but that path does not work in the browser build (Part V, 5.7) — use the menus.

## Performance

**Micro-stutter.** The build runs on one thread; garbage-collector pauses freeze it for ~35–40 ms. A brief music hiccup is the reliable tell that a GC pause just happened. Pause length scales with how much is loaded — heavy characters and crowded team modes make it worse; lighter characters play smoother, especially online. Shipped default: `GOGC=100` — frequent short pauses feel better at 60 fps than rare long ones.

Three renderer changes cut stutter significantly since v1.0:
- The engine renders at the 60 fps it is authored for, not the monitor's refresh rate (a 240 Hz display was rendering 4x the necessary frames for no visual gain).
- The per-sprite drawing path no longer allocates memory per frame (previously the main source of GC pressure, generating gigabytes of garbage per minute).
- All WebGL commands batch into a single JS crossing per frame instead of hundreds.

Under load, GC collections now happen roughly every 14 seconds instead of every ~5. High-refresh-rate monitors and weak laptops benefit most.

## Storage, privacy, and mods

- In-game settings (key bindings, options) persist in the browser's localStorage — per browser, per device. A major site update can occasionally reset them when shipped defaults change.
- Mods added through the **Mod Studio** page live in the browser's IndexedDB only — no account, no upload, nobody else sees them. Budget is roughly 5 GB; the Studio shows a live usage estimate. Mods are per-site (and per-port): a mod added on one address is invisible on another.
- **Replays are not available in the browser build** — they need a file-write path that doesn't exist here. Desktop-engine feature only.
- If the game hard-crashes: don't reload before reporting. The crash log lives only in memory and reload destroys it. A screenshot of whatever's on screen (especially the green NETPLAY bar, if online) is the most useful thing to capture.

## Quick answers

- **Removing built-in characters/stages:** in the Mod Studio page, shipped items have a Remove button (reversible — "Restore" brings them back). The last stage cannot be removed; a build always keeps at least one.
- **The build size in the running foot is the export that is picked** (exportsize.js, `GET /api/build-size?kind=web|lite|desktop[&public=1]`, 2026-11-23). Website: `vfslib.build()` with export.js's own options (the motif's screenpack only, the public roster for Public build) plus the engine .wasm - exact, the same files the pak is written from. Website with Lite build: an estimate ("about"), the last lite export's ratio in the same folder applied to today's website figure (unchanged content gives back the exact game.lite size), else a third. Desktop: an estimate, desktop.js's content (chars, stages, music, the chosen screenpack) plus the engine zip's files the export leaves in place (chars/ is emptied; a file the export writes over the zip's counts once). Never sum the Studio's own index for it: that holds every installed screenpack (707 MB against a 457 MB website). The cards keep `buildSizes` (a character is the same size in every export).
- **GIVER / RECEIVER tags and the colored ring in the Studio:** GIVER/RECEIVER mark adult-compatibility roles (Part IV). The ring around a portrait is download size only — green up to 25 MB, amber to 49, red at 50 and above. It does not predict online performance.
- **Escaping a broken screenpack:** the Studio is a separate page from the game. Open it and switch the theme back — the designed recovery path.
- **White screen before an arcade match:** not a freeze — an intro cutscene whose art is missing (Part VI). Press any button to skip it.

## Training mode power tools: Scene Viewer & Lock-On

Every build ships a Training-mode sandbox not found in stock MUGEN, rebuilt automatically from the roster on every export so it always reflects the current characters — the web build and, since 2026-09-13, the desktop export too (as files of its own, never edits to the engine's scripts: `external/mods/sceneviewer.lua` and `external/mods/training-team.lua`, which the stock engine autoloads, and `data/sceneviewer.zss`, the facing hook, listed in `save/config.ini` as `[Common] States1` beside the engine's own list. The team mod wraps the training item and `start.f_remapAI` so the dummy side can be Simul — eight characters in the room, not five — and zeroes every AI level the stock setup hands out; the pause menu re-applies the dummy's own level each round. Delete the two `.lua` files to remove the sandbox; the `.zss` is inert without the mod, and to drop it as well remove the `States1` line, since a listed file that is missing fails character loading). Load Training with the characters wanted — a 2v2 Simul in Training shows a full pair — then:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **`Tab`** — Scene Viewer | Hands the keyboard to the next character on screen; cycles through everyone in the match (up to four). Others stand idle — no AI fights back — so one body can be driven while the rest are posed. |
| **`Caps Lock`** — Lock-On | Locks the controlled character to face a chosen opponent; press again to cycle targets. Facing holds — it will not auto-turn away mid-move, which is what lines up a pair scene. |
| **`Shift`+`Tab`** | Turns both off, returns to normal Training. |

An on-screen overlay shows who is currently being controlled. When that character is a **giver** (Part IV), the overlay is meant to also list its **scene commands** — the hold-direction position switches — pulled directly from the character's own files. **In play this is not reliable:** the owner has seen the list for one giver only (DongHwan); others show none. Do not point anyone at it (the band's tips do not) until it is looked into.

`Shift`+`Tab` rather than `Ctrl`+`Tab`, because browsers reserve `Ctrl`+`Tab` for switching browser tabs.

**`Shift`+`Tab` puts back the controls the fight had, not "every slot on its own number".** The first `Tab` saves every slot's input (`getRemapInput`); `Tab` gives the focused character the leader's saved input, swapped with the slot that held it; `Shift`+`Tab` puts the saved inputs back. On the modern-input engine the fight's mapping is not the identity: the leader can be on another input (side select), a slot nobody plays has none (0), and in an add004 tag build team-play.lua gives the Simul partners the leader's input. The identity reset took the leader's controls away and left a tagged-in partner standing still for the rest of the fight. A new fight's setup (`start.f_remapAI`) ends a viewer left on, so a later `Shift`+`Tab` cannot put back an earlier fight's inputs. On an engine without `getRemapInput` it behaves as before (input 1, the identity). Test: `tools/test-sceneviewer-remap.js`.

# Part II — Online play

Read **the three iron rules** below first if nothing else in this part.

## Connecting: room codes

The host picks Network → Host, optionally types a password, and gets a short code like `spicy-tiger-42`. The guest picks Join, types the code (and password). That's it.

- Rooms hold exactly two players. A third joiner is refused ("room full"). There is no spectating.
- Codes expire ~30 minutes after creation — "no room with that code" usually means asking the host for a fresh one (or checking spelling).
- The lobby service behind the codes only ferries a few kilobytes of connection setup, then gets out of the way. It never sees match traffic, and rooms are ephemeral — nothing is stored anywhere.
- If the lobby is unreachable, the panel falls back automatically to manual connect: the host copies an "offer" code, the guest pastes it and sends back an "answer" code over any chat app. A "Manual connect instead" button is also available. The manual path needs no infrastructure at all.
- The manual code is long because it is the entire connection description — every network route to reach the peer, plus an encryption fingerprint — not a password. A short code cannot carry that; that is exactly what the lobby exists to carry instead.
- First manual paste may trigger a clipboard permission prompt; if blocked, click the box and `Ctrl+V`.

## The three iron rules

Lockstep netplay desyncs if the two games differ at all. So:

1. **Same build.** The Build ID and the Engine code on both boot screens must match. The game also checks a content fingerprint on connect and refuses with *"Game contents differ between players!"*. A refresh does not fix that: anything added or changed in the Studio lives in the browser and survives a refresh. Compare Build IDs — the boot page's *Compare with a friend* box says which rule broke and which half of the build moved — then make them match: on a site with the Studio page, one player presses **Send my build** and the other **Import a build** (§3.1); or make identical changes on both sides; or use **Reset** on the boot page's Browser data line to return to the shipped build.
2. **Same netcode.** Rollback vs Delay is checked on connect; a mismatch is refused with a message. Rollback is the default; change it only if both players change it.
3. **Same theme.** Enforced automatically as part of the Build ID check (see Build ID, above). The select screen's grid comes from the theme, and netplay syncs *inputs*, not character picks — different grids mean the cursors land on different characters. Match themes before playing.

## What to expect

- **Modes online:** Versus 2P, Arcade co-op, Survival co-op — strictly two players. Team modes (Simul/Turns/Tag) are deliberately absent online: extra characters inflate memory and wreck netcode on a single thread.
- **The whole build sits in the tab's memory.** The play page downloads the pak into memory and keeps it there: the tab needs about 0.3 GB plus the build's size, and the engine's startup adds a few hundred MB on top for a moment. Read the pak with `readPak` (`vfs.js`): when the server states Content-Length and sends no Content-Encoding, the buffer is made once at that size and each chunk is written into it. Otherwise it keeps the chunk path (chunks, then one copy), which briefly holds the pak twice; the duplicate can linger until a GC. Measured on a 542 MB pak, as the renderer process's true peak commit: download alone 1,134 MB with the chunk path vs 699 MB with the buffer; the whole boot 1,407 vs 1,261 MB. A 36 MB pak (old loader) peaks at 0.46 GB for the tab and 1.16 GB for all of Chrome. The engine, its drawing and its garbage collector share one thread; a 2D match frame took about 1.3 ms of the 16.7 ms on a fast desktop CPU, so single-core speed matters more than core count.
- **Big characters load slower, not worse.** The Studio's ring (green ≤ 25 MB, amber ≤ 49, red 50+) is download size. Online, both players wait for whoever loads slower; garbage-collector pause length still scales with how much sprite data is loaded, so lighter rosters stutter less on weak machines.
- **Bandwidth is tiny:** ~4 bytes per frame each way, roughly 1–2 MB/hour. Direct peer-to-peer costs nothing; only the relay fallback (needed behind the strictest home routers) touches a relay quota.
- **Ping runs a bit higher than native netplay clients.** Inherent to the platform — the browser's network stack adds layers, and game + network + GC share one thread. Not fixable with settings.
- **When everything matches:** full matches, no desyncs, identical results both sides, slight adaptive delay on the guest.

## Patience rules (read before rage-quitting)

- **Hosts: wait is unbounded by design.** A friend cold-downloading the game can take minutes before they can even join. Leave the room open.
- **Both players stay on the connecting screen** through the whole process. Abandoning it mid-negotiation can strand the other side.
- *"Connection unstable — waiting for it to recover"* is not death: brief drops are normal and get ~12 seconds to self-heal. Only retry after it actually fails.
- **Some pairings can't connect directly** (strict/symmetric routers on both ends). A VPN or a phone hotspot on one side usually gets through.

## The green NETPLAY bar

During online play a diagnostics bar docks under the game: ping, bytes sent/received, the connection path, and a running event log. **The rollback ping is a game round trip, not a network one** (2.4.1): GGPO's quality report is answered from inside the other engine's frame loop, so a ~1 s freeze of EITHER page reads as a ~900 ms ping on a perfect network. GGPO keeps only the last reply's time and the engine shows it once a second, so a freeze that spans two reports can show no spike at all. It keeps updating even if the game freezes — a screenshot of this bar is the single most useful thing to attach to a connection bug report.

| Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recv` climbing, `engine-read` stuck | the engine is wedged |
| both counters stuck after connect | the other side silently left |
| `recv 0B` | never connected at all |
| send-buffer growing | data isn't leaving the local machine |
| path `relay->relay` | on the TURN relay (works, costs quota) |
| path `host->host` / `srflx->srflx` | direct connection (ideal) |
| `[ping 40ms net 35 peak 900]` | game ping, then the network-only round trip in ms (WebRTC getStats; missing on some browsers and paths; the browser refreshes it only every few seconds, so a short path stall may not show in it), then the highest ping of the last 5 s when it is higher than now |
| `ping 900 ms, network 38 ms: we ran steady -> their game paused or the path stalled` | a spike while this page's frames ran on time: the other player's game stopped for that long (hidden window, a slow PC) or the connection stalled |
| `...: our game paused 900 ms (window hidden) -> this side` / `(frame gap)` | this page stopped within the last 2.5 s for at least half the spike, so that explains it (a shorter pause does not take the blame) |
| `frame gap 420 ms on this side` / `window hidden 0.9 s` | this page's game paused that long (a game pauses while its window is hidden); one gap of about 0.3 s as a match loads is normal |
| (rule) | **Read BOTH players' bars.** The side that stalled always logs its own frame gap or hidden window; the other side shows a spike only sometimes (in a headless test, 3 of 15 one-second freezes), because GGPO keeps only the last reply's round trip. Verdict lines repeat at most once per kind every 15 s, so a steady high-ping pairing cannot push the log off the bar. |

---

# Part III — The modder's guide

## 3.1 Mugen Studio

Mugen Studio is the desktop program (`MugenStudio.exe`): it builds a MUGEN build from characters, stages, music and a screenpack kept on disk, and exports it. Web builds carry a much smaller in-page Studio, studio-lite, which keeps what a player adds in their own browser; entries marked *browser Studio* are about that one, and *desktop Studio* means Mugen Studio. Drop zones:

- **Characters** — a folder, `.zip`, `.rar` or `.7z` exactly as downloaded (archives are unpacked for you; no tools needed: the desktop Studio through Windows' tar.exe, the browser Studio through libarchive.js, below). A package that ships its own stage (a second `.def` with `[BGdef]`/`[StageInfo]`, shallowest folder only) gets that stage added and set as the character's arcade stage; audio inside a character package goes to the music library unassigned, because it is usually storyboard music.
- **Stages** — a folder or archive (`.zip`, `.rar`, `.7z`) with the stage's `.def` and sprites.
- **Music** — `.ogg` or `.mp3`; assign tracks to stages via each stage's dropdown.
- **Theme** — a screenpack folder or archive (`.zip`, `.rar`, `.7z`) containing a `system.def`.

**.rar and .7z in the browser Studio** (studio-lite, 2026-10-29: the owner's "make .rar files auto extract as well, just as the Mugen Studio does"). A page cannot run tar.exe, so it runs libarchive itself: **libarchive.js 2.0.2** (MIT) from npm, kept byte for byte in `public/ikemen/vendor/libarchive/2.0.2/` (`libarchive.js`, `worker-bundle.js`, `libarchive.wasm`: libarchive 3.7.2 with zlib, bzip2, liblzma and OpenSSL's libcrypto, bundling Comlink) with a license text for each part and `VENDOR.json` (the npm tarball's size and sha256, each file's size and sha256, how the .wasm was built, the parts with their versions and licenses). **It loads only when needed:** imported the first time a `.rar` or `.7z` is dropped, one worker per archive; the page's first load and a `.zip` fetch nothing of it (a `.zip` keeps the page's own `unzip()`). The first archive fetches about 1.07 MB (the module 8 KB, the worker 62 KB, the .wasm 1.0 MB). **What the bytes are decides the path, not the name:** a PK zip named `.rar` goes to `unzip()`, a `.7z` or RAR named `.zip` to libarchive, as on the desktop. The Characters, Stages and Theme boxes take all three, with the zip path's root-folder stripping and messages (`ARCHIVE_RE`, `unpackArchive`). **Names are one character per stored byte, as `unzip()` keeps them:** RAR 5, 7z and Unicode RAR 4 names as their UTF-8 bytes (what a `.zip` with the UTF-8 flag stores, so one pack gives the same paths in all three); an old RAR 4 name without the Unicode flag raw from the archive's own header (libarchive.js decodes it as UTF-8 and garbles a Shift-JIS name). **libarchive.js stops listing at a header it cannot read and never checks a CRC** (it reads each file's exact size; libarchive checks the CRC one read later): a RAR 5 cut at 20,000 bytes came back as 4 of its 13 files and a RAR 4 with damaged data whole, both with no error. So the page walks a `.rar`'s block headers itself (`rarHeaders`, RAR 4 and RAR 5) and refuses it unless every file comes back with its header's size and CRC-32; the walk is trusted only when it lines up with libarchive's list (the same count, every plain-ASCII RAR 4 name equal). A damaged, cut-short, password-protected or non-archive file is refused in words that name it (after modlib's `untarTrouble`), and nothing is added. The page reads the worker's flat list (`reader.client.extractFiles()`, an internal of the pinned 2.0.2: the public call folds it into folders and loses order and repeated names), so a version bump re-runs the test. Not wired, because none of them takes a `.zip`: the music box, the "choose a folder…" pickers, Import a build. **A library a page loads by itself ships as a whole `vendor/<name>/<version>/` folder:** export.js copies every one `index.html` or `studio-lite.html` names (a dynamic import has no `<script src>`; a missing folder throws), `tools/export-selfcheck.js` refuses a build without the folder or without a file or license its VENDOR.json lists, and `scripts/make-notices.js` names every part from VENDOR.json in the web and portable notices (appended, so the earlier section numbers stay). Size: 13 files, 1,116,611 bytes (about 531 KB zipped). Not tested: a password `.7z` (nothing on the machine writes one; its message matches libarchive's crypto wording). Tests: `tools/test-lite-archives.js` (51; `MUGEN_TEST_RAR` adds a real RAR 4 against tar.exe's unpacking), `tools/test-licenses.js`.

Per character, the Studio provides:

- **Download-size ring** around the portrait — green up to 25 MB, amber to 49, red at 50 and above. Size only; it does not predict online performance.
- **GIVER/RECEIVER badges** — adult-compatibility roles, detected from the files (Part IV explains the model).
- **Size dropdown (0.75×–1.25×)** — writes the character's `[Size]` scale so sprites and hitboxes scale together (stays fair), and never compounds: 1× always restores the exact original.
- **"Fix palette slots"** — re-keys the body palette so SFF v2 conversions with palettes mis-keyed as group 0 become selectable again (§4.9). Two refusals: when another palette already holds the `(1,1)` key the card says *preview only: color slots start one early* and offers no button, because re-keying would break the character in a match; and when the character's pair-scene art shares the body palette the browser Studio asks for a second click (the scenes will follow the color pick, §4.5) while the desktop Studio refuses outright.
- **"Add lifebar portrait"** — some screenpacks draw the in-match face from sprite `9000,20`, which standard characters don't ship; this adds one as a zero-copy link to the character's existing portrait.
- **Name collisions are handled** — adding a character whose folder name matches an existing one mounts it as `name_2`, never silently overwriting. A song is the same: a track whose file name the library already holds with different bytes lands as `<stem>_2`, `_3`, …, and the add answers with the name it wrote, so a stage that brings a song names its own file; the same bytes under the same name are shared, not copied again. A second song of the same name used to replace the first for every stage and screen that played it (`modlib.addMusic`, 2026-10-12).
- **Shipped roster is removable** — built-in characters/stages show Remove (reversible). At least one stage always remains.
- **Select, then delete several at once** (desktop Studio, **Select** on the Characters, Stages and Music bars) — while Select is on, a click ticks an item instead of opening it and shift-click ticks everything between the last tick and this one, in the order on screen; the roster grid and the A–Z list tick the same characters. The strip under the bar shows the count (and how many ticks the filter is hiding), **All shown**, **None**, and **Delete N**, which arms on its first click (its tooltip names what will go) and deletes on the second. Every item goes through the same remover as a single delete, so a batch leaves exactly what one-by-one deletes would. An item the single delete refuses is refused here too and stays ticked with its reason: the last stage, and the track set as the stage fallback. Esc or **Done** leaves Select mode. Test: `tools/test-remove-many.js`.
- **Delete through the Studio, never in the Content folder.** A bundle's `roster.json` is the build: `select.def` is not stored anywhere, it is generated from `roster.json` at every build. So a character folder, stage or track deleted by hand leaves the roster naming it — a select slot pointing at a folder that is not there, characters pointing at a stage that is gone, stages and menu screens naming a missing song. The Studio's delete removes those references along with the files (from the bundle only, never from your original copies). **`roster.json` is written whole, then renamed** (vfslib `writeRoster`): the new text goes to `roster.json.tmp` and one rename puts it in place, tried again up to five times 100 ms apart when Windows refuses it (EPERM, EBUSY, EACCES: a scanner or a sync client holding the file), never falling back to a write in place. Closing the window kills the server at once, and a kill in the middle of an in-place write left half a roster, the bundle's whole state; now a reader sees the old roster or the new one. A `roster.json.tmp` left by a kill is harmless: the next save replaces it.
- **Pair bench** (desktop Studio, the ♥ button on the roster bar; it appears only when the roster holds a detected giver or receiver) — pick a giver and a receiver and see, by registry family, every H number the giver asks a victim for, on two layers. G = guarded (`SelfAnimExist`): green when the receiver ships her own tailored action there with its frames present in her sprite file, gray when she does not (the giver falls back). U = unguarded (`ChangeAnim2`): the giver's own action driven on the receiver's *sprites*, so the check is whether her `.sff` holds every `(group,index)` that action draws — green renders in her own art under the giver's choreography, amber partly, red vanishes at that pose. A receiver can render a scene while shipping none of the giver's action numbers, as long as she carries the sprite groups his fallbacks draw with (§4.1); the bench lists that, not a verdict. Dashed = a number the receiver also plays herself (§4.5). Counts and numbers only, never a percentage (§4.3). **Launch this pair** starts the desktop export's engine straight into the fight — giver as P1, receiver as P2 with AI off, one round, no clock — through the engine's own command line, which works on desktop and not in the browser build (Part V, 5.7). Both characters must be in the desktop export. **Click a chip** for the sprites, one **scene** at a time: a number sits in one custom state or a dozen, each under its own giver pose, so the panel picks the scene (a select when there are several, labeled with the giver state and the variable assignment) and both panes follow it. Left: the giver's own animations in the state he holds while she is in that custom state, read the way the engine runs it (§4.10) — through the handoff after a grab, a computed TargetState solved for its variables, each animation labeled with how it is chosen (certain, `var(40)=4`, at tick 76, random, if she has 19234, then…), and flags when a helper draws him, he is invisible, or he idles. Right: what she shows — her tailored action, the giver's action drawn with *her* sprite file for an unguarded number, and every fallback of that scene, each with its verdict; a mirror toggle turns her to face left, mirrored about her axis with her boxes, and her GIF follows. The two are not positioned as the engine binds them, they are the two halves side by side; an action with no frame in her file says so instead of drawing nothing. Both panes are the shared player, so collision boxes and the GIF button work in them as in the Animation panel: a GIF of a cross-sprite entry is written with her sprite file and her palette pick, named `giver-action-on-receiver.gif`. Chips: **G** guarded, **A** assumed (played unchecked), **U** unguarded fallback (§4.10). What the file cannot settle is named in the pane, never guessed.
- **All slots** (the ▦ button on the Palettes panel) — every selectable palette in one window: the stance in each color, and under it a receiver's pair art in that color wherever the art follows the body palette, so the §4.5 corruption is one glance instead of twelve clicks. Pair art on its own palette is stated once and not repeated. Each cell is headed by the palette's name, with its number in the tooltip, as on the Palettes rows. A separate window on purpose (`palgrid.html`): nothing of it is on the Studio page, only the cells on screen load their images, and closing the window clears everything — it holds no timer and no storage. Preview only. **The sprites follow the window**: each is drawn at a WHOLE multiple of its own size (pixel art between multiples is mush), the larger of two answers — the biggest multiple at which every slot is on screen at once, and one more multiple for every 520×390 of window whatever the slot count (a character with forty slots cannot fit at any size, and drawing them tiny is the wrong answer; it scrolls) — never so large that one sprite is wider than the window, up to 8×. The header's **− / +** (and the keys, with **0** for auto) override it for as long as the window is open. The sizes come from the animation's frame data, so the layout is right before an image has loaded.
- **Sounds** (desktop Studio, the ♪ button on the roster bar) — two tabs. **Sounds**, the default: every sound the character's own `.snd` holds, in file order, with its length, format (rate, mono/stereo, bits), how many moves name it by literal and where the first one is, and a ▶ that plays it at the slider's volume, 50% by default (the game plays a character's own `PlaySnd` at 39% in this build and in full on the stock desktop engine, §4.7). Each `.snd` entry is a complete WAV, so the browser plays it as the file holds it: the list costs one header walk, a sound is fetched only when pressed and never stored (the route says `no-store`; a replay re-reads the local file in milliseconds), and ⤓ saves the same bytes as `character-group-index.wav`. Nothing is converted or decoded on the server: a `.snd` is a table of contents over untouched WAV files, and the state files are read only to say which moves name which sound. A sound no move names by literal is marked so; it may still be reached by a computed call. **Audit**, the second tab — one character or the whole roster: every own-file `PlaySnd`, and every S-prefixed `hitsound`/`guardsound`, whose `group,index` the `.snd` does not hold, with the file and line of each call; the roster sweep sorts by missing sounds, then by loud lines, and a row opens the character's detail. Loud `volume`/`volumescale` literals are listed per file and kind with the count of unprefixed calls. Same numbers as `tools/sound-audit.js`.
- **Send my build / Import a build** (the browser Studio, beside *Your build:* in the online box) — one `.wmbuild` file holding every file added in this browser plus the Studio's own lists and picks: roster order, hidden built-ins, theme, rules, menu music. The other player opens the Studio on the same site, presses Import and picks the file; the import **replaces** everything they added (a second click confirms) and keeps their key bindings, netcode and online name, and both loading screens then print the same Build ID. Replace, never merge: the ID covers the whole overlay, so one extra local file would still differ. Same site version required: the shipped half of the ID is the upload's own file list, so a bundle from another upload transfers the content but cannot match, and the import card says so before anything is touched. A `.wmbuild` dropped on a drop zone is handed to Import rather than read as a character. A bundle that carries the engine's own `save/` files (options and key bindings, patched per player at boot) is refused before anything is written, one import runs at a time, and the second click of the confirmation counts only after a moment, so a double-click cannot replace a build. Nothing is uploaded; there is no server for it.
- **Online** (desktop Studio, Settings → Online) — the self-hosting fields in one place: the lobby relay address, the TURN app and key (`local-config.json`), and the leaderboard address plus the online-name switch (`roster.json`), each with what it is for, numbered steps for getting the value (the TURN steps name Metered's own buttons), a visible hint under each field with an example, and a **Test** per group that has the Studio's server dial the endpoint the way a player's game would, typed or saved. Each edit is written as it is made, whole file renamed into place; a blank removes the key, and nothing on the tab can delete the file. The export guard is unchanged: these values never reach a public export. Once a leaderboard address is set, a **Leaderboard page** choice appears under it - **Plain standings** (the default: a table of the top 100) or the **Score Ranking board** (the arcade attract loop of the top 8) - with a live preview, a Sample data tick for an empty board, and an own-window button; the Website export then writes the chosen page beside the game as `leaderboard.html`, its `window.RANKING` block filled with the leaderboard address and the site's title and credit (`public/ranking/`, a public build gets none). With the board chosen, its **look** has five rows. **Board format**: Classic board (the climbing board), Select screen, Podium, Hi-score table or Broadcast. **Header style**: how the title (SCORE RANKING, RANK 1) and the logo card's line are drawn, Banner (the default), Ruled, Flat glow or Underline bar, four flat looks that suit any font (the 3D gradient, outline and drop shadow they replaced suited only the font it was drawn for). **Fonts**, one row per role (title, names, numbers, text): Default, the system font each part has always had, or one of 16 arcade fonts that ship in `public/ranking/leaderboard-fonts/`. **Colors**: a preset (Classic, the board's own, or one of the Studio's looks: Energy, WB, DJ-AR, SHiZUKA, High contrast, each its night printing) and **Custom colors**, six swatches (background, glow, accent, names, ratings, places) over it, with Reset; picking a preset starts over from its colors. It is all one value, `roster.leaderboardLook` (`leaderboardlook.js`: `{ header, format, fonts, colors: { preset, ...hand-set } }`, only what differs from the default, no key at all for the default; unknown values fall back), saved whole on each change; the export writes it into the board's `RANKING` and copies the fonts it names, and only those, beside the page in `leaderboard-fonts/`; the preview passes it as `?look=`. The page applies it in its head script, before it paints: `data-header` and `data-format` on `<html>` (markup: banner, classic), the colors as custom properties (every other color on the page is mixed from them, so a preset recolors everything), an `@font-face` per chosen font. Its tables are leaderboardlook.js's (`tools/test-ranking-pages.js` compares them). The classic board scales a 480-unit stage over a full-window backdrop and widens with the window, so no frame shape shows bars; each other format has a wide and a tall (stacked) composition of fixed proportions in `--u` units (`BOXES`), and `fitFlow()` picks the one that shows bigger in the window and scales it to fit whole, so an in-between window (a 930x1160 pop-out, say) never gets a layout stretched out of proportion. A name wider than its place scrolls to its end and back instead of being cut off (`scrollIfLong`; with reduced motion it keeps its ellipsis). It is measured in the font it shows: the board asks for each chosen font before it starts (`chosenFonts`, 3 s at most), since `document.fonts.ready` resolves before a face no text has used yet even begins to load, and measures again when a face still loading then lands. A podium block grows to hold its words rather than squeeze the name; broadcast's champion name ends before the pose (with no art, at the card's edge), shrinking to fit there, to half its size, before it scrolls; select's nameplate scrolls to its end before the cursor moves on. The classic stage checks its names again whenever its width changes (a resized window), and the names pass never hands `scrollIfLong` to `forEach` bare (its index arrived as a 0 s time limit). A hi-score table wider than its composition (a wide face on a phone) is drawn smaller to fit. The preview's frame is resizable: **Preview size** (Fit the page width, the default 340 tall; 16:9 window; 4:3 window; Square; Phone) or a drag of its corner (Your own size), kept across the tab's redraws, so any shape can be checked inside the Studio, not only in the pop-out. Sample data fights with the bundle's own characters when it has art. A bundle switched to Plain standings keeps its board look for when the board comes back. **Board text** (a fold under the look rows; **Page text** with Plain standings) makes each of the page's phrases the host's own (`look.text`, leaderboardlook.js `TEXT_KEYS`: blank is the default, at most 80 characters, `<` and `>` removed, `*stars*` mark words in the accent color; the pages build them with the DOM, never as markup). Two of its lines are the logo card's big and small lines (`logoMain`, `logoSub`, whose default is `''`): left blank they are the site's credit (else title) and its title letter-spaced, as before, and the boxes show those words as their placeholders; set, they replace them on the board only, shown as typed. The site title itself (roster `siteTitle`, set to the bundle's name when the bundle is made, and shown by the exported game too) still has no field in the Studio: his call (2026-10-28) was board only, site-wide only if that proves not enough. **Rank icons** gives each rank of the server's rules, and UNRANKED, a shield in two colors with 0-7 pips or a picture of the host's own (`look.ranks`; PNG, WebP or SVG of 256 KB at most, `POST /api/leaderboard-rank-image`, kept in the bundle's `leaderboard-ranks/` folder, layout.js `LEADERBOARD_RANKS`, served to the preview at `/ranking/leaderboard-ranks/`, an SVG under a sandboxing CSP, and copied beside the exported board). An SVG is refused when it could run or fetch anything: a script or foreignObject behind any prefix, an event handler, a link out, a namespace other than SVG's and XLink's (so an Inkscape save with its editor namespaces must be saved again as a plain SVG, or as a PNG). A rank name the board has no built-in colors for takes them from its place in the server's ranks list. The plain standings page takes the look's text and each rank's top color. **Background picture** (both pages, under the look rows with the board, above Page text with the standings) puts one picture, animated GIF or WebP, or short video behind the whole page (`look.background`: `{ file, fit, dim }`; PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF up to 10 MB, MP4 or WebM up to 20 MB, each checked by its type and opening bytes; `POST /api/leaderboard-background` with the file's own bytes as the body, kept in the bundle's `leaderboard-bg/` as `bg-<12 hex of its sha256>.<kind>`, layout.js `LEADERBOARD_BG`, served to the preview at `/ranking/leaderboard-bg/` with byte ranges, copied beside the exported page; the pages load only a name of that shape from that folder). **Fill the page** (cover, the default), **Show all of it** (contain) or **Tile it**, and **N% darker** (0-90, default 40), which lays the page's own background color over it. A video plays muted, looping and inline, and holds its first frame for reduced motion. Remove goes back to the page's own backdrop and leaves the file in the folder. The templates carry no server, name or font file of their own (`tools/test-ranking-pages.js`); the board draws character art from a `leaderboard-art/` folder beside it (`manifest.json` + PNGs, made by `tools/extract-charart.js`). **The art belongs to the bundle it is made from** (`layout.LEADERBOARD_ART`, the one place that knows): `Content/<bundle>/leaderboard-art/`, except the checkout's Main, whose folder is the private site's beside the program folder. Not the program folder (another bundle has other characters) and not the export folder (a Website export empties it, so the art would start from nothing every time). **A leaderboard switches the art on**: a non-public Website export of any bundle with a leaderboard address refreshes that bundle's folder, in the author's tree and in a shareable copy alike (`modlib.canBoardArt`: the extractor and its encoder `tools/gif.js` present, and an address), incrementally - files added and overwritten, the manifest rebuilt from the roster, nothing deleted. **Never another bundle's folder**: `export.makeBoardArt` takes no destination, and the extractor refuses the checkout Main's folder or any other bundle's (`layout.isOtherBundleArt`) and an in-process call that names none, because it rebuilds the manifest from the ACTIVE roster - the bundle test's one-character Test Run once left the site's board knowing only KFM. A board export copies what the new manifest names beside `leaderboard.html` (`copyBoardArt`); the plain standings draw none; a public export makes none. The Studio serves the active bundle's folder at `/ranking/leaderboard-art/` (PNG and JSON only, nothing outside it), so the preview shows it, and with the board chosen a **Character art** row says how many characters it has and when it was made, with a button that makes it now (`POST /api/leaderboard-art`, the export's own step). Only a copy with no extractor (the legacy kit) draws the board without art, and only there does the Studio say so (`/api/local-config`: `boardArtTool` = this copy can make it, `boardArt` = the folder has a manifest, `boardArtChars`, `boardArtMade`). The animation panel's **Leaderboard win pose** box follows the same rule, so a bundle with no leaderboard offers none; it sits in the GIF options, so a `--no-gif` copy offers none either and its art uses the win pose the engine plays. The group itself appears wherever `public/ikemen/identity.js` exists - the author's tree and a shareable copy, not the legacy kit. An **Open the setup guide** button opens `docs/RANKED-SETUP.md` (served at `/api/setup-guide`, drawn by `guide.html`), which a portable copy carries beside the program. **What a field wants is on the page, never only in a tooltip**, and a field takes what people paste: the TURN app name accepts `yourname`, `yourname.metered.live` or the full `https://` address and stores `yourname`. **Your own servers (Cloudflare)** is the tab's first group wherever the copy carries `hostkit/`: one pasted token and **Set up my servers** put the host kit on the host's own free Cloudflare account, then fill this install's relay address and the active bundle's leaderboard address and Online menu, asking first before replacing anything already filled in; the manual groups stay for other providers (§5.14). **Players**, under Leaderboard, lists that leaderboard's names and records and changes them - a new recovery code, a released name, a row removed or corrected, a reset with a copy saved first - through the server's admin key, which the page never holds (§5.15).
- **Lobby look** (Settings → Online, 2026-11-14) — the winner-stays lobby's look on the web game page, chosen by the site's host; players cannot change it. Its own group under **Lobby relay**: **Colors** (a preset: Classic, the sidebar's own, or Energy, WB, DJ-AR, SHiZUKA, High contrast, each a Studio look's night printing) and **Custom colors**, eight swatches over it with Reset (background, panels, text, quiet text, accent, text on the accent, borders, chat and boxes); **Header style**, the sidebar's head band, flat looks only (Solid band, the default; Panel band; Underline); **Heading font** and **Text font** from the leaderboard's 16 fonts (`public/ranking/leaderboard-fonts/`, with `FONTS.txt`) or Monospace, the lobby's own; **Page picture**, one PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF (animated ones play) up to 10 MB or MP4/WebM up to 20 MB behind the page, and **Panel picture**, the same kinds behind the lobby panel itself (like a speedrun timer's background; the panel's body and chat show it, buttons, boxes and the code stay solid, text gets a hard 1 px shadow), each with Fill (keep ratio) / Fit (keep ratio) / Stretch / Tile it / Actual size and **N% darker** (0-90, default 60); kept as roster.lobbyLook.background and .panelBg. **Panel theme**: Flat (as always) or a whole restyle with the same words: **Versus** (a fighting game’s VS card: the two players on slanted plates with a VS between them, the rest as tiles under a striped band), **Terminal** (a CRT console: scan lines, bracketed buttons, dotted leaders; a panel picture shows faintly through, whatever its darkness) or **Booklet** (a 2000s fighting-game instruction booklet page: speed-cut chapter band over halftone dots, outlined chapter numbers 01-03, the match in a tip box, a numbered roster with the players on slanted plates under outlined P1/P2, printed buttons that press in, the chat as a ruled notes page); a theme draws its own header, so Header style applies to Flat. Themes hang off webrtc.js hooks (lb-now / lb-next / lb-streak / lb-pass on the match lines, data-st and data-p on member rows). **See-through**: Lines and borders, Panel fill and Chat and boxes, each 0-100 % (0 = solid); buttons and tags stay solid (roster.lobbyLook.style, .see). The Lobby look and the leaderboard board’s look are edited in TABS (lobby: Colors, Panel, Fonts, Pictures; board: Layout, Colors, Fonts, Pictures, Text, Ranks; plain standings: Pictures, Text) with the live preview pinned beside them (stacked, preview first, under 1100 px); the tab shown is kept across saves. There is no corner, shadow or transparency choice at all: everything the page can write is square and solid (the owner's rule). Below them a live **preview**, the game's own sidebar beside a stand-in game (`public/ikemen/lobby-preview.html`, Studio-only, never exported; `?look=`; it sets `IKEMEN_LOBBY_PREVIEW`, which makes webrtc.js offer `ikemenLobbyPreview(state)` and open no socket), Open in its own window, and Back to the default look. One value, `roster.lobbyLook` (`lobbylook.js`: `{ colors: { preset, ...hand-set }, fonts: { head, body }, header, background: { file, fit, dim } }`, only what differs, no key for the default; one of the six online keys `bundles.js` carries between bundles, and `/api/roster` takes it from the disk like gameOnly), saved whole through `/api/local-config`; the background goes in first through `POST /api/lobby-background` (the board background's kinds, caps and byte checks), kept in the bundle's `lobby-bg/` (layout.js `LOBBY_BG`; for the checkout's Main beside the program folder) as `bg-<12 hex of its sha256>.<kind>`, served at `/ikemen/lobby-bg/` (that name shape only, really in the folder; refused in a read-only bundle). **The page** reads it from `IKEMEN_BRAND.lobbyLook` (`public/ikemen/lobby-look.js`, which holds the presets for the Studio too): the Website export writes it there only for a bundle that has one and only on a non-public build (a public build has no lobby server), with `fontDir: 'leaderboard-fonts/'` and `bgDir: 'lobby-bg/'`, copies the chosen fonts with their note and the background beside the page, and leaves out (and says so) a background that is missing, over its cap, not what its name says or not named by its own hash; the Studio's server adds it after the brand block of the `index.html` it serves, so **Test in Browser** shows it (a bundle without one gets the file's own bytes). **Tokens**: the sidebar (webrtc.js `LOBBY_CSS`) draws every color and font from `--lob-bg`, `--lob-panel`, `--lob-text`, `--lob-dim`, `--lob-accent`, `--lob-accent-text`, `--lob-border`, `--lob-chat-bg`, `--lob-font`, `--lob-head-font`, plus six it never asks anyone for (`--lob-rule`, `--lob-rule-soft`, `--lob-faint`, `--lob-off-border`, `--lob-off-text`, `--lob-warn`), all defaulting to the step 2 look at `:where(:root)` (zero weight, so the look's own `:root` rule always wins); a look with colors sets all eight and mixes the six from them, a look without keeps the literals, so no look is exactly the old sidebar (`tools/test-lobby-look.js` compares all 62 elements' computed styles with e2bbf69's). New lobby UI uses these tokens and nothing else. **In a lobby** (`html.inlobby`, set while the sidebar exists) the page around the game takes the look: its background, the info and hide buttons square and solid in its colors; the strip's own controls (Compare's box, Check, Copy mine, Rollback / Delay, 480p / 720p, Reset: styled inline, so these rules carry `!important`) square with 2px borders in its colors, the chosen netcode and picture size (`aria-pressed`) filled with the accent, Reset in the warning color; the canvas framed in the border color; the netplay line under the game square and solid in the chat colors; with a background picture (`html.lob-bg`) it fills the window behind the game under the look's background color at its darkness, and the sidebar's panel stays solid in front of it at every width (it let the picture through at first, which read badly over a busy picture and is a see-through resting fill: removed the same day). Outside a lobby the page is exactly as before, Game only included. **The folded tab** stays out of the way: invisible at rest (opacity 0, still in the Tab order), shown while the mouse is within 96 px of the right edge, while hovered or focused, and on a tap near the edge, and gone 2 s after the pointer leaves that strip; a tap on it while hidden only shows it; folding shows it once so it is seen going there. Tests: `tools/test-lobby-look.js` (the tables, the routes, four real exports, and the page in headless Chrome against e2bbf69's sidebar, with the strip's own rows built by index.html's scripts: in a lobby, in every look, the whole document with the strip open square and solid and its controls and netplay line in the look's colors; the tab's states; about 30 s).
- **The roster bar** (desktop Studio) keeps the build count on the left, then glyph buttons for the per-character tools — **+** add, **♥** pair bench (only when the roster holds a giver or receiver), **♪** sounds, **✓** audit; their names are in the tooltips — and on the right tile size, sort, reverse, and **≡ Filter** last. The sort has four orders: **Alphabetical** (the default), **File size** (largest first), **Last added** (newest first, by the character folder's creation time - not its modified time, which a repair moves) and **Build order** (the roster's own, the order the export writes); the reverse button turns any of them around, and both are remembered per browser (`ikemen-studio:char-sort`, `ikemen-studio:char-sort-dir`). Every control in it keeps its width and the column clips, so when the middle column is narrower than the bar it gives way in steps instead of losing its right end: the word *sort* goes (the box keeps the name *Sort*), the count shortens, **Filter** and **Select** become ≡ and ☑ (their names stay for screen readers), the sort box narrows, the count goes (the list's title carries the number) unless it is the way into **Other versions**, then on the narrowest windows the tile-size and reverse buttons (their choices stay) and a still narrower sort box. The bar's width at every step is measured once when its contents change, and the step for a width is then arithmetic: re-measuring on each resize cost several layouts per frame of a column drag. On the booklet page its keys print as the booklet's small buttons and the sort as a fill-in line.
- **The Characters columns are resizable** (desktop Studio). A handle in each gap sizes the roster list and the Properties panel; the middle takes the rest. Double-click a handle (or Enter on a focused one) for the window's default width; a focused handle moves 16px per arrow key, 64 with Shift, and Home/End make the pane its narrowest and widest (the handle's value is the pane's width, and its maximum is the width it can reach in this window). The handles sit between the columns in tab order, and pressing one closes the Filter dropdown like any other press. Limits: the list 160–360px, the panel 300–760px, and the middle never narrower than two portraits or than its bar at its most compact. **Past its narrowest the list folds to a strip** of its 24px row portraits (44px: the portrait, the row's edge mark and the frame's border, with no scrollbar). It is a detent, not a range: a drag past halfway between 160 and the strip folds it, a drag back past halfway opens it at 160, and one arrow key (or Home) crosses it, so the list is never a column of names cut to a letter. The names stay in each row for screen readers and as the portrait's tooltip; the title keeps only the count, which turns the accent color and names the filter in its tooltip when a filter narrows the roster (the filter box is hidden). The `/` key opens a folded list to the width it had before folding (`ikemen-studio:list-open-width`), then focuses the filter. A window that squeezes the list stops at 160: only the person folds it. In Select mode the check box sits on the portrait's corner. The widths are remembered per browser (`ikemen-studio:list-width`, `ikemen-studio:detail-width`); a width saved in a larger window gives way in a smaller one and comes back in the larger. When both saved widths do not fit, the column sized last keeps its width and the other gives way first, so what a drag leaves on screen is what every later fit gives back. Below 900px wide the list is hidden and the panel is fixed, so there are no handles. The widths are custom properties that every width rule reads with its own breakpoint value as the fallback, so an untouched roster keeps the breakpoints exactly; they are registered as **not inheriting** (`@property … inherits: false`), because an inherited property on the frame restyles every element inside it — every portrait, every list row, the action picker's hundreds of options — on each drag step (measured 5.9 ms a step against 2.7 ms, where a 238Hz frame is 4.2 ms). The handles are direct children of the frame, placed in the gaps by grid column: the list and the panel empty themselves on every render. The portraits follow the middle column on their own (the grid fits as many tiles as the width holds and stretches them to fill it); the tile-size button still chooses between more, smaller portraits and fewer, larger ones.
- **The Characters tab is the booklet's spread** (studio.html, `public/booklet-chars.css`; 2026-10-18). The tab's three boxed columns became one open spread printed on the stock: the **section band** (`#charBand`, "Characters キャラクター", with the build's character count, those on disk only, and their megabytes - a second version that shares another's files is not counted twice: `charBandMeta`); the left page holds the **index** (`#charList`: the same alphabetical list, each row a 20px face, the name, leader dots and the megabytes, with a **letter head** hanging in the margin on the first SHOWN row of each letter, so a filter never hides a head with its row: `charLetters`, `.lrow[data-lt]`), the **select grid** (`#charGrid`: each portrait on a plate, its caption the name and the **select slot** numeral, then the `.def` and the size; the picked one printed in reverse with the band's rule); both run the page's whole height (WB's hint box at its foot, `#charHint`, went in the owner's second review, 2026-10-18: the band's tips are a slip laid over the page, see *The band's tips*). The fold between the pages is the Properties handle (`#detailSizer`), drawn as a 2px rule at rest. The right page is the **character page** (`#charDetail`): its top line is the slot ("No.03 of 5 cells, select slot"), **Hide ›** and **Remove** (the delete corner, same two clicks; it read ✕ before); then the select portrait on a plate framed in the **download-size ring's** ink (green, amber, red; its tooltip the Studio's own `sizeNote`), drawn at a WHOLE multiple of its size up to the plate (`charPlate`), with **Portraits…** under it (a twin of the card's, `.cportraits.ro-edit`; the card's own is `.cardportraits`, hidden on the page) and an **Edited** flag on its corner when health, speed, size or a fighting stat differs from what shipped; the name as the page title (click to rename, as before); the profile (`charProfile`: File, Author from the library, Sprites SFF v1/v2, Size with the ring's swatch); Stage and Music as **fill-in lines**; the repair row; then Palettes, Animation, Versions and the H role under **side heads**. A page under 500px wide puts a 120x140 plate beside the name and the profile under both; 500px and over, a 240x280 plate down the left and palettes in two columns (container queries on `#charDetail`). **Two DOM moves a later change can trip on:** the page's head is `.dhead > .cplate + .cident`, and `selectChar` moves the adopted card's body (`.dbody`) INTO `.cident` after the unchanged `panel.append(detailHead(id), head, body, versionsSection(id), hRoleSection(id),` line (test-h-module reads it literally), and the slot and the delete corner into `.phead`; `layoutCharacters` and `selectChar` still find the card with `querySelector('.card.char')`. **A grid trap:** an item placed by row only is placed before the auto items, so (when the grid still had a hint row) with the hint hidden in a short window the page took the FIRST free column - it stays pinned to the last (`grid-column: -2 / -1`, row 1).
- **The select slot** is the cell the select screen gives the character, numbered the way the engine hands cells out and E-Select shows them (studio.html `charSlots`, a port of modlib `cellIndexes`; main.lua's `[Characters]` walk): a placeholder (dummyslot, skipslot, randomselect) is a cell; a slot group (consecutive entries with one slot id, `slot = { }`) is ONE cell and its members print that number and a letter in list order, **04a 04b** (the player swaps between them on the select screen); **`exclude = 1` takes no cell** (main.lua sets the line aside and adds the character after the last cell), so the next entry takes the cell and the character prints **off grid**. "Of" is the cells the entries take, printed **"of N cells"**. The number is printed on the tile (`.cap .slot`; "off grid" as `.slot.offgrid`), on the page's top line ("No.04b of 31 cells, slot group of 2" - the clause after the count is `.cslot .why`, dropped on a page under 440px, the tooltip keeps it) and in the running foot's **folio** (`folioForChar` -> `setFolio('04b', '31 cells')`; setFolio takes a slot LABEL as a number: digits plus an optional letter or `-N`, `FOLIO_SLOT = /^\d+([a-z]|-\d+)?$/`), which follows the picked character while this tab shows and clears on the other tabs (a MutationObserver on the panel's `hidden`, `wireCharBooklet`). The tile's and the page's tooltip (`slotTitle`) says which cell, what "of" counts, and every mate of a slot group. `charSlots().no(id)` stays the cell NUMBER; `label(id)` is what prints. The **Theme tab's grid preview** walks the same cells (`gridCells` skips an `exclude = 1` character and an excluded slot-group member, `SLOT_OFF_GRID`, as modlib's motifSelectInfo does), so its "N of M cells used" agrees with the Characters page, E-Select and the engine. `tools/test-char-slots.js` (59 checks) holds the walk and the grid preview against modlib `cellIndexes` on 305 rosters and the owner's shape, setFolio's labels and words, and the Moves… query and band.
- **Build order is the roster's order, never the DOM's** (`charOrderKey`, `sortCards`, `returnCard`). The character page borrows the open character's card from `#chars`; it gave the card back with an append, and the sort read the cards' DOM order, so every character opened since the last render sank to the end of Build order - with Build order saved the page opens on cell 1, and one re-sort put No.01 below the last cell (the owner's "there IS NO no. 1", 2026-10-18). Build order now comes from `state.roster.chars`: on-grid characters by roster index, off-grid ones after the last cell (where the engine adds them), on-disk ones after all in the library's order; a borrowed card goes back to its place.
- **The blank cells print in Build order** (`cellPlates`, `CELL_KINDS`, booklet-chars.css `.cellplate`): each placeholder is an empty numbered plate where it falls, in either direction - hatched hairlines, the number on a paper patch, "blank cell" / "skipped cell" / "random select" under it. It is not a character: not a `.ptile` (the filter, the facets, the keys, picks and the A-Z strip never see it), not pickable (`aria-disabled`), its tooltip names the cell and says placement is edited in E-Select or on the Theme tab's grid; hidden while a filter narrows the grid (`applyRosterFilter`); no plates in the other sorts, which keep their order and the same labels.
- **The A-Z strip** (`#charAZ`) stands in for the index wherever the index is not on the page: a window under 900px wide (the list is hidden there) or the list folded to its portraits. A letter jumps the grid to its first shown tile, scrolling the grid only; a letter with nobody under it prints unlit and cannot be pressed; `#` is added when a name starts with a digit or a sign. The picked character's letter is marked.
- **Advanced** (Options › Advanced settings) still decides whether Health / Speed / Size / Fighting stats show, but on the character page they print as a block UNDER Stage and Music (labels over fill-ins) instead of replacing them: the page always says what the character fights on and to.
- **Default widths:** the character page is the spread's wider page: the Properties column's default is 540px above 1320px wide and 420px from 1101 to 1320 (it was 372 / 340); 312px at 1100 and under, the list's widths and every handle limit (list 160-360, panel 300-760) are unchanged, and a width the person set is kept. Two numbers in the main `<style>` and two in `columnHandles`' `ladder()`.
- **A frame ends above the running foot.** On a frame tab `main:has(> .panel:not([hidden]) > :is(#charWrap, .pframe)) { padding-bottom: 14px }` outranks the chrome's `#main { padding-bottom: calc(var(--foot-h) + 14px) }`, so a frame measured to the window's bottom ran 34px under the fixed foot: `#charWrap` subtracts `--foot-h` in booklet-chars.css and every other `.pframe` in the chrome (`#main > .panel > .pframe`, above 700px wide; About's spread sets its own height).
- **The Stages and Music tabs are the booklet's stage-select page and sound test** (studio.html, `public/booklet-stages.css`; 2026-10-18, Phase B). Each tab is a section band (`#stageBand` "Stages ステージ", `#musicBand` "Music サウンドテスト"; the meta `#stageBandMeta` / `#musicBandMeta` prints the stages in the build and how many are narrower than the build / the tracks and their megabytes) over a spread inside the tab's `.pframe` (still the drop target, still sized by fitRoster): the left page is the list under a side-head line (`.pbar`: "Stage select" / "Sound test", + Add, Select), the right page (`aside.bkm-margin`) the margin notes, the page's whole height (the band's hint box pinned at their foot, `#stageHint` / `#musicHint`, went in the owner's second review, 2026-10-18).
  - **The master preview volume** (the owner, 2026-10-18: "some songs START extremely loud and fiddling for the small native player volume controls is far too inconvenient"; studio.html `masterVolume`, `masterPreviewVolume`, `previewButton`; `public/booklet-stages.css` `.pbar .mvol`). The sound test's top line ends with **Master**, a range 0-100% and the level (`#musicMasterRow` > `#musicMaster` + `#musicMasterN`). Every track preview takes it: `previewButton` writes `au.volume = masterVolume() / 100` on the new `<audio>` BEFORE `src` and `play()`, so a song's first bar already plays at it, and moving the slider changes the preview that is playing (`previewNow.audio.volume`). The player's own volume control still works under it until the slider moves again. Remembered per machine (localStorage `ikemen-studio:preview-volume`; blocked storage or a non-number reads as 100). **The first value is 100%, what a preview played at before** (the element's default 1.0). `previewButton` is the Studio's only music preview: the Stages page picks songs with selects and plays nothing, so "Music and Stages" is this one player (a future preview anywhere must set `masterVolume()` the same way). The Sounds dialog's slider (a character's own .snd, 50% default) is a different player and is untouched.
  - **A stage** is an entry under an inked rule (still `.card.stage[data-id=<file>]`): its picture on a plate cut like the select screen's (`.stplate`, the `/api/stage-thumb` image; "No picture" when the server cannot draw one) with its number in the select screen's order (`.stno`, roster order), the name as a small title, the file and size, its songs as **fill-in lines** (the label once, a blank per song, the dashed "+ add a song" blank), and two printed notes: the thumbnail line (`.thumbline`, `data-state` own / added / none) and the **widescreen-fit verdict** (`.wideline`, `data-state` fitted / fits): fitted prints a stamp "widescreen fit: 320,240 → 426,240" + Undo widescreen fit; offered prints the Widescreen fit button and, after it, what the stage is ("320×240, narrower than the build", plus the void warning the button's tooltip carries) on a warning rule. The band's "N narrower than the build" counts from the same widefit answers (`stageMeta`/`drawStageMeta`, a per-render `_gen` so a late answer from an older render cannot write). The remove ✕ sits in the entry's corner. The line still STARTS with its label (test-page-speed reads `.wideline` textContent).
  - **A track** is a row of the sound-test table (`#music > .card[data-id=<track>]`, a CSS subgrid row under the printed head `.mhead`: No. / Track / Size / Listen / Stage fallback / remove). The buttons stay the row's OWN children (a read-only build hides `#music .card > button`). The stage fallback prints an "★ In use" stamp (`.meta.fb`, title "Plays on stages with no song of their own") + **Clear**; every other track offers **Use as fallback** (the two buttons were "★ stage fallback — clear" and "use for stages with no song"; their titles are unchanged and their aria-labels name the track). No tracks: a dashed box saying how to add one.
  - **Menu music** stays at the bottom of the Music tab (DJ AR's tip says "set at the bottom of the music tab", and a tip is never edited): `#menuMusic` under its own side head, two fill-in lines (Title screen, Character select).
  - **The notes** (`dl.bkm-notes`) say what each control does, from the controls' own tooltips and this file; the adding/removing notes (`.rw`) are hidden in a build opened read-only. The notes scroll; the hint keeps the foot. Under 760px tall the hint steps aside (as on Characters); under 900px wide the whole margin page does and the list takes the page. Select mode: a stage's tick sits on its plate's top right, a track's takes the No. column.
  - Helpers this layout relies on, unchanged: `removeButton` returns one `button.danger`, `previewButton` one `span` wrap, `musicSelect` a `select` or a `span.roval` - recheck the Music table's grid if one of them changes.
- **The Theme tab is the booklet's "screen and system" spread** (`public/booklet-theme.css`, Phase B, 2026-10-18). The section band (`#themeBand`) carries the title, the count of installed screenpacks (`#themeBarCount` + `#themeBarWord`, "1 screenpack" / "4 screenpacks", written by render's count block) and **+ Add** (`[data-add]`, which still opens the three drop targets and the path row, now under the band); the old `.pbar` is gone from Theme and Mods. The frame (`.pframe`, still the drop target and the one frame fitRoster measures) holds a two-page spread, `#themeSpread` (7fr | fold | 5fr), each page scrolling on its own:
  - **Left page, the screen** (`#themeScreenPg`): side head SCREENPACK, then `#themes` (the screenpack in use, its option groups and common states in `#themeOptCards`, the installed packs, the packs that cannot be used or are incomplete), `#logoStatus` (the startup logo: a label + its state, "Each build uses its screenpack's own." or "<def> (yours - used by both exports)"), `#themeCopy`, and side head SELECT SCREEN with `#gridCap` as its aside over the `#selGrid` plate.
  - **Right page, the fight screen** (`#themeFightPg`): `#lifebarMix` (side head LIFEBARS AND FIGHT EFFECTS, kicker ライフバー); SHiZUKA's hint box at its foot (`#themeHint`) went in the owner's second review (2026-10-18).
  - **Every row the renderers draw as a `.card` is printed as a fill-in line** by CSS alone: its first `<label>` in a 132px margin column (sentence case through `::first-letter`; the renderers still write "lifebars "), the select as a blank on its rule, its buttons beside it, the `.meta` under the value in the second ink. A row of `#themes` with a `.note` ("cannot be used", "incomplete pack") is flagged: the flag ink in the margin, the label in `--bad`. Installed packs and library lifebars are printed tags (`.chip`), the delete square on each keeps its two-click arming.
  - **The select-screen preview is re-drawn when the Theme tab is shown** (`ON_SHOW.theme: () => renderSelectGrid()`): it is sized from its column's width, which is 0 while the tab is hidden; the old entry was `ON_SHOW.chars`, from when the preview lived there, so a Studio opened on Characters drew it at the 900px fallback (too wide for a 7fr page; measured after the fix: the plate's scroll width equals its width).
- **The Mods tab is the booklet's "extras" spread.** Band `#modsBand` (MODS, "Your mods 1 of 2 on" from `#modBarCount`, hidden while there are none, and **+ Add**). `#mods` holds both pages so every selector the suites use (`#mods .arow`, `#mods .mcard`, `#mods .grp[data-grp]`, `#mods .mempty`) and `#mods`' text stay as they were; the frame's body `#modsSpread` is a grid (7fr | fold | 5fr over three rows) and `#mods` takes its tracks through CSS `subgrid` (Chromium 117+, WebView2):
  - **Left page, the Studio's add-ons** (`.grp[data-grp="builtin"]`): an options list - a square to tick in the margin (the real checkbox, self-drawn), the name, ALWAYS ON / OFF BY DEFAULT / NOT IN THIS BUILD as outlined stamps, what it does, and what Off loses; an add-on switched off from its default is marked in the warn ink. The **H-MUGEN module** row is drawn by the same code under the same rules as before (GRAIL Part IV's hmodule bullet); it is an ordinary `.arow`.
  - **Right page, your mods** (`.grp[data-grp="user"]`): where they are kept, the drop target and File... / Folder... / Open mods folder, then each mod as a catalog entry - its picture on a plate, name, version, its own On square, maker, files, description, homepage, overlap and warning chips, Read me / Open folder / Remove. A mod that is off has its picture grayed and an OFF stamp on the plate.
  - `.after` is the right page's footnote; `#mods` holds only the mods (test-mods-ui and test-page-speed read `#mods`' text and HTML: the H gallery's name must be nowhere in it outside H-Mugen mode). WB's hint box `#modsHint`, which sat under the footnote outside `#mods`, went in the owner's second review: `#modsSpread` has two rows now, the pages and the footnote. A group's summary is the page's side head; folding still works (`MODS_SHUT`).
  - Both spreads: under 900px wide each becomes one column that scrolls as a page. Buttons inside the renderers' rows print as `.bk-btn.sm` (restated with two ids over the old `#themes button:not(...)` / `#mods button:not(...)` rules). A read-only build hides `[data-add]`, `#themeCopy`, `#logoStatus button` and the whole Mods tab exactly as before. `#pathRow` (Browse... / File... / the path / Add, shared by every tab) still wears its old print.
- **The Settings tab is the booklet's options section** (studio.html `#panel-settings`, `renderSettings`; `public/booklet-settings.css`; 2026-10-18, Phase B). Still one `.pframe` (`#setFrame`, so fitRoster sizes it like every frame tab) with `.pbody` (`#setBody`) the one scroller. The **section band** (`#setBand`, "Settings 設定") carries the override count in its meta (`#setBarCount`: "**3** changed from the engine", or "engine defaults"; the rail badge `#setCount` is unchanged). The page (`#settings`, filled by renderSettings exactly as before) opens with the **chapter strip** - Common, All, Controls, Online, Engine (`.settabs .tab`, `aria-selected`) - printed on the plate with the open chapter in the band ink; renderSettings appends its caption before the strip, so the strip is printed first with `order: -1` (do not "fix" the DOM order: the caption is inserted with `insertBefore(host.firstChild)`). Each group (`details.grp`, `details.kslot`) is a **side head that opens**: an empty square when shut, solid when open, caps, the count, the run-in rule; "N changed" prints as a mark chip and a changed row carries the mark down its edge with its name in the mark ink. Rows are ruled, zebra on the plate; fields are boxed (`--line`, `--sunk`), the filter a fill-in line. The outer **margin** holds, on Common and All only (`#setBody:has(#settings > .filterrow)`), a **key to the row marks** (desktop only, web only, website default, advanced, the warning sign, a changed row), each in the words of that mark's own tooltip - new printed text, no new behavior. The margin scrolls with the page. The Settings margin (`.set-margin`) holds only the marks key now: a chapter that prints no marks (no filter row: Controls, Engine) gives the page the margin's width (`#setBody:not(:has(#settings > .filterrow))`, booklet-settings.css): 1232px of page against 927px at 1400x900. (WB's hint box `#setHint` went in the owner's second review, 2026-10-18.) Under 1100px wide or 760px tall the margin narrows; under 760px wide it goes under the page. Online, Controls and Engine are the same chapters re-printed: asks boxed in the warn ink (danger: the flag ink), the setup log as a ruled data-face log, the Players table with a band head, a key slot's groups under small side heads, the engine zip's file name keeping its case (`bk-nocaps`). **A disabled button on this page prints with no fill and dimmed** (opacity .6): test-host-ui reads exactly that for "Set up my servers" waiting for a token. The punch / kick strength icons are the band constants `--wb` / `--tmpl` / `--ar`. The `#panel-settings #settings ...` two-id selectors exist only to outrank studio.html's old `#settings button:not(...)` x6 rules; when those go, an id can go.

Its rules are `:root #topbar #optsPop ...` in booklet-settings.css (they must outrank the chrome's `#topbar #optsPop`).

It is built from the h3's `::before` (the cut) and `::after` (the paper with the rule) in a flex row - no wrapper markup - so code that sets a title with `textContent` keeps working. A long title wraps on the plate; `--tail` reserves room on the rule for the kicker and Close.

A new rule that dims text in a sheet must use `--ink2`.   - **A new dialog:** add its id to the `:is(...)` lists in booklet-dialogs.css (spelled out per rule because each needs the `:root :is(#id)` specificity to outrank the dialog's own `<style>` later in studio.html), give it an `<h3>` first (after its Close button) and a `data-k`.
