Callers: Characters (the picked character's select slot), **About** (`aboutFolio`: while the tab shows, "Ver." + the number in the cover's "Version 2.0"; the dash back when it closes, unless another page wrote the folio), the **export's back page** (`folioWas = setFolio.state(); setFolio('Back')` on open, `setFolio.restore(folioWas)` on close if the folio still says Back). **The Moves window prints the select slot**: Characters' `Moves…` passes the slot LABEL and what "of" counts, `&slot=04b&of=31%20cells` (`charSlots().label`; none for a character off the grid or on disk only), and moves.html prints "No.04b" as the band's `.no` (`#slotNo`, title "Select screen cell 04b of 31 cells"); an older opener's bare numbers (`&slot=8&of=17`) still print ("No.08", "of 17 cells"); nothing when absent. **The header mascot's blink**: `scheduleBlink` arms no timer while `#wbSlot .art` has no box (a head too narrow for him, `fitTabRow`'s `tm`); a pose change (setWbState) re-arms it. - **The chrome is the booklet's** (2026-10-18): a **running head** (the energy.jp imprint plate, which opens About; the title; then Select Screen ↗, Test in Browser, Website / Desktop, Export, Options), a **thumb-tab rail** printed down the outer (right) edge (Characters, Stages, Music, Theme, Mods, Settings, About - About is a printed tab now, not the "?"; Up/Down and Left/Right move between tabs; inactive tabs in the printing's own inks, the active one in the band ink - see the printing bullet), and a **running foot** (the readout: Ready, the counts, the build size, a failure's first line, the loading seconds, the working bar on its top rule; the energy.jp imprint line; the folio, `setFolio(no, of)`, "No.08 of 17" for the open character's select slot). Nothing clips. **A failure keeps its line** as before: cut at a word under 48 characters (`failLine`, `48ch` in the CSS), whole on hover and in the toast; the `.t1` step leaves a failure's line alone and the `tf` step takes it only after the size, so a failure never makes the foot give up more than the Ready state does at the same width. **Try again** stays clickable under the loading gate, and a read that lands puts "Ready" back. While the first read runs, the readout says it can take a minute and, from 8 s on, counts the seconds (`still reading - N s`). Each tab carries its symbol and title side by side and the step only swaps which one shows; with symbols, the name and count move to the tooltip and the name stays the tab's aria-label. The symbol takes the title line's exact height, so the row never jumps when it switches. **About** is the last tab, printed as the booklet's first spread: the **front cover** on the left page (the logotype over SHiZUKA, her glasses swirling - next bullet) and the **staff page** on the right (what the Studio is and why it exists, the links to energyjp.com and the engine's GitHub fork, the band line-up, the credits, Credits & licenses... and the keys the Studio answers). A tab with no kind (Settings, About) hides the paste-a-path row, and `.pathrow[hidden] { display: none }` has to stay: `.pathrow`'s own `display: flex` beats `[hidden]`, and the row showed whenever the Studio opened on one of those tabs. The Options popover's rows are the same case (`#optsPop label[hidden]`, `#optsPop .optrow[hidden]`, `.buildsize[hidden]`): without that rule the Website showed the Desktop's rows and the Desktop showed Public build.
- **SHiZUKA's swirling glasses** (About; aboutTab in studio.html, public/about, tools/about-art.py):
  - **The picture ships with its lens pixels cut out, and the swirl is painted UNDER the holes**, one canvas per lens. Hair crosses both lenses (whole strands and thin dark wisps), and it stays in the picture, so it is drawn over the swirl. Drawing a swirl on top of the picture would paint over her hair.
  - **Lens paint** is the lavender ground and the violet spiral: blue the largest channel, red never past it (skin is red over blue), green present (her hair has none), not dark, not fully saturated. A flood from each lens's middle over lens paint is the lens. Enclosed islands join it unless they look like a strand's cut-off tip. After the fits, the old line's darkest violet stuck beside a strand joins the hole (three steps at most) and a strand's faint gray tail goes back to the strand, so no still violet sits on a strand while the swirl turns.
  - **The swirl** is an Archimedean spiral in the lens's own fitted ellipse, refit to the one the artist drew (center, turns, direction, phase, width). The line, its darker middle and its dithered soft edge are colors measured off the picture. The ground under it is a degree-4 polynomial surface fitted to the plain ground: it holds the violet shading toward the rim, and it cannot hold a spiral. A painted-out ground (the old line filled in from beside it) kept a ghost of the old spiral a few levels deep, which shows through the moving one. Specks are scattered on the picture's own grain of about three pixels.
  - **The still frame** (reduced motion) is the fitted spiral placed and phased where the artist drew hers: close to the drawing, not the drawing itself. Measured against the drawn lenses: color error about 15 and 18 levels against about 28 and 33 for a flat lens, and the line overlapping at 0.60 and 0.56 (IoU).
  - **Its own clock:** requestAnimationFrame gated to about 24 updates a second (20 on a 60Hz screen), speed kept in real time (0.45 turns a second, clockwise, drawing the eye inward). It draws only while the About tab shows, and the first tick after a start only sets the clock, because the canvases already hold that frame. The art is not fetched until the tab is first opened.
  - **The cover is always dark, and she is a shadow in it** (2026-10-22, the owner: "I would rather that part of the screen be always dark and scary looking like the previous look we had"; studio.html `aboutTab`, `public/booklet-about.css`). The cover prints on its own inks in every printing and every Look - the old dark pane's ground as it rendered (`--cv-ground` #161130), a deeper black for the title field and the strips (`--cv-deep`), a thin cut of her violet along the field's edge, MUGEN in a pale ink over STUDIO on a deep violet bar - while the staff page beside it follows the printing. She is the old pane's SHiZUKA again: her body faded toward the left and the bottom (`--fade`, two gradients intersected) and **multiplied into the cover** over her own violet glow (`.aboutArt::before`), so only her glasses keep their full strength; every time the tab opens she **enters as a silhouette** (`img.shade`: the same picture, brightness 0, a violet rim; held 900 ms, then a 1.8 s fade into the blend - `enter`), and under reduced motion she is simply there. For the blend to reach the cover, **her box must not be a stacking context** (no z-index, transform, opacity below 1 or filter: it sits in the cover's own layer after the field in the markup, under the title and strips), and the cover keeps `isolation: isolate` so it is the group she multiplies into. From 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-22 the booklet had printed her opaque on the cover's plate ink (the band-ink field); that look is gone.
  - **Each swirl canvas is clipped to its lens hole**, by a mask of the art's own alpha, inverted (the art laid over the canvas, excluded from a solid layer). The opaque picture over the canvases hides their rectangles too, and the mask stays so the swirl can never show outside the holes if the picture over it ever stops being opaque. The test compares the canvases' corners with the swirl on and off (a few levels' allowance), then RAISES the canvases over the picture: masked they still show nothing outside the holes; raised and unmasked (the negative control) they show.
  - **Where she stands** (`aboutTab` `fit`): 110% of the cover's width, never taller than 68% of it (the title keeps the field above her hat), the picture's bottom cut standing on the foot strip, her far hair cropped by the cover's right edge (`right` = -(width - 0.98 x cover) x 0.62). Her box takes its ratio from shizuka.json. Her lenses stay inside the cover, clear of the title, the top and foot strips and the staff page's text at every window shape the test sweeps (2048x1080 down to 760x800, portrait 864x1460).
  - **Rebuilding the art** needs the original full picture, kept outside the repo: `python tools/about-art.py <source .png>`. The rough lens ellipses in it are read off that picture. Check a rebuild with `node tools/shoot-about.js <folder> --reduce --dump` then `python tools/about-art-check.py <source .png> <folder> reduce`. Test: `tools/test-about.js`.

  Each tip is a true, useful thing about building, in the member's own voice from their profiles and diary on energyjp.com. **WB** writes whole, dry sentences, a few thousand years tired, and dodges questions about himself. **DJ AR** is all lower case, loud, the shades never come off. **SHiZUKA** does not speak, she hums; she writes in lower case with kaomoji and a little Japanese, cute until the last line. Outside it they never show, and no other tip points at them. A tip about the build is measured, not asserted (a function that returns null when it cannot answer), and says something true for an empty library too. Changing a tip's voice never licenses changing its fact without checking it: the old "a smaller grid drops what does not fit" was wrong (who does not fit stays in the build past the last cell, and E-Select's footer names them).

WB: idle, shutter1, shutter2, shut, working, done, error; DJ AR and SHiZUKA: idle, blink, working, done, error. Made by `python tools/mascot-sprites.py <picked folder>` from the picked 1024x1024 pictures on flat green, which are kept OUTSIDE the repo (like the About art's source): it measures the ground per picture, keys by how much greener than red and blue a pixel is, unmixes the ground out of edge pixels and de-spills (no pixel greener than its own red or blue, again after the resample), ALIGNS every frame on idle by searching the shift that lays its feet band and its body band over idle's (both must agree - it refuses a frame that was redrawn at another size; the picks measured 0,0 for all 14), crops a member's frames to ONE union box (his feet on its bottom row, so swapping never moves him), scales the box to 192 rows (premultiplied, Lanczos) and writes bare PNGs - IHDR, IDAT, IEND, nothing else (the picks carried IPTC and XMP). 192 rows: the largest drawing is About's DJ AR at 53px and the head's 44px, so 192 stays a downscale up to 360% scaling (head 430%).

- **The Studio's printing** (Options → Look + Day / Night; the booklet, 2026-10-18). The Studio is printed like a 2000s fighting-game instruction booklet (`docs/STUDIO-BOOKLET.md` is the component contract): five LOOKS - **Energy** (the default), **WB** (was Blue; a saved `blue` reads as `wb`), **DJ-AR**, **SHiZUKA**, **High contrast** - each printed on **Day** stock (paper, the default) or **Night** stock (dark). Ten printings; the default is Energy, day. Energy day is the round-1 manual's two inks (paper `#EFF0EC`, sumi `#17181C`, shu vermilion `#C8301A`, ink 66% `#5C5D62`, 6% screen `#E1E2DE`, 30% screen `#AEAFAC`); Energy night is near-black stock and red (paper `#060607`, plate `#121316`; the owner's first review, 2026-10-18, asked for a darker black than the first `#0E0F12`); the other four keep the booklet round 2's printings. Kept per computer (`studio.look`, `studio.paper` in localStorage), every Studio window follows through the storage event. `public/theme.js` sets `<html data-look>` (no attribute = Energy) and `<html data-paper="day|night">` before the body paints; `window.studioLook` has `get/set`, `paper/setPaper` and `printing()`, and a `studio:printing` event fires on every change. `public/themes.css` restates EVERY token any page draws with, for each printing, from one source: **`tools/printings.js`** (`node tools/printings.js` checks every text/ground pair - every text pair 4.5:1 or better, lines 3:1 - and `--write` regenerates themes.css's block and its header's contrast table). Never hand-edit the block; never draw a color outside the tokens. The booklet tokens (`--paper --plate --ink --ink2 --rule --line --band --onband --band2 --onband2 --spot --onspot --mark --onmark --flag --onflag --warn --onwarn --focus`, and the member tints `--wb-tint --ar-tint --sz-tint`, which no component reads since the hint boxes went in the second review) drive the older ones (`--bg = --panel = paper`, `--panel2 = --face = plate`, `--text = --hi = ink`, `--dim = --mute = ink2`, `--accent = mark`, `--key = line` ...), so the Phase-B tabs, the dialogs and the other windows followed with no CSS of their own until Phase B printed them in their own area files (the Stages/Music, Theme/Mods, Settings, dialogs and E-Select bullets). **The thumb-tab rail prints in the printing's own inks** (`--tab`, `--ontab`, `--tab-hover`, `--tab-edge`, derived in `tools/printings.js tokens()`): an inactive tab is a plate - by day halfway between the 6% plate and the 30% screen (`--rule`), by night the `--line` ink 30% into the plate (55% on hover) - with the ink on it; the active tab is the band ink (`--band`/`--onband`) pulled into the page with the `--band2` cut. High contrast states its own (`P[...].tab/tabHover/tabEdge`): plate tabs with an ink keyline (black by day, white by night). The checker holds ontab/tab and ontab/tab-hover to 4.5:1, the focus ring on an inactive tab (`--focus`) to 3:1, and a tab (or its keyline) to stand off the paper. The focus ring on the ACTIVE tab is `--onband`: Energy's `--spot` is its `--band`, so the old `--spot` ring vanished on the active tab, where the arrow keys leave the focus. Phase A printed every inactive tab in reverse (`--ink` ground, `--paper` type), and since every night printing's ink is a near-white, every look's Night showed the same light block (the owner's "the white of the tabs doesn't change at all", 2026-10-18). The rail's rules live in three places that must stay in step: booklet.css `.bk-thumb`, studio.html's `#main > nav.tabs > .tab.bk-thumb` (chrome style, higher specificity) and booklet-export.css's `body.xback-open` rule (the back page: no tab active, so the Characters tab prints as an inactive one). Rules learned: `--line` is the 3:1 FIELD rule and a mid tone, so it is never a background behind text (E-Select's menu highlight moved to `--plate`); `--good --bad --warn --ok` are fitted toward the ink until they clear 4.5:1 on paper AND plate (`--ok` is a printing token, not the mockup's constant green, because text is printed in it); the toast is printed in reverse on day stock (`--toast-bg/--toast-ink`) so the band's bright speaker colors stay readable; High contrast's own page rules belong to its NIGHT printing (`[data-paper="night"]`); E-Select's Launch green is `--launch` (white type 5.9:1; the old green carried it at 3.4:1). Everything is square: `:root button, select, input` radius 0, `--r-art`/`--r-thumb` 0 in every window. **The moving sky retired** with the old looks (`#lookSky`, `html.sky`, the gradients, the frosted top bar, Options → Moving background); a saved `studio.lookMotion` is ignored. The old looks' rules (the sky's own clock, the frosted bar's `::before`, DJ-AR's darkened reds) went with them; the DEVLOG keeps their story.
- **In the desktop app a tool window is a window the app owns** (`studio-go/cmd/mugenstudio/toolwindow.go`). Every `window.open()` for the Studio's own address - Select Screen, Moves, Palettes, the animation editor and player - lands in a window the shell creates, hosting its own WebView2 controller as the main window does, and the page gets it back through `put_NewWindow`: a name still finds the open window, `opener` works, `close()` works from either side, the page's `<title>` is the window title, and a `width=/height=` request is honored in CSS pixels. Any other web address goes to the real browser and a `mailto:` link to the mail program, each only on a click, and every other scheme is refused; a tool window's page can also ask for the main window back and to be asked before it closes (§3.1b, *Tool-window messages*). **Why:** WebView2's stock popup draws text with grayscale smoothing, while the same page in an app-hosted WebView gets ClearType. At 125% the stock popup's text reads as blurry next to the browser's own. Nothing in the page changes that. **To test the shell without a window on screen:** build the package's files beside a harness `main` that overrides `toolShow` / `toolPlace` (off-screen, tool-window style, shown without activation), set `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=N --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion`, drive the pages over CDP, and capture with `PrintWindow(..., PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` from a DPI-aware thread. A change to the Go shell needs `node scripts/build-app.js`.
- **The Animation panel grows with Properties.** The stage takes what the controls beside it leave (it is sized from its section's width by a container query, on the stage itself rather than through an inherited variable): 138px at every default panel width, up to 420px or about half the window's height. The panel always keeps its scrollbar's room (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`), or the section would be 9px wider whenever the panel did not scroll, and a stage that grows can bring the scrollbar back. Past its default the sprite is scaled up in whole numbers only (crisp pixel art, like the pop-out window); at 138px nothing is magnified, as before. The player re-fits when its stage changes size and keeps the point a zoomed view was on. Its arrow and space keys stay on the stage, so they never also walk the roster.
- **A character whose own stand action is blank** (`modlib.charBodyAction`, 2026-10-19). When action 0 exists and none of its frames draws a sprite the file has, the action list (`/api/char-actions`) carries `body`: the action the game draws the body with, and the player opens on it with one plain line under its readout (`.avnote`). Found from the state files the .def names (st, stN, cmd, cns and a char-local stcommon via `scenelib.stateFiles` - never a folder glob, an engine file skipped): a `ChangeAnim`/`ChangeAnim2` that ONLY A HELPER CAN FIRE - its triggerall, or every live trigger group, needs `ishelper`/`ishelper(N)` (the rule `movelib helperRunStates` uses; `trigger1 = ishelper(5)` beside `trigger2 = 1` is one the root fires too and does not count; `scenelib.ishelperNeed`: the whole trigger, or a conjunct of one with no top-level `||`, brackets around either read through, so `(IsHelper(7))` counts; a dead group such as `trigger1 = 0` and `!ishelper` do not count) and whose value is a literal action that draws. The helper is named when every group names the same one. Preferred: one whose first frame is group 0 -> "This character's stand animation (action 0) draws nothing; showing action 44000, which its files have helper 22 play" (what the files show, never a claim about why). Else the first action whose frames draw group 0, then the first helper candidate, then the first action that draws - those two say so without naming a helper. Cached per character on the stamps of the .def, .air, .sff and each state file. Grim Reaper Mai (VirtualTek Fighter; 20,168 actions, 141 with a sprite; 3.9 MB of state files): helper 22 -> 44000; her action list answers in about 0.17 s the first time and 0.10 s after (the .air parse). A character whose action 0 draws gets no `body` and reads nothing more. The all-slots palette window (`public/palgrid.html`) takes its stance from `body` the same way when action 0 draws nothing ("Stance: sprite 0,0 (action 44000; action 0 draws nothing)"); with no `body` it says "Action 0 draws no sprite", and "No action 0" only when there is none. Test: `tools/test-helper-body.js`.
- **H is a choice per bundle: the H-MUGEN module (hmodule.js, 2026-10-09).** Until then "the scan found an H character" and "show the H side" were one event, so one false positive (a throw table, a meter bank, an effect numbered in a pair window) switched H on in a build with no H content (the owner: "My whole 'H settings as a nice surprise' factor seems to be biting us"). Now the scan only ASKS, once per bundle, after a FULL reading (a build opened read-only asks when its background reading arrives): **Enable the H-MUGEN module?** - Enable / Not now (asked again when a new H character turns up: `roster.hModuleSeen`) / No, not for this bundle. The answer is `roster.hModule` ('on', 'off', 'unasked', 'notnow'), written by `POST /api/h-settings` into the bundle's roster.json (in a read-only bundle, the Studio's own record of the build - the route is on the read-only allowed list); `/api/roster` always takes it, and every character's `hRole`/`hReviewed`, from the disk, like the mod switches; a read-only build's `/api/studio` (whose answers are cached for the session) lays the record's H answers over the cached ones, so an answer shows on the next read without a rescan. **A roster from before the module (no key) is grandfathered once, at server start**: on where its scan (the detected roles only - a scan that throws counts as no pair here) makes a gallery pair and the bundle is not read-only, else 'unasked' - and the answer is written, so it never moves again with a character added, removed or re-marked (a live rule did: the checker's F2). Every roster made since (`bundles.create`, `openExternal`, the whole-build import) starts 'unasked'. **Changed any time**: the Mods tab's first Studio add-on row, **H-MUGEN module**, listed where the scan finds H content, where the module is on, or - once someone has turned it on anywhere (localStorage) - in every bundle; a build opened read-only has no Mods tab, so its switch is the **H-MUGEN** button on the read-only banner. The question's footer names whichever applies. **With it off or unanswered** nothing H shows and the exports leave the gallery out: `modmgr.builtinOn` answers off for `hgallery` and its modes, which the web build (vfslib) and the desktop export both ask, and `modmgr.listMods` (the Mods tab's `/api/mods`) does not list them. **With it on**: Properties has **H role** (As detected / Giver / Receiver / Giver and receiver / Not H: `chars[i].hRole`, which the badges, hearts, filters, pair bench, `vfslib.rosterBadges` and the gallery's pairs - `gallerydata.buildGalleryData`: 'none' in no pair, 'receiver' never a giver, 'giver' never a receiver, 'giver'/'both' tried as givers - take over the scan's; the gallery still shows only scenes it can read), and a **review queue** ("Is this character H?", one dialog, a row each with up to four frames of what the scan read as pair art: H as detected / Not H / Ask later) for the verdicts worth a second look - `hmodule.reviewQueue`, asked by `GET /api/h-review?chars=` for the characters the page's reading found H. Its three signs were measured over the 2,584-character census: SMALL (a receiver's unplayed window actions mostly under 64 px: Nicotine Caffeine's sparks; 5 in the H builds), REACH (its own code reaches them through a multiplied computed number: Valdoll's dragon forms, Chousokabe Motochika; 0 in the H builds), SIX (a giver resting on six-digit numbers outside every family: Rera, Z Helper Futa). Rejected: pair-like sprite groups (~200 real receivers use custom groups), art its own moves draw (27 real, misses Valdoll), the weakest giver doors (11 real givers, Batman). "H as detected" stores the verdict's signature (`hReviewed`); a different verdict asks again. Inside the module, H-Mugen mode is the condition that a character's EFFECTIVE role (`hRoleOf`: the owner's word over the scan's) is giver or receiver (the page's `hMugenMode()`). Every surface that names the adult-content roles appears only in it: the pair bench button, the filter chips and their group, the role in the Filter button's own tooltip, the pair-art sentence on the palette window's button, and SHiZUKA's H tips. Everything H asks that one function, the bench included, and a chip left on from a roster that had H is turned off rather than left quietly filtering. Two surfaces read the scan directly and ask the module themselves: the palette window shows pair art only when the Studio opens it with `pair=1` (the module on and the character a receiver - before, every action in a pair window was "pair art", family name and all, in any bundle), and the content audit names a role only with the module on (its common-state note no longer says "receiver" either: "a state the opponent puts her in can set it"). A build of ordinary fighters says nothing about any of it. Two things are deliberate: the "turned on anywhere" flag is per machine, so after one Enable the Mods row and the banner button show in SFW bundles too (off, one click from on); and Properties addresses a character by its `mountAs`, so variants sharing one (a rare roster shape) share the H role control's first match. Tests: `tools/test-h-cards.js` (the source), `tools/test-h-module.js` (the module), `tools/test-band-tips.js` (the page, off and on). Since the booklet (2026-10-18) the H role sits under its own side head on the character page. **The H marks keep fixed hues in every printing** (the owner, the same day: "Pink for the heart and receiver, and blue for giver, no matter the theme"; `public/booklet-hmarks.css`): `--h-pink #E5308A` and `--h-blue #2E78F0`, constants like `--tmpl`, with black type on them (`--h-on`). They are the brightest values that still clear 3:1 (non-text) on every printing's paper, plate and ink, day and night: a lighter pink drops under 3:1 on Energy day's plate, a darker one on WB night's. Where: a tile's heart (the pink heart on a black square, so it reads on any portrait: 5.12:1), the GIVER / RECEIVER badges on the character page (filled in the role's hue, black caps 5.06 / 5.12:1; the heart after the word keeps a gap), the H role side head's mark (the pink heart), the Filter dropdown's giver / receiver chips (a square of the hue ruled in black - `renderFacetBar` sets `data-facet` on every chip; the black rule is what holds 3:1 on that dropdown's old see-through chip ground, a mid gray by day), and the pair bench (the roster bar's ♥ key in pink, the sheet's heart as a tile's, a square of the hue before "giver" / "receiver", the scene panes' top rules). Measured on all 10 printings, lowest 3.58:1 (see the lane notes). E-Select and the index rows print no H mark; a heart inside a `<select>` option cannot take a color. Still shown only with the module on and a character H (verified hidden with it off by test-h-cards / test-band-tips).
- **Filter** (desktop Studio, ≡ Filter at the right end of the roster bar) — a dropdown of chips that narrow the roster grid and list by what the Studio already knows about each character: sprite format (SFF v1 / v2), a palette repair on offer, Studio edits with a backup to revert, more than one `.def` in the folder, giver / receiver, in the build or only on disk. Chips in the same group widen (v1 or v2); chips in different groups narrow (receiver and a repair on offer); both combine with the name filter. Each chip shows how many characters it matches on its own. The palette and edit chips use the same conditions Properties uses to offer a repair or a revert. Characters only on disk have not been scanned, so they match only the build chips. The chips are remembered; the dropdown closes like a menu (a click elsewhere, or Esc), and while any chip is on the button shows how many and the roster count reads shown / total.
- **Other versions** (desktop Studio: click the build count on the roster bar — it is underlined only when there are some) — the other `.def` files in your characters' folders that are not on the select screen yet, listed with what each one is (AI build, AI removed, older engine, engine target, different art, separate character — the same labels as Properties › Versions). **Add** puts one on the select screen as its own slot; **Show** opens the character at its Versions section. Duplicates of a version already in the build are not counted.
- **Settings › Engine** — which official upstream zip the desktop export builds against (since Phase 8 only `Ikemen_GO-modern-input-windows.zip` or a versioned release newer than 1.0.x; see 5.6 and Decision 24; this line first described the older `Ikemen_GO-<version>-windows.zip` rule): the newest by *version* (by file name, v0.99 sorts above v0.100), a warning when more than one sits in the folder, whether the zip holds what an export reads (the executable, the menu scripts, the common states, the lifebars, a default screenpack), and which engine the desktop export folder was last built with. The website export and Test in Browser never read the zip. The Studio server also prints the zip it found at startup.
- **Options › Content › Bundles…** — separate sets of content. **Main** is the content beside the program; a new bundle starts empty with one stage (Mountainside Temple) in `Content/<name>/`, and exports to its own folders (`dist-desktop-<name>`, `dist-pack-v2-<name>`), so switching never overwrites another build. A bundle opens only in a new server process, because every folder is resolved once at start (layout.js, and the modules that keep paths from it). **In the desktop app, Switch to this is the whole switch:** the choice is written, the window restarts its own server and reloads the page (below), and the page says which bundle opened, read back from the server. **Anywhere else** (a browser, or a window built before it could restart) the button is **Open this next**: it records the choice and a popup says it opens when the Studio is closed and opened again. **Stay on this** cancels a pending switch; in the app a pending choice also offers **Switch now**. **A bundle's name** is 1-40 characters from A-Z, 0-9, space, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit and never ending in a dot or a space (`bundles.js` `NAME_RE`), because Windows does not keep a trailing dot or space in a folder's name. A name taken from a build's folder is cut to fit by `externalName`, and the Bundles importer's suggested name by the same chain; bundles made before the rule are listed as they are.
  - **A switch waits while something would be cut short:** an export running (`buildState`), a build being imported, or E-Select holding unsaved work, and the toast says which and what to do. E-Select answers over the `studio-restart` BroadcastChannel (`unsaved?` → `{page, unsaved}`, half a second to reply), because the Studio's page loses its handle to that window whenever it reloads itself. Only E-Select answers. The other tool pages write as they go, except the animation editor's work in progress - an arrow-key nudge waiting out its 450 ms pause, a time change or a shared box marked *not saved yet*, a structural plan waiting on Apply: those are moments of work, not saves, and the switch does not wait for them.
  - **The restart** (`nativeRestartServer`, studio-go `server.go`): the window closes every tool window, guards released (their pages show the bundle that is going away, and the page has already asked), closes the server's stdin, starts a new server **on the same port**, and navigates the main window to studio.html. Same port because the page keeps its settings per address (the look, the last tab, E-Select's preferences); a new port would be a Studio that forgot them. A failure calls `window.__serverRestartFailed(message)` and the page says to close and reopen.
  - **A test that calls server.js's request listener with a fake response must give it `on()`**: the listener counts API requests in flight by the response's finish and close. Seven suites lost their route checks without a word until theirs had it.
  - **The server leaves when its stdin closes** (`--exit-on-stdin-close`, passed only by the window): it stops listening, lets the API requests in flight finish (at most 15 seconds; a request is where the Studio writes), then exits. The window kills one still there after 20. A window that dies takes its server with it the same way. A server started by hand never reads stdin. Closing the window still kills the server at once, as before.
  - Measured: the real server goes in under 10 ms and the next answers after about 0.1 s; the page reload is the rest. Tests: `tools/test-bundle-switch.js` (the server and the page, headless), `go test` in studio-go/cmd/mugenstudio (the restart against a stand-in), and `MugenStudio.exe --selftest <expr> --selftest-restart <expr>` for the real window (the second expression runs in the reloaded page). **Close this folder's Studio window first:** the window is one per app folder (a named mutex, `Local\MugenStudio-` and a hash of the folder, `instance.go`), so a selftest started beside an open window prints `selftest: Mugen Studio is already open from this folder` and exits 2, and a second ordinary start from the same folder says "Mugen Studio is already open from this folder." and leaves. Copies in two folders still open side by side. `studio-server.exe`'s own probe for a Studio already on its port asks `/api/readonly`, which answers at once (4 s timeout), not `/api/studio`, which answers after a full read, so a Studio busy with a long first read is recognized instead of reported as a stranger on the port.
  - **A whole build handed to the add path is offered to the build importer, never added as a character or a stage.** A folder is a whole build when its top holds `mugen.exe` or `Ikemen_GO*.exe` (any case, `Ikemen GO.exe` and `Ikemen_GO_x64.exe` included), or `data/` and `chars/` with a `select.def` in `data/` or at the top, or `chars/` with a config the importer reads (`data/mugen.cfg`, `save/config.ini`, `save/config.json`), which is `inspect()`'s own gate, so every folder the importer takes is offered to it. It is one rule, `public/ikemen/wholebuild-core.js`, answered from the folder's top and the names in its `data/` and `save/` alone: the page answers a drop from its entries, and the server answers a picked or pasted path (`buildimport.wholeBuildAt`, `/api/add-local` with `askIfBuild`), both before a byte is copied or uploaded. Only the Characters and Stages adds ask. A screenpack that ships as a whole game still installs as a screenpack, and a caller of `/api/add-local` that does not ask adds as before. The offer ends with "A big build is often better opened where it is: Options › Content › Bundles › Open read-only reads it and copies nothing." (§3.18). **Import as bundle** opens the Bundles dialog's own importer on the folder, read and waiting for its name; a drop carries no path, so the folder picker asks for it first. Being offered is not being importable: Read says why a folder will not come across. An import begun from the offer ends on a question instead of the toast: **Switch to it now** is this dialog's switch, with its waits and its app-versus-browser difference (in a browser it reads *Open it next* and raises the restart prompt); **Show in Bundles** marks the new bundle in the list and scrolls it into view; **Stay here** closes the question. The Studio never switches by itself. Test: `tools/test-build-drop.js` (the rule, the route, and the page headless with the build dragged in for real).
- **Audit** (desktop Studio, the ✓ button on the roster bar) — the content audit of §3.2b as a card, opened on the character in Properties: **Breaks** (files that will not load, and moves that lead to a state no loaded file defines — the character freezes), **Worth a look** (an opponent sent to a missing state, an attack whose animation is missing, sprite groups the `.sff` lacks in played animations), and a folded **Also noted**. Missing numbers are grouped, each with every file:line that asks for it; the locations are selectable for copying. **Check the whole roster** lists every character worst first, about a tenth of a second each; a row opens its card. Results are read fresh each time the card opens, so a repair shows at once.
- **Moves…** (desktop Studio, a character's details) — every attack state with its frames, collision boxes and HitDef values; plain numbers can be edited in place, with the original kept beside the file. §3.10. The window is printed as the booklet's command-list page with an **Edit off / Edit on** switch (§3.10); its Command List section reads `/api/movelist` (§3.10e): its switch is `enabled`, a row flagged `weak` has no real name, `drawable: false` will print blank in the stock pause menu. Every attack state's Command cell prints an input: its Command List line's, else the reader's `inputs` (plain normals with their stance: `X`, `↓ + X`, `AIR X`; throws; a state of a character that ships her own list). The page draws the writer's TOKENS (what the pause menu prints), the .cmd text beside the opened move. A state with an input but no line says why ("Plain normals stay out of the game's Command List", "prints it on another state's line", "ships a Command List of its own"). States nothing in the -1 enters by a command (follow-ups, helpers, system states, var-driven moves) have none. The third group is "Unique attacks 特殊技" (2026-10-18).
- **Edit…** (desktop Studio, the Animation panel) — the animation editor: element times, sprites, offsets and collision boxes, and insert, delete or move with the `AnimElem` triggers renumbered. §3.11.
- **Fighting stats…** (desktop Studio, a character's Advanced side, beside health, speed and size) — the rest of the character's constants: attack, defence, the super, stun and guard meters, the jump speeds, gravity and the two frictions, each with what it does and what it breaks beside the box. §3.12.
- **Settings › Controls** (desktop Studio) — the keys and gamepad buttons this build ships with, bound by pressing them. §3.13.
- **Settings › Engine, the game rules** (desktop Studio) — the constants every character in the build plays by: the multipliers that turn damage into power, dizzy points, guard points and red life, the switches that let the engine's own common state files run, the tag numbers and the two legacy toggles. Written to a file of this build's own, loaded after the engine's, so the engine's installation is never edited. The common state files the build compiles into every character are listed beside them. §3.14.
- **Settings › Engine, the fight screen** (desktop Studio) — the lifebars: the four bars' positions and fill ranges, the portraits, the names, the timer and the combo counters, with each section's own sprites shown beside the numbers and every reference the pack cannot satisfy named. The build takes its own copy of the screenpack's `fight.def`; neither the engine's nor the pack's is written. §3.15.
- **Nothing selects, nothing drags.** The Studio's standing rule is `body { user-select: none }` with images undraggable, and only inputs, selects and the few Properties fields worth copying set back to text. Two places do not take the body's rule and need it restated: a `<dialog>` (it renders in the browser's top layer, so every button and glyph inside resolved to selectable until `dialog { user-select: none }` was added) and any pop-out page (`animplayer.html`, `palgrid.html`), which shares no stylesheet with the page. A new panel is checked by reading `getComputedStyle(el).userSelect` on its buttons, not by assuming inheritance.

**A delete happens, or it says it did not.** The Node runtime the Studio was built from until 2026-10-22 (23.11, still inside every copy handed out before then) returns from `fs.rmSync` without an error and without deleting anything when the path holds a non-ASCII character anywhere — in the file or folder's own name or in any folder above it (an install under a name with an accent), a single file as much as a folder, with or without `force`. `unlinkSync`, `rmdirSync` and the asynchronous `fs.rm` are not affected. Node 24.22.1, the runtime since, deletes those paths (measured); the rule stands, since it costs nothing and still says when a delete did not happen. So every delete of the owner's content — a character, stage, track, screenpack, logo, lifebar pack, custom palette, a revert's backup or the build's own copy, the half-made bundle a failed create leaves, and whatever a desktop export clears in its folder — goes through `rmTree` or `rmFile` (lifebars.js): each walks by hand with `unlinkSync`/`rmdirSync` when `rmSync` left the path, and throws if it is still there. `rmFile` refuses a folder, so a remover handed `''` or `..` for a file name cannot reach the directory above. A junction or symlink is removed as the link: the top of the walk is `lstat`ed, because following a link deletes what it points at. When a remover has already taken the item out of the build and its files cannot go (a file another program holds open), the error says both — it is out of the build, and which files stayed; a character left that way is an ordinary on-disk-only one and can be removed again. A track is deleted before the roster lets go of it, so one that cannot go stays exactly where it was. The website export's clear of its folder goes through them too, and `studio-layout.json` is deleted with `unlinkSync` and a check (layout.js requires nothing). The Studio's temporary files go the same way since 2026-10-12, because a user name with an accent puts the system temp folder under a non-ASCII path, where every `rmSync` left its file: the import's screenpack staging, an unpacked stage archive, the server's upload, dropped-folder and image-to-stage temp files, modlib's state file parsed alone, and the old engine zip in a portable copy (make-portable says so when it cannot remove it). What still uses `rmSync`: `movelib.js` `parseTextAlone` (a `movelib-check-*` file under the system temp folder, made when a Moves edit is checked; a miss there leaves one small file, not lost work), rmTree's own first try in lifebars.js, and the build scripts (`build-app.js`, `build-exe.js`, the retired `make-kit.js`), which run on the developer's machine.

**A chosen export folder is emptied only when it is already a build.** Both exporters replace their folder: the website export always empties it, and the desktop export empties it to unpack the engine whenever it holds no engine or a different one. "Export to…" hands over whatever folder was picked, so a folder picked by mistake was emptied (D:\Games), except under a non-ASCII path, where the silent `rmSync` spared it by accident. A chosen folder must now be missing, empty, or a build of the same kind — for the website, an earlier export (`index.html` beside `ikemen-fs/`, which every export writes); for the desktop, an Ikemen GO build (`Ikemen_GO.exe`, or the `save/.engine` stamp the exporter leaves). Anything else, a file included, is refused before a file is touched (`checkExportFolder` in export.js, `checkBuildFolder` in desktop.js). An Ikemen GO install is still replaced whole on its first Studio export and whenever the engine zip changes, `save/` included: that is what the stamp is for. The default folders — `dist-pack-v2` and the rest and `dist-desktop` beside the program, or a portable copy's own `Website Export` and `Desktop Export` — are the exporters' own and are not checked. **Nor may a chosen folder be a bundle's or a read-only build's** (`bundles.exportClash`, asked by server.js `exportDest` for both exporters before either touches a file; 2026-10-12). Refused, each with its sentence: the root of a build the Studio has open read-only, or any folder inside it (a desktop export to the root answered 200 and emptied the build, then wrote 183 files into it); any folder inside a bundle's own folder, except Main's in a checkout, whose folder is the program's; and a folder that HOLDS the Studio's own folders (the program, `Settings/`, the bundles' home, `Content/`), a bundle or a read-only build, which an export would empty. Each path is compared as written and as its real path (so a folder not made yet under a junction is still caught), case-folded on Windows.

**An export ends on the back of the booklet, not a toast** (studio.html `showExportCard`, `showExportFail`, the `<dialog id="exportDlg">` and its script; `public/booklet-export.css`; server.js `serveExported`, `/api/export-open`, `/api/export-play`, `/api/export-zip`, both export routes' `result.notes`; `exportnotes.js forExport`; export.js `folderSummary`, `zipFolderContents`; 2026-10-18, reworked after the owner's second review the same day). It is a PAGE of the booklet, not a modal: a non-modal dialog fixed over the page area, so the running head, the thumb-tab rail and the running foot stay live; what is under it is inert while it is open; the folio reads "Back" and no thumb tab is the active one; any thumb tab (click or arrows), the energy.jp imprint, Close or Esc turns back. **It says what it is**: the section band reads "Export complete" (エクスポート完了; "Export failed" / エクスポート失敗 after a failure) and the cover's headline (`#exportTitle`) "Your desktop build is ready" / "Your website is ready" (+ " (public build)"), "Desktop export failed" / "Website export failed". One spread, **the cover first and wider**:
- **The back cover** (left, `#exportCoverPg`, 60% of the spread by default): the headline, the build's title (the desktop build's window title when set, else the site title; the website's is what its index.html is branded with) in two inks, the speed cut, **the faces marquee** (`#exportLineup`, `startMarquee`): the build's select faces (48 at most, the list icons' sprite at a whole multiple: 3x in a 75 px cell, 2x in 50 px on a tight page, cropped at 1x when bigger, never scaled by a fraction) run right to left at 32 px a second, one set repeated until it is wider than the strip and drawn twice so the loop has no seam; it stops under the pointer or a focus inside it (a face's name is its tooltip) and is a still row under `prefers-reduced-motion` (the second copy hidden); one face stands still. Then the contents line in the Studio's own counts (the Characters tab's: roster entries that are not empty or random cells; the roster's stages; the export's own size; the engine version or "website"), then the card itself (`#exportOut`): **Play this export and Open folder first, the two largest controls on the page** (`.bk-btn.lg`; Play is the band's primary), a line saying what Play does, Written to, the yellow lines (pre-flight missing files, files another build left, missing license notices, a refused state file, itch.io's limits), Make .zip / Make upload .zip (small, "to hand the build to a friend" / "for itch.io or any host") and the small print (the build's sentence, size and largest file, leaderboard art, the export's other notes, How to put it online / To hand it to a friend), and the colophon (the imprint, "Mugen Studio 2.0 instruction booklet, back cover", the printing's name). `#exportOut` keeps every class and button text the suites read (`p.warn`, `.zipout`, `Make .zip`, `Make upload .zip`, `▶ Play this export`).
- **Play this export starts THIS export.** Website: its own address, `/exported/<id>/` (below), opened in the browser as before. Desktop (new): `POST /api/export-play { id }` starts the `Ikemen_GO.exe` that export wrote, in its folder, with no arguments - what `/api/launch-build` does for E-Select's Launch Ikemen GO and what a double-click does - through `startDetached` (the launcher tests stub). By id only, never a path; only a file whose real path is directly in the export folder's real path and is a file (a link leading out, or a folder by that name, is refused: 400; the exe gone: 404); Windows only (`card.play` is false elsewhere and the button is not drawn; the line then says which file starts the game). `{ id, dryRun: true }` answers `{ ok, kind, dryRun, cmd, args, cwd }` (the website: `{ kind: 'web', url }`) and starts nothing: the tests and headless proofs use it, since a real Play opens a game window. A desktop action route (own pages only), allowed in a read-only bundle (it starts an export's program, never the build's), and quiet in the Studio's mutation broadcast (`announceOnMutation`'s QUIET, with `/api/export-open` and `/api/export-zip`, which were announcing a roster change - and making E-Select rescan - on every Open folder and zip). The button is disabled 3 s after a click, so one click is one game window.
- **The divider** (`#exportSplit`, the fold made a `role="separator"`, `aria-valuenow` = the cover's percent): dragged (pointer capture), or the arrow keys (2; with Shift 10), Home = the default 60, End = the widest (80), a double-click = the default; the cover is 35% to 80% and the log keeps at least 300 px whatever was saved. Kept per computer: localStorage `studio.exportSplit` (read in a try; a refused storage keeps it for the session). Under 900 px wide the pages stack, the cover first, and the divider is hidden.
- **The audit log** (right, `#exportNotes`, `role="log"`, focusable so the keyboard scrolls it): the NOTES of the first build, printed as a terminal log in Share Tech Mono on the sunk ground in a ruled frame, under an "Audit log" (監査ログ) plate. A prompt line ("> Desktop export of <title>: the audit read 8 of 8 characters in 0.7 s"), then one entry per character whose content audit has BREAKS (its headline tier: a file the def names that is not there - every one listed, fatal structure - the whole detail, a literal state number no loaded file defines in code it runs - every state and every site), then one entry per kind of repair the export made in its COPY, naming every character it touched; **each entry's first line opens with the select faces of the characters it names** (24px plates at a whole multiple, ten at most then "+N"; the owner kept the icons on the log); each entry is its lines: `BREAK` (reversed on `--flag`) or `FIXED` (`--good`) + the names + the finding, `at` + the evidence (file:line, files, counts; `--ink2`), `export` + what the export did (`--mark`). Entries alternate the sunk ground and the plate. **Every line is whole**: it wraps (`pre-wrap`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere`), nothing is cut with an ellipsis, no "+N" or "…" lists; the log scrolls inside its pane. Then the NOTE lines: the owner's own choices carried out in the copies ("Also in the copies, as you set them: ..."), the characters the audit had no time for (named), the count of characters with things worth a look with **Open the content audit**; WB's sign-off (BAND's `signoff`, never a tip) when the export repaired something, his idle sprite in the tag column (`Booklet.sprites('wb')` + `paintSprite` at 40px, as the head paints him; the box takes no room until it is painted - never a `canvas[data-band]`, whose painter went with the block art and which then stayed a blank 300 x 150 canvas; test-mascots "WB signs the export log"); a closing prompt with a still block cursor. **The log types itself out** (`typeOut`, the owner: "being typed really fast like a terminal"): built whole, then printed back in document order - text a few characters a frame, a face, a button or the cursor when the typing reaches it, an entry when its first character does - at 900 characters a second or more and never much longer than two seconds for the whole log; a click, a key or the wheel in it prints the rest at once, prefers-reduced-motion prints it whole, and `aria-busy` holds a screen reader until it is complete. A break is "Left as written": the Studio never changes what a character's code asks for. Notes name numbers, files and lines only - never a state's label or a command's text. A repair kind the page has no wording for is printed as "fixed in the build's copy (<kind>)", never dropped.
- **A failed export prints the ERRATUM slip** on the cover (`showExportFail`, called from `runExport`'s catch and its pre-flight stop) under "Desktop export failed" in `--bad`, with the band saying "Export failed": the readout's line exactly as failLine cuts it (first line, under 48 characters, at a word), the message in full, and what to do (the pre-flight stop: nothing was written). The card (Play, Open folder) is not shown. The log stays that of the last export that finished this session (its prompt says "The last Website export of ..."); the size only from an export of the same kind.
- `booklet-export.css` restates `.bk-btn` under `#exportDlg` because studio.html's old global `button` rules outrank the component's single class (the chrome does the same under `#topbar`); while the page is open the toast is lifted over it (`body.xback-open #toast`) and the active thumb tab is drawn plain.
- **An exported site does not run from its folder.** The game page fetches its data, and a page opened as a file cannot, so opening `index.html` by double-click shows a boot error. Play this export serves the folder from a web address: `/exported/<id>/`, read-only (GET and HEAD), the folder an export of THIS server process just wrote and nothing else. The id is random, kept in memory (the last twelve) and forgotten on a restart; no route takes a path. A path that resolves outside the folder, a colon (an NTFS stream), a dotfile (`.htaccess`, as a host would), and a link leading out are refused; files below the folder's top are served as data (sandboxed, nosniff), like `/ikemen-fs/`; another site's page is refused (Sec-Fetch-Site), as on `/api/`. A Desktop build is never served.
- **It is the Studio's own address**, so it shares that address's browser storage with Test in Browser: the config saved from playing there is loaded over the export's too, as a returning player's is (§3.16, *The build's rules come across*). A fresh browser profile is what a first-time visitor sees.
- **It is the real site, online parts included.** A private build carries the leaderboard address and this computer's relay, and the host kit answers any origin, so a name claimed from Play this export counts on the real leaderboard. The card's *Online* line says so whenever the build carries a leaderboard: names, matchmaking and the leaderboard work on the exported site and never in Test in Browser.
- **The zip is the folder's contents, beside it:** `<folder>.zip` next to the folder, the files at the zip's root (itch.io looks for `index.html` there; a friend's *Extract All* makes a folder of the zip's name). Written by .NET's `ZipFile` with forward slashes, as `make-portable --zip` and `tools/make-itch-zips.ps1` do; never Compress-Archive, whose backslash entry names itch.io takes as one file name at the root. The paths reach PowerShell as environment variables. It is made as `<zip>.part` and renamed over an earlier zip only after reading back with every file of the folder in it; one zip per folder at a time; the server keeps answering while it runs.
- **Host limits:** itch.io takes 1,000 files, 500 MB in all and 200 MB for any one file for a browser game (itch.io/docs/creators/html5; paths up to 240 characters, which an export never nears), and the Website card says so in yellow, with the build's own numbers, when any is passed. The one-file limit is the one a big roster meets first: game.pak holds the characters. A pak past 2 GiB still finishes: its cache stamp is hashed as each piece is written, never by reading the finished pak back (Node refuses to read a file past 2 GiB whole, and the export failed at its last step). Nothing warns before such a pack yet, and whether a browser loads a pak that size is not measured (`vfs.js` reads the pak whole).
- Test: `tools/test-export-card.js` (the routes, the zips, traversal attempts; `--shots <dir>` adds the cards and Play this export in headless Chrome).

**What an export hands its result page** (`exportnotes.js forExport({ kind, roster, charFixes, budgetMs })`, called by both export routes after the export, each in a try - a failure leaves `notes: null`, never fails an export; `result.notes`, fields ADDED - nothing in the result was renamed or removed): `{ kind, title, characters, stages, chars: [{id, folder}], breaks: [{id, def, headline, missing, fatal, freezes: [{n, sites, definedIn}]}], fixes: {kind: [{id, files, count, ...}]}, choices: {...}, audit: {audited, of, skipped, failed, worthALook, ms} }`. `characters` is the Studio's count (studio.html `realChars`: roster entries without `kind`; two entries of one folder are two), never the desktop export's `characters` (folders copied). A public website build counts its own cut (`exportSite` hands the built roster, unlisted, as a non-enumerable `builtRoster`; it never reaches the JSON). The audit runs per character with pixel comparison off (about 0.12 s a character on Main, 30 in 3.6 s) and stops at **20 s**; the characters it did not reach are named, and the page says the content audit reads the rest. One that throws costs only itself. `fixes` groups the export's own `charFixes` (`{ file: 'chars/<mountAs>/<rel>', kind, ... }` - one shape for desktop.js `fixCopiedCharacters` and the website build's vfslib overlay, which `exportSite` now returns too) by kind and character: `ai-switch-release`, `v2-own-palettes`, `v1-base-palette`, `mugen-hit-priority`, `plus-frames` are audit-like repairs; `portrait-fit`, `palettes`, `palette-order` and `command-list` go to `choices`; an unknown kind is passed on as a repair. Tests: `tools/test-export-notes.js` (the module on a stand-in audit, and the hooks in studio.html, server.js, make-portable); the real exports are proven headless (DEVLOG 2026-10-18).

**Finding (verified 2026-10-18; FIXED the same day, `shippedKey`, see the 3.16 bullet): the website build skipped two repairs on a file-name case mismatch.** RyuDX's def names `data/ryuDX.st` / `data/ryuDX.cmd` while the files are `Data/RyuDX.st` / `Data/RyuDX.cmd`; the repair loop looked the .def's spelling up in the VFS map (keyed by the names on disk), missed, and shipped him without the hit-priority repair (70 HitDefs) and the AI-switch release the desktop build writes. Seen in the two exports' own `charFixes` of one scratch bundle (the back page made the two lists comparable). Every repair in the chain, the Command List writer's def and its `movelist.dat` included, now resolves its file through `shippedKey` and is filed under the build's own key.

Every roster change alters the Build ID. For online play, the opponent needs the identical build (Part II, rule 1).

### Caches: same output, less work (the speed pass, 2026-10-12)

**A cache may change how long an answer takes, never one byte of the answer.** Each one is keyed by a stamp of exactly the files its answer is made from - the path, size and modification time of each (`size@mtimeMs`), as the older caches here already were - and anything else the answer reads goes into the key too, or is read again on every call. A file that would not read is never remembered: the next call tries it again, as a call without the cache would. Every cache is bounded, by entries or by an estimate of its bytes. What the stamp cannot see: a same-size edit inside one file-time tick (about a millisecond on NTFS), the house pattern's known blind spot. The proof for each one is the same three runs, byte-compared with the code before it: cold, warm, and after one edit that must move the answer. Where each cache lives and what it leaves out:
- The H scan and the sprite-key read: §4.3, *A scan is remembered by its files*.
- The tiles' cell portraits: §3.4, *The cell-portrait measurements*.
- The library's names and a folder's main `.def`: §3.1b, *E-Select's reads* and §3.3c.
- The motif's `system.def` and `.sff`: §3.1b, *E-Select's reads*.
- The shipped-copy repairs (v1 base palette, palette order, added colors, hit priority): §3.4f, §4.8c and Part V's hit-priority bullet.
- The H gallery's pairs, kept on disk across starts: §4.10b, *the pair file*.
- The Stages tab's widescreen-fit lines: §3.9, *Widescreen fit*. The Mods tab's list: §3.17.

**The page builds a character card's pickers when the card is shown** (studio.html `deferOptions`, `fillOptions`, `fillCardOptions`). `render()` makes a card for every character, and only one is ever shown, in Properties; each card used to carry every stage and track as an `<option>` (117,843 options at 800 characters). Now a card's stage, music, speed and size pickers are made empty, and the SAME code fills them, from the values captured when the card was made (its stage, the roster's stage list, the music list, its speed and scale), when `selectChar` adopts the card into Properties, or on the first focus, pointer or key event on a picker anywhere else. The hidden pool (`#chars`) is the only place an empty picker lives, and nothing reads a pool card's pickers. `render()` at 800 characters: 973 -> 301 ms. Test: `tools/test-page-speed.js`.

## 3.1b E-Select, the Select Screen editor: what its menus are in this Studio

The desktop Studio's Select Screen editor (`public/grid.html`, the **Select Screen** button) is **E-Select**. Its title row, its three menus (☰, the engine word **Ikemen GO**, the screenpack's name), Preferences and About are modeled on VSelect 2.0.3, and every preference but one defaults to VSelect's own value: a drop onto a character swaps the two (`dropOnOccupied: 'swap'`, the Studio's behavior before 1.0), where VSelect's default moves the rest on. The owner asked for the swap back; Move existing characters stays a choice. VSelect edits a MUGEN install's files where they lie; in this Studio most of those files are generated from the bundle, so each VSelect action is mapped onto the place the Studio keeps that thing. The user guide is `docs/SELECT-EDITOR.md`. Tests: `tools/test-eselect.js` (headless Chrome over its own scratch bundle, with the launch, open and file-dialog routes answered inside the browser so nothing starts; the bundle is made from the engine's files alone - seven kfm copies, two of them `cj` and `Dex_Standin` under [Info] names of their own, and a roster written by the suite - so nothing in the owner's Content/test, which he changes as he plays, can move its count) and `tools/test-eselect-server.js` (the routes, with the program launcher stubbed).

**E-Select is printed as the booklet's select-screen spread** (2026-10-18, Phase B, `public/booklet-eselect.css`, linked after grid.html's own `<style>`; grid.html also links `booklet.css` and `booklet.js`, so its faces are the booklet's: Saira for the UI, Share Tech Mono for data). The layout, the sizes and every behavior are VSelect's as before; only the print changed. The **title row** is the band plate (the ☰ button, E-SELECT, セレクト画面, cut at the slant with the speed cut, `.es-plate`) followed by the path's two menu words and the toolbar as booklet buttons (Save is the one primary, Launch keeps `--launch`); it stays one line at 1400px (47px) and wraps the toolbar below as one block on a narrow window. The **library** is the left page (printed index tabs, the open one ruled in the band; the rows' names in the body face and their second line as data; the log a ruled notes strip). The **screenpack** is the figure, framed in a 2px ink outline (none with Show offscreen cells, where `.screenedge` draws the screen's edge). **Properties** is the right page: side heads, printed labels, boxed values, and the **select slot** beside the title, `No.03` (`#insNo.bk-slotno`), the cell the select screen gives the character - the same walk as the Studio's `charSlots` (a slot group is one cell, a placeholder is a cell), so E-Select and the Characters page print the same number (`printSlot`); the cell tooltip prints it at the cursor ahead of the label (`#celltip[data-no]`, drawn by `::before` so the label stays the tooltip's first text node). The **status bar** is the running foot, its **folio** (`#esFolio`) printing the picked cell's slot, **"No.03 of 7 cells"** (as the Studio's folio counts; "of" = the cells up to the last entry; "No. –" for none or a cell past the end). **The folio never gives way** (the owner, 2026-10-18: the "No." clipped through on a long name/author): it is `flex: none`; the hover line takes only the room left (`flex: 1 1 0`) and ellipsizes in it, the footer's spacer stands down, and the grid readout (`#geom`) ellipsizes last, only when it and the folio alone are wider than the window. Before, the folio could shrink to its 132px min-width while its text needed ~160: the number box shrank to `2ch` and "No.01" ran over "of 4" (measured: the number 28px wide holding 60px of text; now 60/60). **The band's mascot** (`#esMascot`, `Booklet.mascot(b, { page: 'eselect' })`) stands in the head after the plate and deals E-Select's tips as a slip over the page through the Studio's deck (the opener), so the same-window E-Select (pop out off) has none; SHiZUKA's hint box (`#esHint`, `syncHint`) went in the owner's second review (2026-10-18). The Order tab's Arcade / Survival switch is the booklet's segmented choice and Max Matches a side head (its inline colors from `drawOrder` are overruled in the stylesheet). Menus, the cell tooltip, the drop veil, the dialogs and pickers are printed: a 2px ink frame and no soft shadow (VSelect's menu shadow went with the booklet), a dialog's title on its own band plate, the backdrop screening toward the ink by day and the black stock by night. E-Select's dialogs (`.edlg`, `.picker`) keep their own frame; the Studio's `booklet-dialogs.css` is not linked there. **Two traps:** About's name and the stage details' labels must not be uppercased by CSS (the suite reads `innerText`, which applies `text-transform`), and anything added inside `.stage` changes what `computeFit` measures, so the figure has a frame and no caption. No slot numeral is printed on every grid cell: at a fitted zoom the cells are about 16px wide and a numeral would bury the screenpack. A slot group's member count on its cell (`.badge`, "(2)") is printed as the warning fill with its own type (`--warn`/`--onwarn`, 5.9:1 or better in every printing; booklet-eselect.css): grid.html's own rule put the `--warn` ink on a translucent black, 3.5:1 in the day printings (the final merge walk, 2026-10-18).

### What the menus map to

- **Edit mugen.cfg → Engine settings (config.ini)…**, which opens the Studio's Settings tab (Common). `config.ini` is never opened in a text editor: each desktop export rewrites the keys the Settings tab owns, so a hand edit to one of them is undone by the next export without a word. Popped out, E-Select calls its opener's `setTab('settings')` and `setSettingsTab('common')` and raises the main window; in the Studio's own window it stores the two tabs (`ikemen-studio:tab`, `ikemen-studio:settings-tab`) and leaves through the Exit routine.
- **Edit select.def → View select.def…**, read-only. `select.def` is not stored anywhere; it is generated from `roster.json` at every build (§3.1, *Delete through the Studio*), so an edit to the file would be thrown away. The dialog shows `/ikemen-fs/file/data/select.def`, which is what an export writes now, and notes when there are unsaved cell edits it does not include. Everything a `[Characters]` line can hold is placed from the grid, a slot, a lock or Properties (§4.12, *No raw lines*).
- **Edit system.def** opens the pack's own `system.def` in Notepad: the screenpack IS the file the engine reads, so it is edited in place, and E-Select reads the edit on Reload (F5).
- **Select new engine… → Select engine…** and the **Engine executable** preference choose what **Launch** starts: the preference when it is set and valid, else the desktop export's `Ikemen_GO.exe` (`layout.DESKTOP_EXPORT`). Valid means an absolute path to an existing `.exe` with a `data` folder beside it, not a network path, and not inside the bundle's `cache`, `stages`, `themes`, `music` or `lifebars` (other people's archives, which can carry an `.exe` with a `data` folder). `\\host\share`, `//host/share`, `\\?\UNC\` and `\\.\` are refused before any `stat`: a stat of a share that does not answer holds the single-threaded server for tens of seconds, and Windows offers the user's sign-in to the host the share names. A mapped drive letter pointing at a dead share still stalls it. The engine starts with no arguments in its own folder, so it runs what that install was last EXPORTED with; Launch compares the install's `data/select.def` date with `roster.json`'s, says so before starting when the build is older or edits are unsaved, and names the export that fixes it (Export Desktop for the export folder, Export to folder… for any other).
- **Open Motif…, Open new motif…, Open default motif** are the Studio's own screenpack switch and install: `POST /api/theme` (the Theme tab's route; `{motif:''}` is the default screenpack, meaning the roster's motif UNSET, not ikemen1 chosen), `/api/pick-file` then `/api/add-local {kind:'theme'}` (whose result carries the installed pack's `motif`), and the list from `/api/themes`, which skips the character rescan `/api/studio` does. A switch is an undoable step; a switch to the pack already in use is a logged no-op, decided from `/api/roster` rather than from what a menu last showed.
- **Default motif** is a state, not a command: checked when the roster's motif is unset.
- **On startup** chooses the ZOOM E-Select opens at (fit, 100%, the last zoom), because E-Select always opens the build's own screenpack; VSelect's choice there is which motif to open.
- **Empty cell display** is a view setting only. The pack's `showemptyboxes` and `moveoveremptyboxes` are written only from the empty-cell inspector (§4.12).
- Preferences are per viewer, one JSON object in localStorage `eselect:prefs`, applied at once and followed by every open E-Select window through the storage event. The one that reaches the build is the lock label, and only through Save.
- **The stored object is sparse and versioned**: only the keys whose value differs from `PREF_DEFAULTS`, plus `v: 2` (`writePrefs`; Reset stores `{v: 2}`). A key left out reads as its default, so a default changed later reaches every viewer who never chose otherwise. The 1.0 page wrote EVERY key whenever any one changed, so its copy cannot tell a choice from a default it repeated. An object without `v: 2` is read as 1.0's (`storedPrefs`): its `dropOnOccupied: 'move'`, 1.0's default, is dropped; every other key is kept (one equal to its default is only redundant); and the object is written back in the new form once, at load. A later change of a default needs no migration; a change in what a stored value means still does, and needs the next version number.

### Locks

VSelect locks a cell by writing a label comment at the end of its `select.def` line. Here `select.def` is generated, so **a lock is a field on the roster entry**, `locked: '1'`, on a character, on a slot's first member (a lock on any member locks the cell), or on a `skip`, `random` or `dummy` placeholder. It is in `CHAR_PERSIST`, so it survives `cleanChar`, `/api/roster` round trips and Revert, and `setBuildOrder` carries it. A character saved without `locked` keeps the lock the roster has; a placeholder saved without it comes back unlocked, because a placeholder has no identity to look the old value up by. So every caller that saves placeholders sends `locked` on each one (E-Select's `savedOrder`, the Studio's `addToBuild` and `saveOrder`), and an unlocked character is sent as `locked: ''`.

**The label goes on the same line.** motif-core `buildCharacterLines` appends the label to each locked line: `kfm/kfm.def ; LOCKED`, a locked slot member on its own member line, never on `slot = {`. That is safe because main.lua strips every `;` comment from the whole file before any line is parsed (main.lua:1521 in the fork, 1517 in the 1.0.0 zip), so `unlock=`, which is read to the end of its line (main.lua:1344), never sees the label, and `slot = {` and `}` still match their anchored patterns. If an engine ever parses before stripping, the label has to move to a line of its own above the entry. The label is the viewer's preference, sent with every order save and stored as `roster.lockLabel` only when it is not the default (`; LOCKED`); one typed without a `;` gets `; ` put in front, and newlines are flattened. Output without locks is byte-identical to a build that never had them. **Only the DESKTOP build's select.def carries labels** (`buildSelectDef(roster, {locks:true})` in desktop.js, and `/api/select-def`, which View select.def shows); the web build's is written without them, so a lock never moves the web Build ID and nothing browser-side has to parse a comment.

**Anything that reads a shipped select.def strips `;` comments first**, as the engine does. The build import (buildimport.js `parseSelect`) reads the raw line's trailing comment before stripping it: a comment equal to the default label in any case and spacing (`LOCKED` alone counts) or to the active bundle's own `lockLabel` becomes `locked`, and a label on `slot = {` locks the block's first member. studio-lite's `parseShipped` does not strip comments, which is one more reason the web build's select.def is written without labels.

**The server never fills a locked cell** (`placeInRoster` takes the first unlocked unused cell on the grid, else the end of the list, and only with `replaceRandom` on a grid the list already fills, the first unlocked RandomSelect), and a screenpack switch that drops the previous pack's layout skipslots keeps the locked ones. Everything else is the page's, and only while Preferences › Lock cells is on (off, locks are ignored and kept): a locked cell refuses drag, drop, replace, remove, a kind change, a slot, a split and a fill, and a row or column delete refuses to run while a locked cell is in that row or column, or in the last one (the delete would push it off the grid). Every edit that renumbers cells is made as if nothing were locked, then each locked cell is lifted out and put back at its old place (`pinLocks` / `unpinLocks`), which is what "a shift passes over a locked cell" means for any edit. Two edits are the server's, so the page asks for them: Exclude from grid sends `keepCell` to `/api/char-props` when a locked cell follows, and the server leaves an unused cell where the character stood (only when a cell really emptied); **Use this screenpack's slot layout** rearranges every cell and asks first when locks are on and cells are locked.

### Replace… and Insert… with a character already in the build

Both take the character from the picker (`pickCharacter`), and it is the only place they can say anything: the log sits under the picker's backdrop, so a refusal written only there read as a pick that did nothing. `onPick` answers a reason when it refuses and the picker stays open with it above its buttons; `lockRefuses` and `onDrop` answer their reasons (a truthy string) for that. A row for a character in the build names where he is (`buildPlaces`: *cell N*, *cells N, M* for one in the build twice, or *off the grid* for `exclude = 1` and for a cell past the grid's last). Typing highlights the first match; Enter picks the highlighted row, or the only match; Up and Down move the highlight; Escape closes.

- **Replace X with Y, Y alone in a cell on the grid and X's cell not a slot** (a slot being a cell of more than one member, as the cell menu counts it): a swap, `onDrop('cell:' + Y's cell, X's cell, false, {mode: 'swap'})`, identical to that drag in swap mode whatever the preference.
- **Otherwise** (Y in a shared slot, off the grid, or X's cell a slot): Y is lifted out (`liftFromBuild`) and takes X's whole cell; X, and a slot's other members, go back to the library, as Replace always did with a library character.
- **Insert Y into an empty cell** is a library drop whose mover is lifted: `onDrop('lib:' + id, i, false, {lift: true})`. Never a `cell:` drop, which closes the gap it leaves when the target is past the end of the list, and hands the target's empty kind to the cell left behind.
- **Lifting renumbers nothing**: a cell Y had alone becomes a dummy, a shared slot keeps its other members, and an off-grid Y leaves `offGrid` with `exclude` cleared (`takeFromLibrary`).
- **Locks** (Lock cells on) refuse when any cell whose content would change is locked: X's, or Y's own cell or slot. An off-grid Y has no cell, and brings his lock along.
- Each is one `Session.record` step.
- **A character can be in the build twice** (a cell of his own and a slot's member, or two cells), so `buildPlaces` keeps EVERY place per id, in list order; `whereInBuild` is the first, which is where Insert and Replace take him from, and the picker row names every cell. `replaceWith` asks X's own cell first: Y alone in it is refused (*already in cell i*), Y a member of its slot is the member who stays (`liftFromBuild(id, place)`). Going by the first place alone, Replace on the second copy's cell pulled the first copy out of its slot and dropped this cell's own without a word, or swapped the two copies, a step that changed nothing.
- **Insert onto reserved ground.** `onDrop` slides a target the pack reserves to the next usable cell (`firstUsableCell`) before anything else. With `lift`, a slid target that holds Y (his cell, or a slot he is in) is refused before the lift: lifting him first left the destination entry out of `order`, and the mover went onto the end of the list with no log line and no step. A slid target that holds someone else gets what the drag of Y's cell gets: `liftFromBuild` answers the dummy it left (`hole`, null when shared, off the grid or past the grid's last cell), and in swap mode the victim takes it, where `vacated` (only a `cell:` drag sets it) would have left him to `parkEntry`; in move mode that dummy is already where the drag's move branch puts one back. No path of `onDrop` may change `order` without a log line and a `Session.record`.
- **The picker's keys are read at the document** (capture) while it is open, not on its box: the focus leaves the search box more easily than it looks (the Browse… dialog closing hands it to the page, a click on the title), and Escape then did nothing. The Browse… dialog on top, and any E-Select dialog opened over the picker, keep their own keys; a focused picker button keeps its Enter and Space; a printable key with the focus elsewhere focuses the search box first, so the text lands there. `modal`'s `onShut` gives the search box its focus back, and a press in the box (not its buttons, the search box or the list's scroll bar) keeps it there. A picker taken out of the page without `shut` stops listening on its next key.
- **Browse…'s failures are refusals too**: an error from `/api/add-local`, or a request that never answers, goes into the picker's reason line as well as the log.

### Undo is snapshots, not inverses

Every edit already goes through `Session.record`, and that is where a step is taken. A state holds the page's cell order and off-grid list (deep copies), whether they were saved, and the two files an edit can write: `roster.json` as text, and the screenpack's `system.def` text. A staged edit (only the order moved) shares the previous state's files. An immediate edit has written and called `load(true)` in the same task as its record, so its files are read only after that reload settles; read earlier, the step would hold the page from before the edit. Records made in one task are one step, committed on the next task through a `MessageChannel`, not `setTimeout(0)`, because a window that is not in front has its timers held back a second or more. 100 steps.

Going back writes `roster.json` first and the screenpack text second, each only when it differs, because the roster names which pack file the text belongs to. The page then reloads and takes the state's own order, which may hold staged edits the files never had, so undoing an immediate edit also brings back the staged edits its reload discarded. The Revert journal gives back or takes back the step's labels, so `Revert (n)` stays true. Undo and Redo refuse while any load, save, reload, revert or step is in flight.
