**The fit (`widefit.js`, the Widescreen fit button on a stage card) widens `localcoord` at the same height** to floor(height x aspect) - a hair under, never over: 426 leaves the stage a hair taller than the screen, which the engine trims from the bottom within `cutlow`; 427 would leave it shorter, which the engine answers by shifting the stage down and showing a hairline of void along the top. `boundleft`/`boundright` are pulled in by the extra half-width divided by `zoomout` (rounded up: the engine reads the bounds as int32; `autozoom` drops zoomout, see below), clamped at 0, so the camera zoomed all the way out reaches no further past the old frame than before the fit; at zoom 1 it scrolls a little less far than it used to (the owner's call, 2026-11-23); how far a stage fell short of that is reported as possible void at the sides, and only the game says whether the picture actually stops there. **The select-screen picture scales with the coordinate space** - the engine draws a stage's 9000,1 at `portraitscale x motif width / stage width` - so widening 320 to 426 alone shrinks the thumbnail to 75% of its window (seen in the game). The fit raises `[StageInfo] portraitscale` by the same factor and undo restores it; a marker from before that was recorded leaves the key alone. Stages already the build's shape or wider are left alone, and so is every stage when the build itself is 4:3. The old values ride on a marker line under `[StageInfo]`, so undo restores the file byte for byte; nothing else in the def is touched. Test: `tools/test-widefit.js`.

**The void estimate counts `zoomout`.** The screen's edge reaches `bound + localcoord.w / (2 * zoomout)` stage units from center (`camera.go` Reset: `maxRight = boundright * localscl + halfWidth / zoomout`, `minLeft` mirrors it; `autozoom` uses `halfWidth`, so zoomout drops out), the same reach `widefit3d.js` uses. Widening by `2 * pull` grows that reach by `pull / zoomout` per side, and the bounds pull in by that much (`boundPull`) where they can, so void is left only where a bound hits 0: the reported void is `pull / zoomout + boundleft - newBoundleft` (right mirrored), one decimal. TouhouCasino (320x240, bounds -29/29, zoomout 0.6): its bounds already hit 0, so 24 at zoom 1, 59.3 zoomed all the way out. A stage scrolling 150 at zoomout 0.6: bounds -61/61 (pull 89), no void; under the old pull of 53 it was -97/97 with 35.3. A stage fitted before 2026-11-23 keeps the bounds it got; Undo and fit again to take the new ones. Still measured against the old frame, not the art: a stage whose sprites run past it shows less.

**The Stages tab asks once per draw** (2026-10-12, §3.1 *Caches*). `GET /api/stage-widefit?all=1` answers `{ results: { <file>: what ?file= answers, or null where it answers an error } }` over the roster's stages from one roster read, and each card takes its line from it; a stage the answer does not name, or a batch that fails, falls back to the one-stage GET. The page asks only when there are stages and the build is not read-only. `widefit.status` keeps each answer per `.def` path under the file's size + `mtimeMs` + `ctimeMs` and the build's aspect (the ctime catches a same-size edit whose time was put back), stored as its JSON so no caller can change the kept copy; a fit or an undo drops its own entry; 4,096 entries, then cleared. The plan reads only the `.def` and the aspect, so nothing else is in the key. Test: `tools/test-page-speed.js`.

### Span: camera scale as a single number

**Span — how many screens wide the picture is.** Span 1 shows all of it with the camera pinned (the generator's original, single-screen behavior). Span 2 shows half, the camera scrolls across the rest, and fighters appear twice the size on screen. The arithmetic lives in `public/ikemen/stage-geom.js`, shared by `stagegen.js` (writes the `.def`) and the placement dialog (draws the preview), so the viewport rectangle shown and the bounds the engine gets are computed by the same code and cannot disagree.

Rules taken directly from engine source:

- **The stage is fitted to the screen by WIDTH alone** (`stage.go:1573`, `localscl = gameWidth / localcoord[0]`), so one screen of picture is `w/span` wide and `w/span * gameH/gameW` tall — the GAME's aspect, regardless of what `localcoord[1]` claims. The aspect comes from `Video.GameWidth/GameHeight` on the roster (a user setting, `settings-schema.js:112`), defaulting to 854x480.
- **A span has a floor.** Below `w*aspect/h`, one screen's height would poke past the picture into the void, so the slider is clamped there: e.g. a 1600x500 panorama on 16:9 starts at 1.80, not 1.
- **The floor row always lands on `zoffset`.** `zoffset` is placed at the stock 200-of-240 of the view, clamped so the picture covers the view at rest, and `start.y = zoffset - floorY` lifts the picture to match. At span 1 on a matching aspect this collapses to `start.y = 0, zoffset = floorY` — the original, single-screen behavior, unchanged.
- **Bounds are the off-screen picture, less what zoom needs, less one pixel in hand.** Horizontal: how far the picture reaches past the view on its SHORTER side (an odd width reaches one pixel less on the right), minus the zoom term below, minus 1. Vertical: from the pulled-back view's top to the picture's top, and its bottom to the picture's bottom (see the vertical-axis section). All four are 0 at span 1.
- **Zoom-out and the bounds share one budget, and the engine spends part of it on its own.** `camera.go:120-121`: whenever `zoomout != 1` and the stage does not declare `autozoom`, the engine widens `boundleft`/`boundright` by `(1-z)/z * gameWidth/2` screen px on each side (a full half screen at z=0.5). Real stages survive this because authors set bounds well inside their art; a generated stage must write its bounds pulled IN by that same term, so the engine's own widening lands the pulled-back camera exactly on the picture's edge. In stage units the term is `(1-z)/(2z) * V` — `gameWidth` cancels, so it holds at any resolution. At `z = 1/span` it would eat the whole slack (the stage wouldn't scroll at all at normal zoom), so zoom-out is allowed at most HALF the slack (`z >= 2/(span+1)`), leaving the rest for ordinary scrolling. There is no vertical widening in this branch (`ExtraBoundH` runs only under autozoom, `camera.go:175`), and no vertical compensation of any kind (see the vertical-axis section). `zoomin` stays 1.

### Rounding correction (integer axis, localcoord, zoomout)

The `.def` cannot carry exact arithmetic — it carries integers and three-decimal values, and rounding in the wrong direction can leave a hairline of void along one edge of the view (seen on an odd-width picture at span > 1). The rule: **compute from what the `.def` will actually carry, not from the ideal value.** This governs five things in `stage-geom.js`:

1. Extents come from the axis, `-axisX .. w - axisX`, and the SHORTER side governs both bounds. The picture is at most one pixel off-center, so this costs at most one pixel of travel.
2. The view width is `floor(w/span)`, never `round` — a floored view is never wider than the one `minSpan` proved fits, and never more than `2 * min(extL, extR)`. At span 1 an odd-width picture gets a view one pixel narrower than itself, with the spare column hidden on the left.
3. `zoomout` is rounded UP to three decimals.
4. `start.y` is rounded to the nearest integer, then held inside `[viewH - h, 0]` — the range in which the picture covers the view at rest. (A 720-row picture at span 1 fits a 719.44-row view with `start.y` -0.56; rounding that to -1 would leave 0.44 rows of void along the bottom.)
5. The slack is floored, and one pixel is kept in hand for whatever the draw itself rounds.

Example (127x131 picture, ground at row 102, span 1.25), before and after applying the fix — `.sff` untouched, only the `.def` changed:

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| localcoord | 102, 57 | 101, 57 |
| boundleft / boundright | -4 / 4 | -5 / 5 |
| boundhigh | -53 | -47, plus `boundhighzoomdelta = 1` (see below) |
| boundlow | 18 | 18 |
| zoomout | 0.889 | 0.889 |
| cuthigh / cutlow | absent | 0 / 78 (see below) |

Pulled all the way back, the view now spans x -61.8..61.8 against a picture at -64..63: inside on both sides with a pixel to spare, where before it was inside on the left and 0.3 past the edge on the right.

### The vertical axis

**Zoom anchors on the ground row, not on the view.** `stage.go:623` shifts a stage BG by `zoffset * (1/scl - 1)` before scaling it by `scl`, so as the camera pulls back, the ground row stays where it was on screen and the view grows both ways from it: `zoffset/scl` rows above the ground, `(viewH - zoffset)/scl` below. The picture has `floorY` rows above its ground and `h - floorY` below. So zoom-out has a floor on EACH side of the ground — `zoffset/floorY` and `(viewH - zoffset)/(h - floorY)` — and a single combined ratio (`Vh/h`) is too loose whenever the ground sits at a different proportion of the picture than of the view. Example: a 2000x600 panorama with its ground at row 520 has 80 rows below the ground; at span 2 the view needs 79 of them at rest, leaving no room to pull back at all — writing `zoomout = 0.937` there would show four rows of void along the bottom whenever the fighters spread out. The corrected value is 1; at span 3 it is 0.79, not 0.625. A picture with little room below its ground barely zooms — that is a property of the picture, not a bug, and the dialog's readout reports how far it can pull back.

**The camera's y is clamped to `[boundhigh, boundlow]` at ANY zoom** (`camera.go:604`), unlike x, which `XBound` widens by the zoom. So `boundhigh` must be written for the pulled-back view — `zoffset/zoomout - floorY`, plus the pixel in hand — or a high jump while the fighters are far apart shows void along the top. On its own that costs ordinary jumps their travel at zoom 1 (in the example above, -53 became -47). The fix is `boundhighzoomdelta = 1` (`camera.go:599-602`, read for any stage, not only autozoom ones), which lets the camera rise a further `zoffset * (1/scl - 1/zoomout)` at any tighter zoom — keeping the view's top on the same picture row at every scale, so at zoom 1 the camera reaches -53 again. `boundlow` has no such delta and is pulled in for good, since nothing drives the camera down anyway.

**The aspect correction must come out zero.** `camera.go:131-146` compares the stage's `localcoord` height, scaled, against the screen. If shorter, the engine shifts the whole stage DOWN to overdraw the bottom — void along the top. If taller, it "cuts" the surplus from the bottom (off screen anyway, no shift) as long as `cutlow` allows it. So `localcoord[1]` is CEILED, and the `.def` carries `cuthigh = 0` and a `cutlow` that always allows the cut. Catch: the engine compares a surplus in SCREEN pixels against `cutlow` in stage units, and the surplus is under one stage pixel — up to `gameWidth / localcoord[0]` screen pixels — so `cutlow` is set to the stage height or `7680 / localcoord[0] + 1`, whichever is larger, which holds up to an 8K screen. Nothing else reads it.

**Verification: `tools/test-stage-geom.js`.** 468 combinations: thirteen picture shapes (16:9, 4:3, HD, square, panorama, tall, plus odd-width/tiny ones — 127x131, 251x199, 97x60), three ground rows, six spans, both game aspects. The checker transcribes the engine rather than restating the arithmetic: the bound-widening term in the exact form of `camera.go:120-121`, then `XBound` at zoom 1 and at the written `zoomout`, at two game widths; vertically, the ground-anchored view at both zooms with the effective `boundhigh` that `boundhighzoomdelta` gives, checked at the top, at rest, and at the bottom of the bound box; and the aspect-correction branch. Every edge is tested strictly (tolerance of a millionth of a stage pixel, for float noise only — the rounding bug above was a third of a stage pixel) against the picture's TRUE extents from its integer axis. Result: 468/468, and span 1 on a matching picture still matches the original single-screen behavior to the integer.

Example — 2000x600 image, ground at row 520, 16:9 — generated at spans 1/2/3:

| span | localcoord | zoffset | start | bounds L/R | bounds H/L | zoomout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (floor 1.87) | 1067, 600 | 520 | 0, 0 | ±465 | 0 / 0 | 1 |
| 2 | 1000, 563 | 483 | 0, -37 | ±499 | -36 / 0 | 1 |
| 3 | 666, 375 | 312 | 0, -208 | ±577 | -124 / 0 | 0.79 |

312 + 208 = 520, the placed floor, at every span.

The placement dialog draws both fighters (p2 mirrored) at the size the span makes them, plus a dashed one-screen rectangle over the picture (hidden at span 1, where it would just outline the whole image). Fighters visibly shrink as span grows, because they are smaller against the whole picture once it becomes more than one screen.

End-to-end flow: dropping an image opens the placement dialog; dragging the line moves the ground and the fighter reference follows; Create writes both files and installs them; the roster picks up the new stage; `removeStage` cleans it out.

## 3.10 A move's numbers: the Moves window

**Where.** Desktop Studio, a character's details, **Moves…**. One window per character, printed as the booklet's command-list page (`public/moves.html`; 2026-10-18). A switch in its band chooses the printing: **Edit off** (the default) is the printed command list; **Edit on** (or `?edit=1`; the switch rewrites the address with `history.replaceState` so a reload keeps it) is the editing UI below. Both are drawn from the same `/api/char-moves` read and every part is always built (edit parts `.ed`, print parts `.pr`, hidden with `display: none` so a hidden input is never focusable), so the suites' DOM stand-in sees the same structure in both; every number is the server's (`framedata.js`) and the page never counts a frame itself. The Lite Studio does not have it.

- **Edit off.** Left page: one row per attack state - its name and input when the Command List reader names it (`/api/movelist`, grouped specials / supers / others, then the attack states it does not name), else the attack description framedata gives (`Standing special attack`); state, startup, active, recovery, total, on hit, on block and damage, all from the row's shown block (the first block that can hit, else the first). The row's first child stays the state number (code and suites read it there; CSS places it in the third column). Right page: the opened move (state, block, file and line, the name with its large input and where the name came from), the training readout and frame meter, the action frame by frame on one ground line with the frame bar under each element (one cell per tick, colored from the block's own meter) and the first active element underlined, a 2x plate of the element on screen at the startup frame with its boxes and hit values, and the game's Command List; the band's mascot (`#bandMascot`) stands in the band when the Studio opened the window and deals the window's tips as a slip over the page (WB's hint box at the foot went in the owner's second review, 2026-10-18).
- **Edit on.** The same list with each damage's tier mark (green / amber / red) and the state's own line under each row, and on the right the editable readout (hitstun, blockstun, hitstop, damage, chip), "Edit timing…", the Edited strip with Revert, the block picker, its triggers and every value in its tier. Nothing an edit does changed (the rest of this section).
- **Cancels and distance (2026-10-18, the owner's second review: "Far and close heavy punch on the same button means it's a proximity normal" / "Are you familiar with super/special cancellable moves? ... It should be noted on a movelist").** The list's Hit cell prints a stamp per kind of cancel the move allows ON HIT, before the number: **SP** (into a special, 1000-2999), **SU** (into a super, 3000-4999), **CH** (a chain: normal 200-999 into normal); the stamp's title lists the moves (name and state, ≈ per move). A dashed stamp is approximate (below). The Command cell prints **close** / **far** after the input for one button's two moves, its title the distance and trigger. The opened move says "Close version: within 25 of the opponent (P2BodyDist X <= 25). Farther out, the same button is state 220" under the input, and after the frame data a **Cancels** side head: one row per kind with the moves, "on hit" / "on block" when only one applies, ≈, and where it was read (the -1 blocks' file:line, the variables). A state nothing cancels says its frame advantage is the whole story. The Hit column is 100px (74px under 1180px wide) to hold the stamps, and the name and Command columns share what is left 1fr / 1.1fr, so at 1400 wide the longest input on Main (a MAX super's charge + X + Y, 179px) prints whole in 181px; at 1.5fr / 1.4fr it lost its last chip (measured on KFM, Sakura, Balrog, Guile and CVS Makoto). Narrower windows cut long inputs, as before this round. Data: GET /api/movelist `cancels` and `inputs[].range` (§3.10e). Not in the Lite Studio (no Moves window there).

**Projectiles (2026-10-19, the owner: "Projectile based characters have odd movelist illustrations, they have framedata, why can't they have specialized entries for projectile moves? ... others are missing when the method of drawing that projectile is different than you're used to. Look at WinMUGEN's case: shake.def").** A **PROJECTILES** section closes the command list: one row per thing a move throws, in the list's own columns - its name (the throwing move's), command, the throwing state, **Out** (the frame of the throw it appears on), **Act.** (frames its hit box is out while it flies; `→` out until it hits or leaves the screen; `?` its motion depends on the game, or its hit box is UNKNOWN - never 0 - because its animation is not read: a formula with no candidate, the common effects, or an action the .air lacks, whose engine fallback is a copy of what the thrower is playing, char.go 7631-7640), **Hits** (`projhits`; `—` for a helper), **Life** (frames before it ends on its own; `∞` never), **PB hit / PB blk** (point blank, below) and damage. Three ways of making one are read (movelib THE PROJECTILES; census of 221 characters: P 116, H 167, E 10):
- **A Projectile controller** (Shake, RyuDX, Ken): its `projanim` (0 when absent; `F` = the common effects, not drawn; an expression gives candidates and "depends on"), `projhitanim` / `projremanim` / `projcancelanim` with the engine's fallbacks (hitanim -1 = gone on contact; an unset remanim copies hitanim, an unset cancelanim copies remanim, bytecode.go 8334-8345), its scale (drawn at `projscale`, times [Size] only with `size.proj.doscale`; **its boxes at [Size], not at projscale**, unless `projclsnscale`, char.go 7648-7657), where it appears (`offset` + `postype`, helperPos char.go 6978-7035; `pos` on a Projectile is an Explod's name and is ignored), and its path.
- **A helper whose own states hold the HitDef and move it** (the CvS Hadouken, Sakura, Marvin). Its hit is the first HitDef that CAN hit: Capcom vs SNK helpers open with a "Miss" HitDef (`trigger1 = 1`, `hitFlag =` empty, no damage) before the real one, and an empty hitflag is 0 to the engine (stored as "" by the controller parser, compiler.go 6015; `parseHitFlag`, compiler_functions.go 1678-1703), which the hit test refuses for a standing, crouching, airborne and lying target (char.go 10797-10800). `framedata.neverHits` names such a HitDef (no H, L, M, A or D in its hitflag): it gets no startup, no active frames on its meter and a note, so neither the entry, the helper's walk (`armOf`) nor a state's row (`shownBlock`) reads it - before 2026-10-20 every CvS fireball read damage 0, chip 0, Unblockable: the family is the literal targets of the Helper controllers' `stateno` and the states they reach by literal ChangeState / SelfState (8 deep, 40 states, the basic states 0-199 / 5000-5999 not followed). Listed when one of its states holds a HitDef, it moves (a velset, VelSet, VelAdd or PosAdd with a nonzero x) and it is not bound to the body (BindToRoot / Parent / Target = a hit box riding the character). Its entry links every state that makes it ("Thrown by"), and its hit state leaves **Other attack states** (its own row read it as if the helper were the player) wherever the entry COUNTS the hit: in the helper's first state, or in a later state the walk below reaches at a frame the files settle (Chowder's Panini 3402 -> 3403 -> 3405, Chowder 6201 -> 6208, the fixture 2691 -> 2692). A hit the walk does not reach at a settled frame (a ChangeState behind a variable, or one its own numbers never meet: Shake's helper 1160 flies level at y -65 and changes to 1190 only on `Pos Y >= 0`; Marvin 2457 reaches 3064 on its first frame, but its motion there depends on `P2BodyDist X < 4`) keeps its own row, and the entry shows Act. / Life / PB as `?` / `—` with the reason and a link to that row. A Command List line that names the helper's state keeps it in that group. **A helper is drawn at its own size**: it starts at its maker's [Size] and the Helper controller's `size.xscale` / `size.yscale` replace it (newHelper char.go 6923, Helper.Run bytecode.go 5642-5645, cueDraw 13038-13041; Marvin's helper 221 is drawn at .1 x .07); its boxes stay at the animation owner's [Size] unless `ownclsnscale = 1` (updateClsnScale 7854-7866). Edit on: "Edit its values in state N" opens the block where it lives.
- **A blank helper drawn by an Explod** (Krillin, Goku's ball, CvS Jill, MK2 Liu Kang): when every frame of the helper's animation has sprite group -1, the Explod in the helper's own states (else the one in the throwing state that fires with the Helper, else its first drawn one) is shown as the look, "drawn by an Explod" - matched by state, not by ID - with the blank helper's boxes on its frames. Not listed: a helper that never moves (pillars, traps), one bound to the body, a blank helper with no Explod, a root HitDef with a long Clsn1 drawn by an Explod (E-root), `helpertype = projectile` (a no-op in Ikemen, char.go 3331).

**Its path** (framedata `projectilePath`, Projectile.update char.go 2576-2707, tick 2825-2878): t = 0 is the tick it appears; each tick the removal check on the position the previous tick left (removetime 0; `removetime <= -2` once its animation has played; moving down below `heightbound[1]` or up above `heightbound[0]`), then pos += velocity, then velocity += accel, *= velmul; a negative x velocity turns the sprite around without changing the motion. `projremovetime = N` is N ticks of life. Collision tests the element its animation shows on that tick (the animation advances later, in cueDraw). Simulated 300 ticks at most; points past a full screen plus `edgebound` are not drawn (the engine removes a projectile there). Screen and stage bounds need the camera and are given as "off screen after N frames thrown from the middle of a still screen / corner to corner". **A helper is followed through its states** (framedata `helperChain`, movelib `projectilesIn` `chainState` / `animOf` / `armOf`): tick by tick from the state its Helper controller names, across every ChangeState / SelfState the files settle, until it destroys itself, lands (physics A with vel y > 0 at or below the ground: the engine sends it to state 52, char.go 12167-12173), changes to a state that is not followed (a ChangeState TARGET that is a common state 0-199 / 5000-5999, a .zss state, one not in its files - its FIRST state is always walked from its own definition, whatever its number: Reflector's helper is made straight into its own state 197), or a cap of **600 frames / 12 states** (said in a note). **Every helper entry is walked this way, a single-state one too** (the old single-state walk, `helperPath`, now draws only the Explods' own motion): its cap is 600 frames (the single-state walk stopped at 300, `PATH_CAP`), its HitDef arms where its own trigger fires tick by tick (`Time > 1` = its third frame; the frame-data startup only when the trigger is not settled), PosSet y is read instead of stopping the walk, and a Turn / HitDef / Pause / ChangeAnim on a trigger it cannot settle is listed and passed instead of stopping it. Each frame: its state code, then pos += vel along its facing, then S friction (a speed under 1 stops) / C friction / A gravity (posUpdate char.go 9928-9990), then time++; a helper runs its first frame on the frame it is made (char.go 13531-13535). **A ChangeState takes effect at once**: time 0 (stateChange1 char.go 6588-6597), the new statedef's physics, velset and anim (StateBytecode.init bytecode.go 15537-15565, stateDef.Run 4891-4935; no `physics` = N, bytecode.go 15530 / compiler.go 6609-6628; no `velset` keeps the velocity; no `anim` keeps the animation and its clock), and the NEW state's code runs in the same frame (changeStateEx char.go 6773-6781); the old state's later controllers do not run (changeState.Run bytecode.go 5196-5219). Its HitDef does not carry over (hitdefpersist 0 by default, compiler.go 6652-6659). Triggers it settles: `time`, `AnimTime` (curtime - totaltime), `AnimElemTime(N)` and `AnimElem = N` (= AnimElemTime(N) = 0) on the state's animation clock (anim.go 503-520, 802-846: past totaltime the clock runs the loop again), its own `Pos Y` / `Vel X` / `Vel Y`, contact triggers as 0 (it has touched nothing in flight). Motion: VelSet / VelAdd / VelMul / PosAdd (bytecode.go 5822-5930), Gravity adds the character's yaccel to vel y on each frame it fires, in any physics (bytecode.go 11404-11418, char.go 9834-9836: Leona's earring bomb bounces 1620 -> 1625 -> 1626 -> 1640 and explodes on frame 91), PosSet y from the ground (PosSet x is on the camera, so the path depends there, 5786-5816), Turn flips its facing and so its motion (9665-9675), ChangeAnim with a number restarts the animation. Its hit counts where its HitDef has FIRED in the current state (its triggers settle the frame; one they cannot settle falls back to the state's frame-data startup, marked ≈) and its animation shows a Clsn1 there. **Pause / SuperPause it calls** (bytecode.go 10420-10520, setPauseTime char.go 9182-9220): the pause starts on the next frame (system.go 2964-2983) and lasts `time` frames, during which everyone without movetime stands frozen - the player and the opponent (actionPrepare char.go 11857-11866); the helper moves for its `movetime` of them (a movetime above the time is 0) and is frozen for the rest, where its path holds still. **Branches the files do not settle** (Win / LoseKO / RoundState, a variable, random, the opponent's or the screen's distance) are LISTED ("May end sooner", the path key's "not followed"), never followed; a motion controller that reads one stops the walk ("depends on ..."). **Active, Life and point blank come from where the hit really is**: point blank is still the PLAYER's advantage on the player's frames - the helper's frame c is the maker's frame F + c, less every frame its own Pause froze the player before contact; a first hit while that pause still freezes both players is left out with the reason (Panini: her first hit on frame 399 is the last frame of her 368-frame Pause); a pause in the move that makes it (a SuperPause, supermovetime) is not counted, so a chain's PB is ≈ then.

**A followed helper on the page** (`public/moves.html` `renderChainFrames`, `chainWords`, `chainEnd`, `pjCells`; `renderProjPath`, `renderProjData`): ITS FRAMES are grouped by state - a numbered heading per state (its frames of the helper's life, what it does there from its own motion: "falls 300 to the ground · moves forward 2 a frame", "holds still · Pause: the others stand frozen 368 frames, it moves on", "moves forward 15 a frame", its HitDef with file:line, how it leaves: "→ state 3403 when (Pos Y >= 0) && (Vel Y > 0)") over that state's strip. **One frame and scale for every state** (the union of all states' sprites and boxes, the 320-wide screen x a whole number), so the ground line never jumps; with Edit off every column is at least that frame's width, so no sprite or box draws into its neighbor (measured: 0 rects outside their cell for Panini, Chowder 6201, Marvin 3051 / 2457, Sakura 1475 at 1400x900 and 1024x700, day and night) and a long state (Panini's 37-element pose) scrolls inside its own strip. ITS PATH draws the whole walk with a numbered mark where it enters each state (marks that would cover one another move right; kept under the tag), and a key: each state's frames, the frames its pause freezes the others, the drawn-frames cut, the ChangeStates not followed. The readout's meter starts at the hitting state when that is past frame 150, with a dark edge where a state starts; Act. / Life read `N+` when the walk stops at its cap. A state heading reads an arc as an arc - "rises 24.7, then falls 67.2 to the ground" (Jill 7410), from the highest (or lowest) point of the walk's own frames in that state, never its net motion alone. **An Explod-drawn helper followed into later states** (tomokaminato 2216 -> 2210, Leona 1620 -> 1625 -> 1626 -> 1640) keeps the Explod's frames, the look the game shows (the aside names its states: "the helper goes on through states 2216 → 2210 (its path)"; the first-hit element is marked there only when that hit is in its first state), while its Act. / Life, meter, path tag, state marks and key are the walk's, as for a helper (tomokaminato 2216: Act. 23+, Life 600+, "still going at frame 600" - never the single-state "→ / ∞ / flies on"). A helper that never leaves its first state, a Projectile, and an Explod-drawn helper that never leaves its first state draw their frames and their path plate with the same code as before (a helper's path is as long as the walk above: up to 600 frames, not 300); a helper's NUMBERS (Act., Life, first hit, PB) come from that walk, so some single-state entries read differently from before (the cap, the HitDef's own trigger, PosSet y: DEVLOG "fix round").

**Point blank (PB)**: the advantage if it connects on the first frame it can, right in front of the thrower - its hitpause freezes the projectile, not the thrower (char.go 13958-13967), so the thrower's own hitstop is 0: on hit = hitstun + 2 + the opponent's hitstop - the thrower's frames after contact, on block = blockstun + 1 + the opponent's blockstop - the same; contact = the frame it appears + its first tick with a hit box (a helper: + its own startup - 1). Later contact leaves the thrower further ahead. **Point blank is the PLAYER's advantage**: a projectile thrown from a HELPER's state (or a helper made by one) is counted on the frames of the player's move that makes that helper - the helper runs its tick 0 on the frame it is made, so its frame k is the move's frame F + k - 1 (pjedge 2800 / 2801: appears on frame 4 + 6 - 1 = 9, PB +12 / +6, not the helper's own +23 / +17). When the helper reaches the throwing state by a ChangeState, or is made by another helper, PB is left out and the entry says why (Grim Reaper Mai: 146 entries). Each unknown PB carries its reason in words (`pointBlank.why`). A throwing move's own row and readout show its projectile's Active, recovery after it appears, and PB on hit / on block with a **PB** stamp where its own are unknown; the opened move lists "Throws" (six links at most, the rest counted). A WinMUGEN character's projectile freezes one frame less on contact (mugenversion other than 1.0 / 1.1, ParseMugenVersion common.go 878-896). **Never guessed**: any of these written as a formula is listed under "Depends on the game" with its text and the number it decides is left out (a hit value keeps the window's fresh-first-hit reading, ≈ with its formula). A division of two literals is folded the engine's way (BytecodeExp.div, bytecode.go 1434-1449): two whole numbers divide as whole numbers toward zero (`10/3` = 3), a decimal on either side as decimals, by zero is undefined (left out); any other division is left out. Time budget 2.5 s and 400 entries per character, with a note past either (Grim Reaper Mai: 310 entries in 336 ms of a 4.98 MB read).

Tests: `tools/test-projectiles.js` (KFM copy with a Projectile, a flying helper, an Explod-drawn helper, a bound helper and a still blank helper as negative controls checked beside their positives, a formula velocity, a helper with its own size, a Projectile thrown by a helper, an animation missing from the .air, a hit in a later state, `10/3`; the page on a stand-in document; 450 controllers capped at 400; a missing KFM copy FAILS; the chain (2720: a fall until Pos Y >= 0 && Vel Y > 0, a pose with Pause time 6 movetime 6 ending on AnimTime = 0, a dash with the only HitDef and a Win branch: states, ticks, path, the hit only where its HitDef fires, the helper moving through its own pause, PB 3 + 27 - 6 = frame 24, +13 / +10 ≈, the page's state headings, one frame for every strip and the path's marks and key), a hit after a settled ChangeState now counted (2690: +7 / +4) and its control behind var(3) (2697 keeps its row), a framedata-only Pause with movetime 2 of 5 and a framedata-only Gravity (y -2.5, -4.5, -6, -7 from vel y -3, yaccel .5), an Explod-drawn helper followed into a still state with no HitDef (2730: row 10+ / 600+, the Explod's strip, "still going at frame 600", 2 state marks and their key), a helper made into its own state 197 (2740: active 20, life 20, as before), a HitDef on `Time > 1` (2750: first hit on tick 2, PB +5 / +2) and an arc (2760: "rises 14, then falls 5")).

**Explod art (2026-10-19, the owner: "A root hit with Explod art. Shouldn't those include the art too? They explain the hitboxes. They should render behind the hit box.")** Shake's lawnmower (state 1213) is the case: the root's long Clsn1 (297..321 at [Size] .5) belongs to an Explod (action 1214, scale .5, pos 32,-58, bindtime 80, vel 3, ontop 1, AnimElem = 5), and the window used to draw the box over empty air. Every Explod an attack state's OWN code spawns is now read (movelib THE EXPLODS, `explodsIn`) and drawn in the opened move's frame-by-frame strip (on each element's first tick) and on the first-active plate, **always under the Clsn1 / Clsn2 boxes**, and layered against the character the way the engine layers them. A legend item **Explod art** switches them off and on (on by default; remembered per viewer in `localStorage` `studio.moves.explodArt`; a keyboard user's focus stays on the switch); the frame data card lists every Explod of the state in words (its animation, the frame it appears on, how long it is bound - "bound for its whole life" when it is removed before its bindtime runs out, as Shake's lawnmower is at age 80, so its own vel never applies -, its own motion and place in the character's game units, its scale, its layer and why) and, for one that is not drawn, why not. An Explod-drawn projectile entry (THE PROJECTILES) draws its own look with the same code (`spriteAt`, the Explod's facing), and the switch does not hide it: that look is the entry's subject, as on master.
- **Framing (the owner, 2026-10-19: "the sprite timeline we have set up for the move list might get messy with this change"; with the switch OFF the strip must look exactly as it did, and with it ON no cell may draw into its neighbor).** The strip's fit is the move's own (`measure`): the art never joins it, so every cell keeps the body's scale and ground line with the switch on or off, and switch-off is master's strip node for node. Each cell's art sits in its own clip layer (`.xcl`, overflow hidden, a child of the cell's stage; its inner `.xin` is placed exactly as the cell's `.stin`), so it is cut cleanly at the cell's edge - the Edit-off column, or the 170 px Edit-on cell - and the boxes go to a second `.stin` after the art drawn over the character, so they stay on top. **The plate is where the art shows whole under its boxes**: only while art is drawn there, the plate's fit takes the art in (four times the area at most) and uses the plate's real size (210 x 260 under the narrow-window rule `max-width 1100px / max-height 760px`, else 250 x 300), so Shake's lawnmower and its long Clsn1 / Clsn2 show whole at 1024 x 700 too; with no art drawn the plate is master's (master's own plate still fits 250 x 300 at 1024, which cuts Shake's long Clsn2 there - pre-existing, left as it was). Why this framing: the Edit-off strip packs its cells into narrow overlapping columns (13 elements in about 500 px), so a fit that took far art in shrank every body (Shake 133 -> 127 px tall, Divesim 16% smaller) and still bled across cells; cutting at the cell keeps the strip as legible as before, and the plate plus the Edit-on cells show the art under the boxes it explains.
- **Drawn only when the files settle all of it**: a literal animation the .air has (absent = action 0; `F` = the common effects, not read; a formula = "depends on <expr>", not drawn; an action the .air lacks = no Explod at all, commitExplod char.go 7114-7126); postype **p1** in stage space (p2 needs the opponent, front / back / left / right and `space = screen` need the camera, None is an absolute stage place - all listed, never drawn at a guessed place); literal pos, vel / velocity, accel, friction, scale, facing, vfacing, bindtime, removetime, animelem; a spawn tick its triggers settle (AnimElem / AnimElemTime / Time, movelib `firingOf` / `ticksOf`, per animation the state may play). A conditional trigger (MoveHit, a variable) lists it "when <text>". `random`, an angle, interpolation and `trans` are noted and drawn at their plain values; a ModifyExplod / RemoveExplod of the same state that reaches it (matchId char.go 1849-1851: no id = all) is noted, not applied; removeongethit is noted.
- **Defaults** (initFromChar char.go 1691-1736): bindtime 1 (1701), scale 1,1, removetime -2 (anim end), postype p1, facing 1, friction 1 (1723), the character's layer. **A MUGEN 1.1 or Ikemen character's postype is None** (explod.Run bytecode.go 6202-6205; an ikemenversion counts as 1.1, compiler.go 8151-8156): its Explods without a postype are an absolute stage place, not drawn. Parameters run in the compiler's order (explodSub compiler_functions.go 855-1064; StateControllerBase.add / run bytecode.go 4809-4835): `vel` wins over `velocity` (891-901); `sprpriority`, then `ontop` (true: layer 1 and sprpriority 0; false: layer 0, bytecode.go 6323-6331), then `layerno` (-1 / 0 / 1, 6314-6322).
- **Place, tick by tick** (the server's, `spawns[action][k].pts` = [its own element, x, y, bound], x and y in the character's units from the character's axis ON THAT TICK): setPos char.go 1767-1847 puts a p1 Explod on the character (pos along its facing, 1769-1771) during the state code; explodUpdate runs after the characters have moved (system.go 2995, 3007, 3049); Explod.update char.go 1941-2155: removed at the start of the update once time >= removetime (1956) or, for removetime <= -2, once its animation has played through; while bindtime != 0 it sits on the character's position of that frame + pos (1987-1998); then time++, bindtime-- when > 0 (2103-2106), newPos = pos + velocity along the facing it was made with (2115; its own `facing` parameter mirrors only the sprite), velocity = velocity * friction + accel, 0 under 0.1 with friction < 1 (2120-2126); its animation shows tick `age` (UpdateSprite 2069 before Action 2131). So **a bound Explod rides with the character** (x, y = pos), and once unbound it stays where it was (plus its own motion) **while the character moves on**: the character's own motion in the move is walked with framedata `helperPath` (its statedef velset - with none the view assumes the move starts at rest and says so - then its time-only VelSet / VelAdd / VelMul / PosAdd, constants such as `const(velocity.run.fwd.x)` read from its cns, contact triggers 0: the move whiffs; physics A without the landing, which would end the state). Where that walk stops ("depends on ..."), an unbound Explod's place is unknown and it is not drawn there. bindtime = 0 places it before the character's move of that frame (the state code runs before posUpdate, char.go 12170).
- **Size**: drawn at its scale x (320 / localcoord) (cueDraw char.go 2157-2330, 2228-2236) - NOT times the character's [Size], which scales the character's sprite and boxes; in the window's units (the character's sprite pixels) an Explod is drawn at scale / [Size] and placed at pos / [Size] (Shake: scale .5 at [Size] .5 = 1:1, pos 32,-58 = 64,-116).
- **Layers** (system.go 3869-3966: layer -1, layer 0 `under`, layer 0, layer 1; DrawList.draw anim.go 1341-1420: ascending sprpriority, and at equal sprpriority the newer sprite is drawn first, anim.go 1403 / 1412; the characters are queued before the Explods, system.go 2893-2909): **over** the character in layer 1 (ontop, layerno 1) or with a sprpriority above the character's (its statedef's, 0 when it sets none - said so; a SprPriority controller in the state is noted); **under** it in layer -1, with `under`, or at a lower or EQUAL sprpriority. Clsn boxes are drawn after every sprite.
- **Bounded**: 24 Explods per state, 600 per character, 1.5 s, 60,000 timeline points, 400 ticks of a move, 200 added animations - each cut is a note (`explodNotes`). Explod animations join the answer's `projAnims` once (an action an attack state already carries is not sent again). Grim Reaper Mai (static read): no Explod in an attack state, read in 390 ms, no change to her answer.
- Not drawn by design: Explods of negative states (-1 / -2 / -3 run every tick) and of states that are not attack states. In the Edit-off strip, far-reaching art is cut at its own column's edge (and the next cell's body may cover what is left, as it covers far-reaching boxes on master); the plate and the Edit-on cells show it under its boxes.

Tests: `tools/test-explod-art.js` (KFM copy at [Size] .5: a long root hit with a p1 Explod bound 10 then left behind by a moving character - x = 21 + age, worked by hand; a formula animation, a P2 Explod; ontop / sprpriority under / equal layering, boxes after all of them; bindtime 0; motion that depends; no postype in MUGEN 1.0 vs 1.1 as the control; an Explod removed before its bindtime runs out (bound for its whole life, vel never applies); KFM itself none; the page's strip, plate, switch and readout on a stand-in document, with THE OWNER'S STRIP RULES: switch off = the strip and plate a model without Explods gets, switch on = the same strip framing for art outside the frame (above the head), every art image in a clip layer of its own cell; 654 Explods capped). 33 checks; the pre-fix lane code (eeaa38a) fails 6 of them (the framing, clip and readout checks), master's code fails it outright.

**What counts as an attack.** Five controller types carry hit data: `HitDef`, `ReversalDef`, `Projectile`, `ModifyHitDef` and `ModifyReversalDef`. A state is listed when it holds one. The files scanned are the ones the engine loads (3.2b): `st`, `stN`, `cmd` and `stcommon` from the first `[Files]` section. A character's own `.zss` state files are named as not scanned, and negative statedefs are not listed as moves. A block is addressed by its file, its state and its place among that state's attack blocks. That address goes stale when a block is added above it, so every write also carries a hash of the file as it was read, and a changed file is refused rather than guessed at.

**There is no single "attack" to name.** A special is often several states and several blocks, chained by `ChangeState` and gated by variables. The window shows the blocks as the files hold them and never merges them into one move. A projectile is its own block: the state that throws it often has no hit box of its own, and the window says so.

**How the engine reads a state file**, where it differs from what the file seems to say:

- **A UTF-8 byte-order mark is stripped** from the `.def`, the constants file and every state file before reading. Without that, a `[Statedef]` on the first line of a file saved with a BOM is invisible, and a later copy of the same state looks like the live one.
- **A parameter's name ends at its first space or tab**, and the `=` that splits the line is the first one outside parentheses. `damage x = 99` sets `damage`, and a `damage = 23` below it is a duplicate the engine ignores. `trigger1 != x` reads as `trigger1 = x`. `trigger1!=x` names `trigger1!`, which is no trigger, and the line is dropped.
- **Names and controller types are lowercased with Go's Unicode rules**, so `İ` (U+0130) in a name reads as `i`.
- **Lines are trimmed the way Go trims**, so a full-width space before `[State` still starts a new controller.
- **`AnimElem = N` has loose syntax.** The engine skips tokens up to the first one ending in `=`, so `AnimElem >= N`, `AnimElem != N`, `AnimElem <= N`, `AnimElem := N`, `AnimElem > = N` and `AnimElem(0) = N` all compile as `AnimElem = N`. Element numbers below 1 or past the last element are never true.

**The frames and their boxes** follow the `.air` rules in 3.2c. Two more rules decide what the window draws:

- **Boxes sit on the character's axis.** The element's x/y offset moves the sprite only, so art moved with an offset no longer lines up with its boxes. `HH` mirrors the sprite and draws it at the negated offset (3.2d). The Studio's animation player and GIF export draw boxes the same way.
- **Box colors are the engine's debug colors.** Red is a HitDef's hit box and orange-red a ReversalDef's. A dark inactive red means the state's `movetype` is `I` or unset: a HitDef there looks like an attack and is not one. Blue is a hurt box.

**When a block fires.** `AnimElem = N` is true on the tick element N starts: the sum of the earlier elements' times, with negatives counting as 0. A time 0 element still takes a number. The window shows a tick only when the triggers pin one down; anything gated on a variable, a command or the opponent is marked conditional. The tick assumes the animation starts when the state is entered: a `ChangeAnim` later in the state shifts it, and those are listed beside the block rather than folded in. An element the engine never displays (3.2c) is badged, and so is the one it holds.

**The frame data readout.** Above the frames, each block reads like a training mode: **startup, active, recovery, total**, **on hit / on block**, a frame meter (startup printed open, active red, recovery solid ink, one cell per frame - three marks that stay apart in every printing), then hitstun, blockstun, hitstop, damage and chip, what it blocks as (Mid / Overhead / Low / Unblockable), what it hits, knockdown and juggle cost. The states list carries each state's startup and advantage down the side. The rules (`framedata.js`):

- **Frame 1 is the first frame of the move.** Startup is the first frame the block is armed AND the element the engine tests that tick carries a hit box (3.2c); active is the run of hit-box frames from there; a later hit box is named, not counted.
- **Total** is the tick the state's end trigger fires, plus one: `AnimTime = 0` fires on the tick after the animation's last, and the character acts the tick after the ChangeState - a 12-tick animation is 13 frames you cannot act. `Time = N` ends it at N. With no end trigger found, the animation's end is assumed and the readout says so. The animation counted is the statedef's own, else the one numbered like the state, else the first it can play.
- **On hit** = hitstun + 2 + (their hitstop - yours) - your frames after contact; **on block** = blockstun + 1 + (their blockstop - yours) - the same. One +1 on both is the opponent's hand-back frame (5.13): control comes back in its state code after the frame's commands were read, exactly as "total" counts on your side. The other +1 on hit is the frame the engine adds to a MUGEN-made opponent's hitstun (char.go:11315-11317); the guard branch has none. Knockdown shows KD instead. Calibrated against the engine with the training frame meter: KFM's standing light punch reads startup 4, active 4, recovery 6, total 13, +4 on hit, -3 on block in both. A formula-driven value is still an estimate (≈).
- **A formula is read as a fresh first hit**: every `var(n)` at 0 and every `fvar(n)` at 1 (the CvS template's damage and meter scaling sit at 1.0 until a combo scales them). A number that rests on that, or on an armed or end frame the file does not settle, is marked **≈** and the assumptions are listed.
- **Blockstun a HitDef leaves out** is derived the engine's way (from `ground.slidetime` in a MUGEN character, `ground.hittime` with `ikemenversion`), and so is blockstop (from `pausetime`).

**The game's Command List, on the Moves page.** The page shows what Ikemen's pause menu would print for this character (§3.10e): each move in Ikemen's own glyph tokens with its name and where the name came from, flags for a move with no real name (`weak`, "No name") and a name neither the stock fonts nor DotGothic16 draw (`drawable: false`, "Won't print": Hangul, simplified-only Chinese; §3.10f), and the exact file the export writes. With Edit on, the switch **Write this list into exported copies** (`POST /api/movelist { char, enabled }`), and a name can be changed or a move hidden from the game's list; "Save names" sends only the changed rows (`POST /api/movelist { char, rows: [{ state, name?, hidden? }] }`), kept for this build, never written into the character's folder. An empty name goes back to the one read from the files. A character that ships its own list is shown as such, with her own file, and nothing is generated. A 404/405 from the route reads "Not available in this build" and the states are listed by number and attack type; any other failure says it could not be read. Every attack state's Command cell prints an input: its Command List line's, else the reader's `inputs` (plain normals with their stance: `X`, `↓ + X`, `AIR X`; throws; a state of a character that ships her own list). The page draws the writer's TOKENS (what the pause menu prints), the .cmd text beside the opened move. A state with an input but no line says why ("Plain normals stay out of the game's Command List", "prints it on another state's line", "ships a Command List of its own"). States nothing in the -1 enters by a command (follow-ups, helpers, system states, var-driven moves) have none. The third group is "Unique attacks 特殊技" (2026-10-18).

**Every value has two names**: what a fighting-game player calls it (Hitstun, Blockstop, Hit pushback, Juggle cost, Chains from...) with what it does, and the engine's parameter underneath. The table is grouped the same way: damage and meter, stun and hitstop, how it hits, pushback and launch, knockdown, juggle and cancels, throws and states, projectile, effects.

**Three kinds of value.**

- **Green: a plain number.** Editable.
- **Amber: the CvS damage template**, `ceil(ifElse(fvar(N) * B < M, M, fvar(N) * B))`. The input holds the base `B`; the write changes both copies of it and leaves the scaling intact.
- **Red: anything else.** The badge says which kind: text and flags (`attr`, `hitflag`, `guardflag`, `animtype`), a table prefix (`S22` is sound 22 from the character's own file, `F100` spark 100 from the common effects), the letter `n`, an expression computed at runtime, a parameter the engine ignores, or more values than it reads. `attr = S, NA` is one value to the engine, not two. **A formula is editable as text**, with what it reads as a first hit beside it; any number may also be replaced by a formula and a formula by a number. A comma outside brackets (it would become another value), a `;` or line break, and unbalanced brackets or quotes are refused; a formula the Studio's reader cannot follow asks to confirm, because one the engine cannot compile stops the character from loading. Everything else red is never written.
- **A value the block leaves out can be added** from the readout (hitstun, blockstun, hitstop, damage, chip): one `name = value` line after the block's last line, validated like any write with every later line allowed to move down by exactly one. An added value pins what the engine would derive.

**Values the engine derives.** When a HitDef leaves them out, `dizzypoints`, `guardpoints`, `redlife`, `getpower` and `givepower` are computed from the hit damage times a multiplier. The multipliers come from the engine's built-in constants, then `data/common.const`, which overrides them, then the character's own first `[Constants]` section. The window shows these as read-only rows with their formula, so a damage edit visibly moves them. Writing one of them into the block pins it: it stops following damage.

**How a write works.** Every edit to a character file, from this window or the animation editor, goes the same way:

1. Only the bytes of the changed number are replaced. Nothing is re-serialized, so comments, spacing, line endings and Shift-JIS text stay byte for byte.
2. The first time a file is touched, the original is copied to `<file>.edit.bak`. That copy is never overwritten, so a second session cannot replace the original with an already-edited file.
3. The new text is parsed again with the same reader and must keep every statedef, controller and trigger. Otherwise nothing is written.
4. The file is written to a temporary name and renamed over the original, so a failure leaves the old file or the new one, never half of each. A failed write removes its temporary file, and the backup too when that write was the one that made it.
5. **Revert** (two clicks) puts the backup back byte for byte and deletes it. It finds backups at any depth in the character's folder. It discards every edit to that file, including trigger renumbers made by the animation editor.

Exports drop `.bak` files, so a backup never ships. The build's file index is refreshed after each write.

**The values, and what each one moves.**

| value | what the engine does with it | what can go wrong | what the window does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `damage` (hit, guard) | Hit damage also sets the default dizzy points, guard points, red life and power | 0 still hits, with pause, hitstun and the state change. A negative number heals. One change moves four other systems | Whole number, 0 or more. Derived rows update |
| `pausetime`, `guard.pausetime` | Guard pause copies hit pause when absent | Changing hit pause changes guard pause too when the block has none | Whole number, 0 or more |
| `ground.hittime`, `air.hittime`, `guard.hittime`, slide and control times | `guard.hittime` falls back to `ground.slidetime` in a MUGEN character and to `ground.hittime` with `ikemenversion` | An edit cascades into guard values the block leaves out | Whole number, 0 or more; the note names the fallback in effect |
| `fall.damage` | Applied as a life change with no attack scaling | Ignores the character's attack power | Whole number, 0 or more |
| `dizzypoints`, `guardpoints`, `redlife`, `getpower`, `givepower` | Derived from damage when absent; guard power is half of hit power | Writing one pins it. Negative power drains | Whole number; a note says it will stop following damage |
| `id`, `chainid`, `nochainid` | Chain-cancel tags | Rewires which moves combo into which | Asks for confirmation before writing |
| `p1stateno`, `p2stateno` | `p2stateno` also makes the opponent run this character's states | Sends either player to a different state; a missing number freezes them (3.2b) | Asks for confirmation before writing |
| `air.juggle` | Read for projectiles, and for everything with `ikemenversion`. The state's own juggle is its `[Statedef]` header | Editing the juggle the engine does not read | Whole number, with a note |
| velocities, accelerations, `fall.*velocity` | Decimal numbers | Nothing structural | Any decimal |
| `priority`, unprefixed `sparkno`, `sparkxy`, sound numbers, `envshake.*`, `palfx.*` | Whole or decimal per parameter | Cosmetic or behavioral only | Whole or decimal as the parameter takes |
| on/off values (`kill`, `fall`, `hitonce`, `forcestand`) | 0 or 1 | — | 0 or 1 only |
| any number | Whole numbers are written plainly (`+3` becomes `3`); a decimal keeps the author's style (`-.8` stays `-.8`) | A stale view writes to the wrong place | Exponents, empty text and very large numbers are refused. A changed file is refused as stale and the window reloads |

**Moves that cannot be charted from the files** (2026-10-19). When the listed attack states (numbered and negative) name at least one animation and not one of them draws a sprite (`-1` frames, or actions the .air lacks), `charMovesIn` adds `blankAttacks { states, inHelpers, named, absent }` (`states` = what the window lists) and the window says so above the list: "None of the N animations this character's S attack states name draws a sprite (A of them are not in its .air), so its moves cannot be charted from its files." Never when the sprite file could not be read (missing, unreadable, no sprites: `geomReaderIn` `hasSprites` false), where every frame measures 0x0 and the animations are not to blame. It adds what the files show about helpers and no more: `movelib helperRunStates` = states entered from a Helper controller's literal stateno, or by a ChangeState/SelfState that only a helper can fire (every live trigger group needs ishelper, `scenelib.ishelperNeed`), closed over literal ChangeState/SelfState - "The files show a helper entering every one of those states", or "The files show a helper entering H of those S states". Grim Reaper Mai: 36 listed attack states (34 numbered, -2 and -1), 61 animations named, 7 not in her .air, 21 states entered by a helper (her state 81 sends `ishelper(81)` into them; the other 13 numbered ones are never named by a literal number). The model keeps `helperAttackStates`. Test: `tools/test-helper-body.js` (one helper-run attack on a blank animation; KFM gets no note, and neither does a KFM copy whose .sff is gone).

**Test characters.** Kung Fu Man covers the plain cases: one HitDef per state, a Clsn2Default shared by several elements, literal damage. RyuDX covers projectiles (state 1000 throws one on element 5, tick 8, from an animation with no hit box of its own) and prefixed sounds. Balrog covers animations chosen by variable: his state 1600 picks its animation from `var(10)`, so the window lists candidates and says they are a guess. Projectiles: Shake (H-LOADER: arcs, `projscale` 0.5 at [Size] 0.5, a five-hit phone, a projectile whose animation has no hit box), Ken-Zero3 (a plain fireball), Marvin (helpers), Krillin (blank helpers drawn by Explods), Grim Reaper Mai (310 invisible Projectiles in her -2: a load test, read statically only). Explod art: Shake 1213 (the lawnmower: a long root Clsn1 drawn by an ontop Explod, bound for its whole 80-frame life; the strip at 1024 x 700 is the owner's legibility check), Amy Sorel 200 (a slash in front of her, sprpriority 5), Divesim 1530 (an Explod at -2,-77, head height, bound 1 frame), Ironhide 3800 (an Explod at P2 on MoveHit: listed, not drawn), KFM (none).

## 3.10e The pause menu's Command List: the writer

**Ikemen GO's pause menu shows a Command List only when the character's .def names a `movelist` file** (`[Files]` `movelist`, then `movelist0`, then `movelist<N>`; char.go `loadMovelists`, read with LoadText: the bytes as they are, a UTF-8 BOM dropped, no Shift-JIS decode of the content). menu.lua `f_commandlistParse` draws it: every key of the motif's `[Glyphs]` found in the text becomes its picture, longest key first (`_D _DF _F _+ ^X ^A ~D ...`); `<#rrggbb>`..`</>` colors a run; a field after one tab is centered, after two or more right-aligned. 8% of 1,747 characters ship one.

**The export writes one for every character that ships none** (`cmdlist.js`, both builds; 2026-10-18): `movelist.dat` beside the def (`<def>-movelist.dat` when that name is taken in the copy) and `movelist = movelist.dat ;Command List written by the export` as the FIRST line of the def's first `[Files]` (a key's first value wins, so it also beats a line naming a file that is not there). Desktop: `fixCopiedCharacters` writes both into the folder it just copied; website: vfslib's repair loop overlays both (`generated`). Last step per def, on the def as every earlier repair left it, in its own try (a failure costs that character its list only). **Never into the character's own folder; a character whose def names a movelist that exists and is not empty is never touched.** `charFixes` gets `{ kind: 'command-list', file, moves, def }`, and the export's back page counts it among the owner's choices (§3.1).

**studio-lite writes it too** (2026-10-29: the owner's "Add that feature to the studio-lite"; the itch page promised the list for characters that never shipped one). The writer is `public/ikemen/cmdlist-core.js` (global `cmdlistCore`), which reads with `scenelib-core.js` (Go's text rules, `decodeText`, the engine's `[Files]` order `stateFilesOf`, `parseStates`) and `cnsexpr-core.js` (cnsexpr.js word for word). All three are pure: no fs, no Buffer, no DOM; bytes go through TextEncoder/TextDecoder (a strict UTF-8 decode keeps a byte-order mark, as Buffer did). The core reads a character through an io `{ read(rel) -> latin1 text | null, isFile(rel), list(rel) }`: paths relative to her folder ('..' leads out of it), letter case ignored, listings sorted, so drop or archive order changes nothing. `readChar(io, def, opts)` is the old readFresh, `shipChar(io, def, opts)` the old shipFor (the list as UTF-8 text with no BOM), `shipFiles(files, def)` is shipChar over the dropped files with `exists` = those files in any case. **`cmdlist.js`, `scenelib.js` and `cnsexpr.js` are those cores for Node,** with the same exports and output: cmdlist.js keeps the read cache, a row's `drawable` flag (jpfont.js) and the cancels; scenelib.js the disk reads (a state file over 8 MB still skipped), the reachability and the H analysis; jpfont.js takes `stockDraws` from the core, so one rule decides which name prints. **In the page** `addCharacter` calls `cmdlistCore.shipFiles(files, def)` before it stores anything: the def with the movelist line and `movelist.dat` (or `<def>-movelist.dat` when the dropped files already hold that name) beside it, in the overlay at `chars/<mount>/...`, the paths the Website export uses. A character with her own list is stored as dropped; there are no roster choices in the web game, so the defaults apply (entryFor's fallback); a failure costs her the list only. The entry records `commandList: { file, moves }` and the toast ends "Command List: N moves". Import a build writes the sender's bytes as they are (the Build ID must match) and writes no list; a sender on this version already carries the lists. The page loads the three cores with `<script>` tags (+134,896 bytes, unlike the archive unpacker), so the export copies them and the itch zip carries them with no list to edit. **Proofs** (2026-10-29): over 184 defs (the checkout's cache and three Content bundles) the Node modules before and after give the same rows, inputs, cancels, def text, list bytes and scenelib parse (39,133 statedefs, 386,409 controllers), 0 differences; in headless Chrome the page's cores give Node's bytes and rows for the same 184 defs; a character with no list dropped as a `.zip`, a RAR 5 and a `.7z` lands as the same files, its def and movelist.dat byte-identical to `shipFor` on the disk, and one that ships her own (Divesim) byte for byte as dropped; seen in the engine: Balrog added in studio-lite, paused, his Command List drawn. A Japanese-only name prints blank there: studio-lite does not add DotGothic16 (3.10f; open, the owner's call). A state file named in Shift-JIS resolves from an old archive that stores the raw bytes; stored as UTF-8 (RAR 5, 7z, .NET zip) it does not, and neither does the engine reach it.

**A row** = a ChangeState in `[Statedef -1]` whose triggers ask for commands and whose value is a state number (a literal, or `Ifelse(<more>, EX, normal)` down its else branch). Read with scenelib's `stateFiles` + `parseStates` (the engine's rules; `[State <any text>]` headers). The input = a `[Command]` definition (its first CHARGE definition, else its first) of the command(s) one trigger group asks for (`holdfwd` + `x` = F+x; `holdfwd` + `holddown` = DF), in the motif's keys step by step: `~D, DF, F, x` -> `_D_DF_F^X` (charges and holds: below); never compressed into quarter-circle glyphs (every motif has the arrows; the page's `Booklet.glyphs` renders the same tokens). The trigger lines are read as expressions (`cmdlist.js` `commandsOfGroup`, cnsexpr's parser): `&&` both sides, `||` the left side when it asks for a command, else the right, `!=` and `!` nothing - so Balrog's throw `(command = "holdfwd" || command = "holdback") && (command = "pp" || command = "kk")` is `_F_+^X_+^Y`, and `command="c" && !(command = "holdfwd" || ...)` is c alone (a line the parser cannot read falls back to the old text scan). A command with several definitions prints its first CHARGE definition, else its first (Guile's Somersault Strike: `~DB, DF, DB, UF, a`, not `~DB, $D, F, UF, a`). The stance the trigger group asks for prints with the input: `statetype = A` -> `_AIR` first (the engine's own KFM list: `_AIR_F_+^X`); `statetype = C` with one press and no down in it -> `_D_+` first; `statetype != A` is only "grounded" (no mark). One row per state, first block in file order. Groups by state number only: 1000-2999 Special, 3000-4999 Super (KOF-style EX specials cost a stock, so power cannot tell them apart), 200-999 **Unique Attacks** when the input is more than a button (F+x, a+b, a motion, or a direction with a button in the air; `uniqueAttack`) - KFM's own movelist.dat heads his command normals so; the group was "Other Moves" before 2026-10-18. Left out: plain/crouching/jumping normals (a button standing, down + button crouching, a button in the air: no shipped list on this machine lists them - KFM's own list gives Unique Attacks and Throws only, the dhalsim template explains the six buttons once, in prose), states under 200, AI routing (a CPU/AI/COM<n> command, a trigger asking AILevel on), never-true blocks, ChangeStates inside moves. A later state of the same group with the same input whose name repeats an earlier one's (a cancel or air version) is one line.

**Charges and holds** (`chargeStart`, `convertCommand`; 2026-10-18, the owner's report "Balrog ... our movelist arrows don't indicate this"). The engine (`src/input.go` ReadCommandSymbols/matching, f598853): `~` = released, `~N` = held at least N ticks then released, `/` = held (Ikemen: `/N` held N ticks), `$` = the direction or a diagonal holding it, `>` = nothing in between, `+` together, `|` either (Ikemen). A bare `~` checks NO hold time - Balrog and Guile count their charge in a variable (`var(48) > 16`), so the notation is the only tell. A command's first step is a CHARGE when it is one direction released or held N > 0 ticks (`~30$B`), or released with no count into the opposite direction: back into forward (`~$B, F`, `~$B, $F`, `~DB, DF`) or down into up (`~$D, U`). Not a charge: a motion's leading release (`~D, DF, F`, `~F, D, DF`, `~B, DB, D` Zero Counter, `~$B, $D`, `~F, B, D, F`). Printed as the motif's hold arrow and its "..." glyph: `~$B, F, x` -> `~B_._F^X`, `~$B, F, B, F, x` -> `~B_._F_B_F^X` (the shipped template's `~B... _F`, dhalsim/divesim/NeoGeegus movelist.dat). A button held N ticks (`~30x`) -> `_HOLD^X`; a bare `~x` -> `^X`; a held direction then buttons is one press (`/F,z` -> `_F_+^Z`, CvS throws); any other `/ $ > ~` on a direction is a plain arrow. Every token is a key of defaultMotif.ini [Glyphs] (`~B` 95 "hold Back", `_.` 40 "...", `_AIR` 121, `_HOLD` 137). Verified in the engine (web build, headless, paused, Command List, 2026-10-18): `~B_._F^X` draws the HOLLOW back arrow, the dots on the arrows' line, then forward and X; that shot shows the list's first page only (the Unique Attacks page and the `_AIR` throw were not seen drawn). A false positive (a bare `~B, F` whose author counts no charge) is possible (none among Main's 38 charge lines, all from charge characters); tighten to "with `$` or ticks" if one is seen (one condition in cmdlist.js `chargeStart` and booklet.js `chargeStart`). Balrog's far and close heavy punch (220/225) both print `^Z`; the Moves page tells them apart (Proximity, below).

**Every input (`inputs`).** Besides the rows, the reader gives every state the -1 reaches by a command its input: `{ state, input, glyphs, stance, file, line, listed }`, the first block in file order. Targets: the literal or the Ifelse's else branch (the rows' state), each when-true branch down an Ifelse chain (with the command its condition asks for, else the block's: `Ifelse(command = "charge" && ..., 3150, 3100)`), and a value with 1..8 possible states from `cnsexpr.valueSet` without variables (`220 + (Abs(P2bodydist X) <= 25) * 5` = 220 and 225). `listed` = the state is a line, a strength merged into one, or a cancel/air twin. A character with her own list gets `inputs` too (rows and text stay empty). The GET body carries them; the Moves window prints them for every attack state (§3.10).

**Proximity (`inputs[].range`, `distTests`, `closeTest`).** One button, two moves by distance. A ChangeState value that tests `P2BodyDist X` or `P2Dist X` is read with the distance at 0 and far away (Balrog's `220 + (Abs(P2bodydist X) <= 25) * 5`: 225 close, 220 far; CvS Mai's `IfElse(P2BodyDist X <= 15,205,200)`). Otherwise a block whose own trigger lines test the distance is close (open near, shut far) or far, and the NEXT block in the -1 on the same glyphs and stance with no distance of its own is the other one (Jill's 221 `triggerall = P2BodyDist X <= 30`, then 220). `range = { kind: 'close'|'far', op, dist, by: 'P2BodyDist X'|'P2Dist X', file, line }`, always stated as the close side's test (`> 30` is close `<= 30`), only on the block the state's input came from. A distance-gated move with no twin (a throw's `P2BodyDist X < 3`) prints close alone. The game's file is unchanged (no distance in movelist.dat). Main (2026-10-18): 76 inputs in 13 characters carry a range.

**The cancels (`cancels`, `cancelsOf`; only for `readFor(..., { cancels: true })`, which the route asks and an export never does).** For every attack state S (a HitDef, ReversalDef, Projectile or a Modify in its own code) and every -1 ChangeState a player's command takes into 200-4999 (AI blocks out, as for the rows): can one of its trigger groups be true while S runs? Each group is read with cnsexpr, three-valued, under: `stateno` = S, `ctrl` = 0, `statetype` / `movetype` = S's header, `hitdefattr = SC, NA, ...` against S's HitDef attrs (state letters and attack types intersect; `AA/AT/AP` expand), contact on hit (`movecontact` = `movehit` = 1) and on block (`moveguarded` = 1), `numhelper(N)` unknown only if S spawns a helper whose id can be N (else 0), `projcontacttime` etc. unknown on contact, `roundstate` 2, `ailevel` 0, `time` 4, 8, 14, 24 and 40 (a window open only in the first 3 ticks is a kara cancel, not one on hit). A group open in a neutral, non-attack state with no contact is no cancel (a route open everywhere). **Variables**: every tick the [State -3] and [State -2] VarSets, then the -1's VarSets in file order up to the block, are run over "worlds" (an unknown trigger forks one; at most 32) - EXACT, `via` names the variable (KFM's `var(1)`, Balrog's -3 `var(6)`/`var(7)`, the CvS template's `var(22)` whose value decides SP or SU, Jill's -2 `var(36)`). A VarSet in S's OWN code adds a world marked APPROXIMATE (the -1 reads it a tick later; ≈ with the variable named: Kotaro's `var(33)`). A VarAdd'ed variable (a counter) is never simulated: unknown in a triggerall (Balrog's charge `var(48) > 16`), 0 in a group line (Jill's combo timer `var(16)`); any variable nothing simulates is unknown in a triggerall and 0 in a group line (a mode such as a custom combo or a groove is off); so is a simulated variable no VarSet wrote in the tick being read (CARRIED from before: unknown in a triggerall, 0 elsewhere - a mode a -2 VarSet sets only under a condition the reader cannot see, as in CvS Mai, Iori and Miyako). Kinds by the target: SU 3000-4999, SP 1000-2999, CH 200-999 from a state under 1000; re-entering the same special or super is not listed. `cancels = [{ state, to: [{ state, kind, hit, block, exact, via, file, line }] }]`. cnsexpr's two hooks (`ctx.unk`, `ctx.cmpHook`) exist for this reader; no other caller passes them. **Blind spots** (not measured): a move that gives control back mid-state (CtrlSet) makes the neutral routes cancels and is not listed; whiff-only cancels are not marked; an unknown trigger (animelemtime, a projectile's contact, a redirect) counts as possibly true, so a helper-projectile route lists supers from every special that spawns that helper; a variable carried over from an earlier state is not followed; a character whose blocks ask for no `command =` (Makoto routes her moves through her own variables, `var(22) != 0 && var(24) = 6`) has neither inputs nor cancels. **Census of Main** (read-only, 2026-10-18): 29 characters, 694 attack states with cancels, 8,190 exact links, 30 approximate (Kotaro), 20-270 ms a character, 1.7 s the slowest (cvsyokoRX), cached by the reader's stamp after the first read (a memo per line and value set; the time samples stop once a tick never reads `time`).

**The name**, first that reads like a name (the census's `descriptive`): the owner's > the header label (`[State -1, Kung Fu Palm]`, or a no-comma header's whole text) > a comment that spells the command name out (ブレス -> ダイヤモンドブレス, EX aside) > the command name (unless several moves share it) > the shortest block comment (above the header, or on its line) > the target statedef's comment. Never a name: a label or comment used for 3+ different states (copy-pasted template, `[State Scramble Dash]`), KFM's "Kung Fu ..." outside KFM, ERROR/null/dummy/debug. Shift-JIS bytes (not valid UTF-8) are decoded; file and page carry UTF-8. **Among the candidates, the first in printable ASCII wins**: the stock pause menu prints a Japanese name BLANK (web: `movelist.text.font = 7` = Open_Sans.def, shadowed by an ASCII pixel font; seen in a headless match on Kula, 2026-10-18; that the desktop build's Open Sans draws no kana either is a hypothesis, not run), so a Japanese name is written only when nothing else names the move (`JP.stockDraws`; the readme is asked only when no candidate is printable ASCII). The row's `drawable` says whether the BUILD draws it (jpfont.js `drawable`): true for printable ASCII and for a name DotGothic16 draws - kana, kanji, Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, read from the font's own cmap - because a build whose list prints such a name ships the font (3.10f); false only for a script the font lacks (Hangul, simplified-only Chinese: the Moves page's "Won't print"). Keeping a Japanese label over an ASCII command name would change builds that print ASCII today (4 of 284 ASCII-only defs in the 182-character census, one of them garbled), so that is the owner's call, not made. In the file a name has no tab, `<`/`>`, or `_ ^ ~` (glyph-key starts: `Hard_Drive` would print a Down arrow), at most 48 characters. Heads `<#f0f000>:Special Moves:</>` (KFM's own color), lines `<name>\t\t<glyphs>`, CRLF, UTF-8 without BOM.

**One line per move: the strengths merge** (`cmdlist.js` `mergeStrengths`, `strengthBase`, `lastButton`; Phase B). CvS-style characters list a move once per button (Makoto: Light/Medium/Strong Hayate, 43 lines). Rows of ONE group whose input is the same motion ending in exactly ONE button of one family (punches x y z, kicks a b c), with different buttons, and whose names are equal once a strength is taken out, print as one line. A strength is a whole word (Light, Lite, Medium, Med, Mid, Middle, Strong, Heavy, Hard, Fierce, Weak, Jab, Short, Roundhouse, L, M, H, LP..HK), a suffix naming the row's own button (`Kacho Sen_x`, `Hadouken_X`), or Japanese 弱/中/強 at either end (`花蝶扇・弱`, `早蕨強`). Names that are identical merge too. All three buttons = the motif's "any punch"/"any kick" glyph **`^P` / `^K`** (defaultMotif.ini `[Glyphs]` 53,0 / 54,0; the engine's own KFM list writes `_QDF^P`, and it draws as a P/K button in the web build's pause menu); two of the three = **`^X/^Y`**: a `/` between two glyphs is text in menu.lua `f_commandlistData` (not a key, not a tag), drawn by the font, as KFM's own `[_B/_F]`. Never merged: an input with two buttons (EX, `x+y`), a button in an earlier step, different groups, a weak name, `s`/`d`/`w`. The line is the first state's: its `state`, the owner's name and hide for that state apply to the line; a later version the owner renamed or hid keeps a line of its own (so a name saved on a later version before the merge existed now prints that version on its own line). The row carries **`merged: [{ state, name, nameFrom, input, glyphs }]`** (each version as the files name it; `modlib.js charMovelist` passes the field) and `input` in .cmd notation with the alternatives (`~D, DF, F, x/y/z`). Measured on Main: Makoto 43 -> 29 lines, Cvs_Mai 28 -> 20, RyuDX 37 -> 29, kotaro_gnsk 23 -> 18 (two strengths: `^X/^Y`); the CVS bundle's Dudley (Light/Strong/Fierce) 31 -> 23. tools/test-cmdlist.js checks every printed input is made only of `[Glyphs]` keys of the engine's defaultMotif.ini plus `/`. **Not seen in a frame yet:** Makoto's merged list was not booted in the web game (two headless boots hung before the first frame); the tokens are the ones the engine's KFM list draws.

**A name from the readme** (`nameFrom: 'readme'`, `readmeEntries`, `readmeInput`, `readmeFits`). Only for a row whose code gives NO name the stock pause menu can print (no descriptive label/command/comment, or only Japanese ones): the character's own text files (top level of the folder and of the def's folder; `.txt`/`.md` whose name says readme/move/command/list/info/manual/howto/faq; never a file the def's [Files] names; at most 256 KB; Shift-JIS decoded) are read for lines `<name> : | - | = | tabs <input>`. The input is read in the notations readmes use: `D DF F ...` (UPPER case; lower-case `b` is the button), `QCF QCB HCF HCB DP RDP`, numpad `236P`, arrows `↓↘→`, buttons `x y z a c` (either case) and `b`, `P`/`K` (any punch/kick), `2P`, `3K`, `LP..HK`, `Start`. A note in brackets is dropped, except one that offers other buttons (`x (or y,z)`): those become alternatives. A line is NOT read when its input has anything else, buttons one after another (`a, b`: a target combo), or "or" outside brackets. **Unambiguous**: the readme lines whose input fits the row must name exactly ONE move; two names for one input (Makoto's `D,DF,F,D,DF,F + z` is Seichuzen Godanzuki "(or y,z)" AND Judanzuki) = no readme name. The readme name joins the candidates last, so the code's printable name always wins; the row's `raw.readme` holds it. On Main today no row changes (the characters with weak or Japanese-only names ship no English move readme) - tested on fixtures and checked on Makoto's readme (136 move lines). `readFor`'s cache stamp includes the readme files.

**In the Moves window** a merged line is read back as one row per version (`clRows()` in moves.html: each version's own name and input), so the printed state list stays per state; the opened move says "In the game's Command List it is one line with its other 2 strengths: Hayate [glyphs]", and the Command List table's source column says "states 1000, 1010, 1020 (one line for 3 strengths)". Renaming or hiding a merged line saves on its first state. `Booklet.glyphs` reads `^P` / `^K` (an ink / band chip "P" / "K", aria "any punch") and `/` between movelist tokens (aria "or"), and in .cmd notation a last step `x/y/z`.

**The switch and the owner's choices** (roster entry key `commandList`, on CHAR_PERSIST: `{ off?: true, names?: {state: name}, hidden?: [state] }`, per bundle, per roster entry - two defs of one folder are two entries).
