  - Measured: every other giver's pair identical on Main (300 of 300); Murakami 114 of 369 steps changed (41 lifted, 46 strokes sustained, 30 gauge climaxes with a longer patience, the demon's `high`); in the corpus only his three copies differ. Played: R.Mika scenes 2-24 all shown (strokes 100%, the lifts, 484's phases), Kung Fu Girl Z's "grab c" 13/17 and its climax, her gauge climax 8/17, Mai's lifts and the demon.
- **ANOTHER STAND.** A scene key that lands while a grab is on its way (the place made, `G.t >= 2`, or the grab about to enter) to a step that stands elsewhere (`LEAN.stand`: its place, reach, edge-only or wide flag, companion, a mode's own place) resets and places again ("another stand: placed again"); before, the first try grabbed from the old stand and missed for 240 ticks (Creatures' worm after quick `]` steps).
- **THE SCENE'S END, A GRACE** (`K.GRACE` = 3, `LEAN.ended`). She out of his states ends the scene only after 3 ticks while he is still in a state of his own (not 0-199 or 5000-5999): a re-grab whose HitDef has `p1stateno` but no `p2stateno` leaves her a tick in her own get-hit state until his next state's Time = 0 TargetState takes her back (Murakami's 2904 -> 2905 -> her 2925).
- **A summon's way in, in the log** (diagnostic): for a step with `clear`, the 'enter' phase logs every 30 ticks the helper's state and x, his and hers ("enter: helper <id> in <state> at x <x>, him at x <x>, her at x <x>").
- **Engine facts the proofs turned up.** A helper's Clsn1 is scaled by its ROOT's [Size] xscale (ownclsnscale off). A state entered by `changeState` has no target: his TargetState and TargetBind do nothing until a HitDef of his connects (Yarimusi's 25400 hands her to its helper, so the presses after the 960-tick handoff move him, 4862 -> 29130 -> 29230, and never her). A model that stops at any Projectile would drop harmless afterimages too (hence the inert rule).

Played headless, one light run per rule through the engine lock (verified): Mina's dash ("place reach 83", its scenes on screen), Succubus' 21000 at 133, Roper's 230/600, several pairs with Mina at -75 and DongHwan at the gap (49/49), the worm (1330), the mino at 80 (36646 at t = 51), Monsters' creatures with the flower girl drawn (1.74% of the frame pink against 0.01% before), Marasama's x/b/c with three creatures while he stays in 0, White-Len's speed from another position, FutaNT's speeds, climax, second version and position 2 on his animations, Eko's loop (100%) and gauge-empty climax (50123), dragon_futa2 x R.Mika 8/8 and x Hong Meiling with no AI chain (its negative control, the aliases removed: scenes 3-4 land in her 16215 / his 16017), FutamaruPlus' 1801 with the lift, Taokaka's intro skipped at frame 605, Tendril's 610 at reach 27, Murakami's phase 1 at t = 2111, Creatures' second stand on the first try.

Not fixed yet: Succubus' grab 21000 lands in his hub 17001, which draws var(20) with `VarRandom range 5` and gives her 17202 + var(20), so she may land in a pose the step does not list ("did not reach this scene"; reading a VarRandom's literal range as the variable's values was tried and taken back: it lost the press-a position and the hub's nav). Tendril's 640 (type A, physics N) never starts, a hand-set lift did not help, and the cause is not traced. Yarimusi's 25400 phases: entered by `changeState` he has no target, his helper takes her as its own, so the presses after the handoff move him and never her (entering through his real lead, 29350, whose TargetState makes her his target, is the likely way: a hypothesis). FutaRB White-Len's and Eko's plain speed ("hold a") is on screen 30-41%: it plays one cycle and goes back to the hub, and after a fresh grab her hub state is never among the hold's earlier states, so the hold never turns into a sustain (the "looping" step shows the speed 100%). Yarimusi's phases inside one state of hers (her animation by time) were out of scope. A timed ladder's later rungs take their patience from their own rung waits (Murakami's phase 2: 1920), and whether a fresh grab into phase 2 runs out was not checked in the engine.

`trimData` works out where each key goes from each step (`navTables`: `nv` { p, v, g, c } and `k` { l, r, u, d, s, f, c, h }, the pair's `nav` its positions' base steps), so the runtime never searches:

- **Left / Right** the previous / next position, going around the pair, at the same version, stage, speed and climax where the new position has them, else the nearest that exists (a climax to its climax, auto to its auto, bent over speed 2 to a ladder's phase 2); a speed is compared by the number its label names where its position names every speed so (Brian's position 4 "speed 2" goes to position 5's "speed 2", its first), else by its rank;
- **Up / Down** the previous / next version of this position (around), at the same speed or climax;
- **Delete / End** one speed slower / faster, auto the top speed; they stop at the ends ("the slowest already", "the fastest already"); a position with one speed has none to step (no speed on its line; Kung Fu Girl's position 7 is "speed 3" alone); at a climax of several pictures (a companion's: speed 1 and 2 on its climax steps) they step between them ("picture 1/2" on the line; "the first picture already"), which no other key reaches - his climax and her orgasm are switched by Up/Down instead, each finisher's own pictures still by Delete/End; at a climax of one they have nothing to do ("Space leaves the climax");
- **Space** the climax on and off: on, the position's climax at this version (its first picture or finish); off, back to the step it was turned on from where that is the same position, version and stage (the runtime remembers it), else the base; a position that is only its climax (Minotaur x Miyako's positions 4) has "CLIMAX" on its line and Space says "only the climax in this position" (-1 in `k`);
- **Home** the next stage, going around; the line names a stage as its label does, of the position's top one ("Home stage base/3", "Home stage 1/3", "Home stage 3/3": the finish count's levels 0, 1 and 3 of Brian's position 1).

A key with nothing to do here (0 in `k`) says so on the status line ("no other speed in this position", "one version of this position"). Out of a leaf (her orgasm) every move grabs again at once. Every move but Page Up / Page Down is a step change in place where the running grab has it (the absolute paths), else a fresh grab; **a version move where her state is one of the new step's already grabs again**: her state would not start again, so neither would what it picks of her art on its first tick (Bao's position 4 reads his var(23) there: in place she kept the under-him art while Bao played on top).

**Controls are hotkeys, most on one side of the keyboard, and P2 is off.** Left / Right the position, Up / Down its version, Delete / End slower / faster, Space the climax, Home the stage, Page Up / Page Down the previous / next pair (the only keys that reload), 1-4 the active pair, + / - the zoom on it (several pairs; below), Insert the overlay on or off (H too), Tab the pair picker, Esc leaves. Inside the picker Insert adds its pair and Delete takes the active pair off the screen (only there; the last pair stays). **Every key is taken inside `run()`** with `if gameMode() == "hgallery"` (one `take` helper), since a key keeps only its last binding and a later one would replace it: Tab hands on to `SceneViewerCycle` outside the gallery; **Space is the engine's own debug key** (debug.lua: `addHotkey('SPACE', false, false, false, false, true, 'full(1); ... full(8); setTime(getRoundTime())')`), taken while the gallery runs (not a debug key there) and given back exactly as debug.lua binds it, debug-only flag and script, when `run()` ends: after the gallery a training match's Space is the engine's again, and does nothing with AllowDebugKeys = 0. None of these keys is P1's in the layout every build writes; the arrows are P2's. A key that acts on the scene or the pair does nothing while the picker is open or waits for keys to go up (it reads the arrows and Page Up / Page Down as menu keys) or while the fight is paused - the engine runs a hotkey paused or not (1.0.0 ignores addHotkey's pause flag), so the handler checks `paused()` itself. The arrows assume P1 is not on them: a build or a player that binds P1 to the arrows gets each gallery arrow as P1's direction on the active giver too (for DongHwan, Forward is a position switch or his see-through). **A reload on its way is never replaced**: the first request wins until its match ends, and every key waits for it - the arrows are also the picker's keys, and a Down pressed right after Insert swapped the add for another pair. Under `-hgallerylog` only, `[` and `]` step through the pair's steps in the data's order (the headless walks).

- **No receiver takes a player's input.** The hook asserts `NoInput` on every receiver the driver marks (`_gal_recv`, every frame from the loop's first tick); the flag is read by the next frame's command update, which resets her buffers before anything runs, so she never walks off during a reset or a place, however long an arrow is held. Her controls are also wired to a config nothing is bound to. A giver never gets NoInput: it would clear P1's keys on him (his asserted commands would survive it, the -4 asserts them after the update).
- **P1's controls follow the active pair, as the Scene Viewer hands them over.** `remapInput(n, m)` has player n read config m's keys and pad (the same table feeds the menu lists the V1 text's `getInput` reads; a V2 build's gallery reads `getAction` instead, plan 1.26 lane B). The active pair's giver reads config 1 (P1's keys and first pad); every other fighter reads config 12: remapInput takes up to MaxPlayerNo (12) and configs exist only up to `Config.Players` (at most 8), so it has no keys and no pad. An engine without a spare config gets the Scene Viewer's swap, and only the hook keeps receivers still. Applied every tick, so 1-4, a reload and a delete follow at once, and once more before each match starts: a match's first frame reads input before the loop's first tick, and after the title menu every control is its own (a P2 key held while the gallery loaded reached the receiver for two frames); `setAILevel(0)` on everyone once per match and switch. P1's keys do everything a player's do on him, beside the driver's commands, which work on every giver whoever holds controller 1: DongHwan's held Up puts the active pair in his position 2, a press of the current position's direction toggles his see-through. On a receiver's helper's pair they also reach what her steps leave out: on DongHwan x Chichi, Back held is position 3, where her bridge blanks her; his position 1 climax made with P1's own c on another step (no re-roll asked) can still send her to 72001/72002. Left so, as for every pair (P1 drives the active giver); keeping P1 off such a giver is the owner's call.
- **While the picker is open or waits for keys, every control is its own** (`resetRemapInput`): the picker reads P1's Enter and P2's arrows, and with pair 3 or 4 active and the default 4 players, config 1 would feed no menu list at all (the lists stop at Config.Players). The fight is paused then. Leaving (Esc, or an error in the loop) calls `resetRemapInput` and clears the marks; the title menu's `main.f_default` resets the remap too.
- **Insert** (outside the picker; H too) hides the overlay, its box and the markers, and shows them again; hiding says for two seconds that Insert brings them back, and so does coming back to the gallery with it hidden (once the fight shows); a note from a key still shows. Kept for the session (pairs, reloads, leaving and coming back), never saved. The picker draws itself either way. What a character draws on the screen itself (a CvS groove gauge) is his and stays. The overlay's lines stop at 51 characters: the 4:3 band at 6 px a character, and the font has no arrow glyphs. Its lines: the pair; the group and which position it is ("position 2   pos 2/4"); the scene and its verdict; in gold, **what this position has, each with its key** - only what it has ("ver 1/2 Up/Dn  speed 2/5 Del/End  Space climax", "phase 2/3 Del/End", "finish 1/2 Del/End  CLIMAX Space off", "Home stage base/3"; "CLIMAX" where the position is only its climax; "nothing more in this position" for a one-off), split in two between its parts where it does not fit one; the status line (a key's note); the keys; and Insert (with several pairs, 1-4 and +/- zoom: "1-3 active pair  +/- zoom  Insert hides this", 44 characters at four). A speed is named as its label names it ("speed base/3", "speed 2/3", "speed auto/3"; a ladder's "phase 2/3").

Esc leaves: the mode sets `main.pauseMenu = false`, so Esc ends `game()` the way it ends Random Test. A pair change calls `endMatch()` from the hotkey and the mode's own loop loads the next pair (`clearSelected` … `loadStart` … `game()`, as `main.f_randomtest`), with `start.f_setRounds(-1, {})` for a round that never times out; the -4 hook also sets `globalNoKo`/`noKoFall`/`noKoVelocity`, refills life under half, and turns the bars, round calls, hit counter and lifebar action texts off.

**Several pairs side by side, and the pair picker.** Up to four pairs play in one match: pair k is giver P(2k-1) on team side 1 and receiver P(2k) on side 2, loaded as Simul teams (the engine's MaxSimul is 4; `setTeamMode` refuses more), with `setCom(pn, 0)` for all eight players. Each pair has its own driver state and every pair ticks each frame; the hook reads its maps on the character running it, so each giver's command and variable requests drive only him - the same giver twice is two independent characters. One pair is ACTIVE: the keys and the overlay are its, its title in its marker's color. With one pair nothing differs from the single-pair gallery.

- **A pair is added or removed by reloading the match**: the engine fills character slots only when a match loads (Loader.load before runMatch), so nothing can join a running one. A slot whose pair did not change is kept loaded - `selectChar`'s override `p<side>.<member>.existed=1` makes the loader reuse the character when its def matches - and every pair comes back at its step from a fresh grab (paths are absolute; a running scene cannot survive the reload). A slot whose place shifted (a pair removed before it) loads fresh. A match that restores pairs cuts the round intros (the hook stands everyone in state 0 during round state 1; a single fresh pair keeps its intro), and every gallery match, a single fresh pair included, then purges once, when the fight starts, everything the intros left the way the engine's own intro skip clears it (`removeExplod` on the characters, `destroySelf` on their helpers, which read the request through `root, map(...)` - Dr. Kira's slime helper otherwise stood over the next pair, and Sakura's intro helper Kei ran on through a single pair's first scene; a helper a character's -2 keeps up comes back the next frame). Restoring is also sped up: the match runs at `setAccel(4)` until every pair shows its step (the engine resets the speed each match, so it is asked every tick). Adding a pair takes about 3-4.5 s from the key to every pair back; removing the last one about 1.5 s.
- **Placement and the camera.** PosSet x is camera-relative, so with several pairs the hook places at `map(_gal_x) - cameraPos x` (in each character's own units), pairs 150 units apart: at 32 px one grab caught two receivers, from 48 px none did. **A scene leans off its place, and the lean is made up for** (`LEAN`): his grab carries both toward her or back, so the scene plays to one side of where they stood - Brian's first scene 18 to the right, Minotaur's position 1 about 20 to the left, Kur0maru's first -17 - and an edge pair leaning outward stood far from the others (his report: "the 3rd pair is moved to the left more. Close to the others", for any third pair). Placement itself was exact (132/168 for slot 3, the mirror of slot 1); the driver now measures each scene 20 ticks into its show (the middle of giver and receiver against where they were placed, in 320-wide units toward the way he faces), keeps it for the session by pair and scene (and by grab, for an unseen scene of the same grab), and the next place stands the pair that much the other way, so the scene plays on its place. Nothing is moved mid-scene (no jump, no explod or helper left behind). A reload's 4x run waits for a new scene's lean and, when it leaned more than 6 off with nothing learned, grabs that pair again at once (Brian: "lean 18 (made up for 0)", placed again at 132, then "lean 18 (made up for 18)"; the three-pair reload went from 3.9 s to 5 s). A lean over 40 is a scene that carries her off and is not kept. Only several pairs, and never a step that needs the screen or its neighbors (`place`, `edgeOnly`, a companion's, a projectile grab) or a receiver's helper's pair: they keep their place. The camera is locked and zoomed out to fit with ModifyStageVar (zoomout = zoomin, both bounds at the center, verticalfollow 0, autocenter 1: below): 0.874 for two pairs, 0.620 for three, 0.480 for four, where everyone is half size and a 4:3 stage shows empty space past its art - two or three pairs on a wide stage is the comfortable range. The stage's reload flag clears it for the next match. A colored, numbered marker is drawn under each pair every frame (red, blue, yellow, green; the active one larger, outlined and blinking), and a translucent box (black, alpha 150/106, inside the 4:3 band) keeps the overlay readable - with several pairs from the start, with one pair too since 2026-10-08 (the owner: "It gets hard to read sometimes"; the demon's scene in the air rises under the help lines).
- **Zoom on the active pair (+ / -).** With several pairs, = (or Shift+=, the + typed), -, and the keypad's + and - step the camera between the fit (level 1: every pair, as above) and closer views on the active pair: each scale of `ZOOMS` (0.62, 0.8, 1, 1.25) more than a tenth past the fit, so two pairs have 0.874, 1, 1.25; three 0.62, 0.8, 1, 1.25; four 0.48, 0.62, 0.8, 1, 1.25. 1.25 is the closest: past normal size the view is anchored on the ground line and only shows less of what normal size shows, so it is clean on any stage. The camera is pinned by the same ModifyStageVar: zoomin = zoomout = the scale, both bounds at one center (at v1.0.0 the camera's limits are the bounds minus and plus half a view at zoomout, so equal bounds leave room for exactly one view) and autocenter 1 (it clamps the camera's target into that room; without it the camera moves only when a tracked fighter nears an edge, and stops short). ModifyStageVar resets the camera's limits, never its place or scale, so the camera pans there by itself: zooming in is gradual, zooming out snaps to the scale and pans. The center is the active pair's, between its giver and its receiver where they stand (a grab moves them off their place: after DongHwan's both stand 20 to the right of the pair's place, until the learned lean above makes up for it at the next place), as near as a camera may go at that scale: to the end of the stage's art (its bounds plus or minus 160 / its zoomout, in 320-wide units, read with Lua `stageVar` when the match starts, before the hook moves them), or of the fit's frame where that reaches further. So an edge pair at a middle level sits toward its edge, as fighters in a corner do (Mountainside Temple, three pairs: pair 3's place is 150, the camera centers on it at 1 and 1.25 and stops at 110 at 0.8). The camera follows the pair: pinned again once the pair's center is 30 from it (a scene that carries her off, a fresh grab back at the place), while smaller moves (a thrust) never sway it. A step that needs the screen's edge and a receiver's helper's pair are pinned on the pair's place instead (placed from the view's edge, the pair would pull the camera after it; her root stands behind him). Lua `posX` is the fighter's position minus the camera's, so a fighter's place is `posX() + cameraPosX()`. 1-4 move the pinned camera to the new active pair at the same level; a reload keeps the level where the new count has it, else the closest level below; one pair keeps the stage's own camera, and + / - say "zoom is for several pairs". The status line names the level ("zoom 3/4 on pair 2", "zoom: every pair"), and a key with nothing to do says so ("the closest zoom already", "every pair in view already"). The keys are taken in `run()` with the others and wait while the picker is open or waits, while paused, and while a reload is on its way. The engine binds the keypad's + and - only with Ctrl (its speed), a binding of its own (one script per key and modifiers), and = and - not at all; none is P1's or P2's in the layout every build writes.
- **Zoomed, nobody is pushed and only the active pair moves the camera.** A fighter with the screenbound flag is clamped into the view every frame and one with movecamera pulls the camera; the engine sets both again on every fighter each frame, before -4, and a scene's own ScreenBound (value 1 every frame: Minotaur, R. Mika, Kula, Miyako and more) runs after -4. So the hook's `[StateDef +1]`, after the state, asserts ScreenBound value 0 on every fighter the driver marks (`_gal_free`: 1 on the active pair, movecamera 1,1; 2 on the others and their helpers, movecamera 0,0): a pair beside the view plays its scene on, partly or fully off screen, and the pair the camera pans to is never pushed toward the view it leaves. Back at level 1 the marks stay until the camera has stood still for three ticks (it pans back from an edge pair, and a pair it has not reached yet would be pushed), then the fit's screenbound is back. A helper keeps the flags it was last given. Placement is absolute (PosSet x minus cameraPos x), so a reset lands at its place wherever the camera is, and the markers are drawn at zoom times (x minus camera), under their pairs at every level.
- **The catch-up runs silent.** A match that brings pairs back (a reload) or has several runs at `K.ACCEL` (4) until every pair shows its scene again ("restoring..." on the status line; at most `K.ACCEL_MAX` match frames). The engine runs that many ticks a frame and every PlaySnd fires per tick, so a moan a scene restarts every 15 ticks (Murakami Ryona Mob's own -2 line at Minotaur's speed 3, `Time > 7`, persistent 15, channel 8) came about 16 times a second - the owner's "like a glitch". The script sets the engine's character-sound mute (`toggleNoSound(true)`, upstream's) with the speed every tick (a match start clears it) and clears it wherever the speed goes back to 1: restored, an error in the script, the match left. Measured headless: the catch-up ends about 150 match frames after the load (two pairs: frame 182; one: 97), under a second at 4x. What the engine does at normal speed was read, not heard: a -2 controller's persistent counter is one per controller in the character's -2 bytecode and is not reset on a state change (bytecode.go StateBlock.Run, char.go stateChange1), his helpers (keyctrl 0, helpertype normal) never run his -2 (char.go actionRun), and his -2 is defined once, so his line restarts every 15 ticks at most.
- **A step that needs the screen waits while zoomed on another pair.** A summon that walks in from the screen edge (`place`: its pair is placed from the view's edge, and its helper spawns at it) and a receiver's helper her root summons at the edge would take the zoomed view's edges, in the middle of other pairs: such a step is placed and grabbed only while the view is its own (every pair in view, or zoomed on its pair with the camera still). A grab that is a projectile's hit (`proj`, from gallerydata.js: Kur0maru's gas 1080/1085) cannot land off screen at all: v1.0.0 removes a projectile past the view's edge plus its edgebound (40 by default), so zoomed on pair 3 at 1.25 Kur0maru's gas at the far left never reached Kula and the grab timed out. It is grabbed only while the camera is still with its pair in view (its place, give or take half the gap, within the half view plus 20). Otherwise the pair waits before the place (`place: waits for the view`, `viewwait` in the log's view of the pairs, counted as settled for a reload's fast run), and a scene of it already running plays on. Anything else a scene reads of the screen (FrontEdgeDist, ScreenPos X, Pos X, which is camera-relative) reads the zoomed view's.
- **Shared by every pair**: a giver's Pause or SuperPause freezes all of them (one global pause time), so a pair's timers count only while its giver advances; screen shakes, palette flashes and zooms hit the whole screen; characters' own screen-fixed HUD pieces stack in the same corners and big effects spill onto a neighbor. A step with `place` (Minotaur's horse walks in from the screen edge he faces) or `edgeOnly` (a helper that walks toward her or whose throw takes his own side: a dog passing her by would take the next pair's giver or receiver) plays only in an edge slot facing that edge, so all its helper can meet beyond her is the screen edge; in a middle slot it stops with a note. At the far left the pair is mirrored (he faces left). A companion's step is `edgeOnly` too (it spawns behind him and goes for the nearest enemy), and the other way round: he faces the other pairs, so it spawns between him and the screen edge (mirrored at the far right). A summon's hit is a throw and hits once (`hitonce` defaults to 1 for throws), and his own receiver stands first in its way. Givers that branch on team mode behave as in Simul (Brian's scene zooms are off, by his own guard).
- **The picker** (Tab) freezes the fight behind it (`togglePause`; re-asserted every frame so the Pause key cannot unfreeze it) and lists the pairs on screen (with two or more, in their colors) > giver > receiver (with position counts) > **position** (each shown by its base step's group and label, numbered as the pair's positions). Enter puts the highlighted pair in the active pair's place, or makes a pair already on screen active and shows a picked position of it in place, at its base (its versions, speeds and climax are the keys' once it shows); Insert adds it at the right (at four it says there is no room); Delete takes the active pair off the screen; Backspace, Left or the b button go back a column and close from the first. Its keys are the players' menu tokens (`getInput(-1, {tok})` in the V1 text, `getAction` in the V2 text), and the engine fires a token once a frame, so each is read once. The fight is unpaused only once no menu or fighting key is still held: unpaused while Enter was down, the first free frame gave it to P1 as a Start press, which toggles DongHwan's afterimage and screen-shake variable. Tab is registered inside `run()` and passes to `SceneViewerCycle` outside the gallery - the Scene Viewer's mod loads after this one and registers Tab too, and a later registration of a key replaces an earlier one. Esc with the picker open still leaves the whole gallery (the engine's Esc cannot be stopped from Lua). A pad can move and confirm in the picker but cannot open it. A giver's companion is an entry of its own right after him ("Bao (Brian)": its name and his first name when that is a word, so the entry fits its column with its count): its pairs are his (the same records, no duplicate pair), listed with the number of its positions in each, and its column lists only its positions, numbered as the pair's; Enter and Insert load his pair at the picked position's base (from the receiver column, its first position unless the pair is at one of its steps, then that position's base). The picker opens on that entry when the active pair is at one of its steps. The portraits at the top right are his. A receiver's helper is a receiver of its own in his column, right after her root, with its position count ("Chichi (Dr.Kira)  (3)" after "Dr.Kira Daidouji  (4)" under DongHwan); the receiver column's help says "Right positions"; its portraits are her root's, the character the pair loads.

**`-hgallery 1` on the command line opens it straight from the title** (or `-hgallery "<giver def>|<receiver def>"` at that pair; a receiver's helper's pair, which loads the same two, `"<giver def>|<receiver def>|<helper id>"`); `-hgallerylog 1` prints each phase and action (`[hgallery] pair i/n scene j/m <phase> recv=<her state> his=<his state>`; `act k/K <mode> <command>`, `act k/K done t=<frames>`, `inplace`, `replay`, `failed`, `cannot act from his <state>`, `place: ...`, and `leave frames=<F> in=<I>` when a step is left: how long it was on screen after it first showed and how much of that in its own states), which is what the headless test reads. The overlay puts the group on a line of its own and cuts a line too long for the screen. The autostart runs from the `main.menu.loop` hook, which fires before the title's logo storyboard, so leaving an autostarted gallery goes through the logo to the title.

**A gallery names one build's characters, so it never outlives the build.** The desktop export writes the script and the hook together or removes both, and the config line follows the hook (a listed common-states file that is missing fails character loading; a pair the engine cannot load stops it). The web build's [Common] is the build's whole (vfs.js), so it follows by itself.

**The script's main chunk sits near gopher-lua's register cap, so its top-level locals are kept few (the register rule).** gopher-lua compiles a function only while its registers - its locals plus the temporaries of its widest expression - stay within 200 (`maxRegisters`, compile.go); over it the engine's mod loader panics with `register overflow(too many local variables)` and the gallery never starts. At the first tier hgallery.lua's top level had 184 locals and used 195 registers on the Main bundle's pairs (59 pairs, 2,451 steps): room for 5 more (the 6th failed). The widest point was the `-hgallery` autostart loop at the script's end, where every top-level local is live. (The lean's first version had added 7 while `test-gallery.js`, compiling a script made from its smaller test data with one register to spare, still passed: why the run test reads the server's real build.) **The rule:** a setting is a field of `K`, a color one of `COL`, a draw cache one of `UI` (the three are declared together right after DATA's guard; each old declaration stays where it was, with its comment, as a field assignment: `K.PRESS_EVERY = 20`, `UI.font, UI.sprites = nil, {}`), state lives in a table (`G`, `MATCH`, `LEAN`, `MODE`), and the autostart runs in a function of its own (`do local function autostart() ... end autostart() end`; not `;(function() ... end)()`, which right after the `main.f_appendItemname(...)` call is parse-ambiguous). A new setting or piece of state is a field of one of these tables, never a new top-level local; a prototype mode's locals belong inside its own `MODE.add` function (§4.10c: a 40-local chunk costs the main chunk nothing, measured). After the rule: 150 top-level locals, 156 registers, room for 44 after `LEAN`; with the prototype modes' `MODE` table (one local) room 43, 157 of 200, on every build the round made; the widest point is now the `main.f_appendItemname(...)` call. In K: ENTER_MAX, PATIENCE, PATIENCE_CAP, PRESS_EVERY, MASH_EVERY, SLIP, REPLAY, SUMMON_MAX, RBACK, HGAP, ACCEL, ACCEL_MAX, ZOOMS, FOLLOW, SETUP_SLOTS, SET_SLOTS (and since the fix pass GRACE); in COL: WHITE, GRAY, NAVC, BLACK, DIM, LIGHT, GOLD, GREEN, TITLE, SELF, SELU, COLORS; in UI: font, sprites, ovRect, mrects, mtexts, pickerSprites, pickerRects, pkPortraits. A second wave (MAX_SLOTS, SPACING, GAP, MARGIN, RELEASE_KEYS, RAW, MOVES, NAV_KEYS, NAV_NOTE, SETUP_PHASES into K, about 10 more registers) is held in reserve. JS-side constants (REACH_MID, REACH_EDGE, INTRO_MAX) cost the script no local. **Measured** with `go run tools/luacheck.go <file> --room <marker>` (cwd: the engine checkout): after the usual OK line it prints `ROOM: n`, how many dummy top-level locals still compile when inserted right after the marker's line (a binary search). Insert them where new state would go: dummies appended at the end of the file find 16 more than there are, because state declared early shifts every later expression. `test-gallery.js` asserts room >= 30 after `local LEAN = ` on each script it builds (plain, with a companion, with a receiver's helper) and that none of the 36 renamed names is a top-level local again; `test-gallery-run.js` saves the script the server built (`<out>/hgallery.lua`, the full pair data) and asserts it compiles under the engine's gopher-lua and keeps room >= 30 before anything runs. The rename was proven pure: on the Main data and all 23 inputs `test-gallery.js` hands gallery.js, the hook is byte-identical and the old script with the same rename is textually the new one once the refactor's own lines are mapped back, and gopher-lua's bytecode shows the same 112 globals in both with no local or parameter named after a renamed name (a missed rename would be a new global; one left in place on purpose failed both checks).

Tests: `tools/test-gallery-data.js` (the data), `tools/test-gallery-rules.js` (the walk's rules, one tiny synthetic giver each, written to the system temp and read back through gallerydata.js and modlib.hScan, with a negative control where one is cheap - the same fixture with the one thing the rule reads taken away: NAV ROLES, TIMED LADDERS, ANIM HUBS with the grab's animation gate, nested summons and `clearAlso`, a summon's lead-in, the gauge and buff climaxes, Win/Lose/MatchOver read 0, an AnimTime behind a redirect, random siblings, grab twins, hScan's fallback, probe-window, dangling and self-asked doors; then every fix-pass rule above, the prototype modes' data seams, and the corpus where it is on this machine, the zip's givers with GALLERY_OCA; about 3 s. Two facts a fixture must respect, both rules of the walk: a state in 5000-5999 is never a scene, and a grab whose actions have no Clsn1 is dropped. A rule the header states that the code does not keep yet is a KNOWN GAP line, counted apart, never a pass), `tools/test-galreach.js` (the reach model: synthetic dash, standing, no-Clsn1, apex and lead, the projectile and the front stand with a control; corpus Mina 83, Succubus 133, White-Len none, Allosaurus, Creatures 107, FutamaruPlus, Tendril, Brian), `tools/test-gallery.js` (the generated files without an engine: the trim of version-2 steps and what it drops, the per-build hook with its command lines, Shift-JIS bytes and slots, the config line, the desktop files; parses the script under gopher-lua) and `tools/test-gallery-run.js` (the mode played headless: on the gallery the server builds for a scratch bundle, its script compiled under gopher-lua first, `--chars donghwan,cvsmika_h` and `--extra <folder>` for a giver outside the Main bundle, every scene of a pair reaching a listed receiver state and whether it was reached in place or by grabbing again; the walks step through every step in the data's order with `]` and `[` (bound under `-hgallerylog` only); `--nav <KEY,...>` plays the player's keys instead (RIGHT/LEFT, UP/DOWN, END/DELETE, SPACE, HOME, PAGEDOWN/PAGEUP, INSERT/H, SHOT): each move must land where the data's `k` says (and Space off back where the climax was turned on) and show that step's states, a key with nothing to do must say so and stay; `--space-after` then leaves, starts a training match through a test mod (injected, F6; it wraps debug.lua's `full`) and presses Space: the engine's full(1..8) must run there and never inside the gallery, none with `--debug-keys-off` (the config's AllowDebugKeys = 0), none with `--no-space-back` (its negative control: the line that gives Space back shut); `--hand` walks a hand-written DongHwan x R. Mika gallery of all four positions with their speeds, climaxes and auto and asserts every step after the first grab, and both wraps, in place; `--data <file>` walks any hand-written version-2 gallery; `--pair <text>` walks that pair; `--multi <pair>,<pair>...` plays up to four pairs side by side, adding each with the picker, stepping the active one in place while the others must keep playing (a grab alone whose scene ended by itself and is grabbed again - Kula's invasion throw drops her to 5100 about every 2 s - is that pair's own replay, not a key reaching it: a reset of the same scene after it showed, from a state outside its states and alsoStates), and deleting them again, with the reload timings and no receiver in another pair's scene; `--zoom <KEY,...>` (with `--multi`, once every pair is on screen) plays the zoom's keys (1-4, PLUS, SHIFTPLUS, KPPLUS, MINUS, KPMINUS, SHOT): each move must ask the camera to its pin and the camera must come to rest there at that scale (`camera still at <x> scale <z> (asked ...)`, with every fighter's place), every other pair playing on (no reset or grab of it but a grab alone's own replay), a key with nothing to do saying so, and with one pair (`--nav PLUS,MINUS`) "zoom is for several pairs"; `--add-after <pair>` (with `--jump`) Inserts one more pair once the jumps are made, so an edge-only step left at the far right is pushed between two pairs and must stop with its note, then play again when the deletes make it the far right pair; `--from <n>` starts the walk at scene n and, after the last one walked, steps once more (a pair with many scenes: Kur0maru's summons are his last); every run fails a grab at which one of his summoned helpers is still out, and `--no-kill` (with `--hand` or `--data`) is its negative control, the hook's kill lines shut, where a grab after a dog step must find the dog still out; every run also fails a companion grab whose pinned variable is not the step's value or whose family lands elsewhere than the same pin did before, or that came later than 90 frames after the stance (its own AI waits 60 ticks in its idle state and grabs only from 20-50 px): `--no-pin` and `--no-cgrab` (with `--data`) are their negative controls, the hook's pin lines or its companion grab line shut; every run also fails a companion step that shows two arts (the log's `companion art: its anim <a>, her anim <b>` each time one shows: its anim's thousands, or hers in one state of hers), with `--no-art-pin` (with `--data`) its negative control, the art pins and his copy of one left out; `--no-meter-pin` (with `--data`) leaves its meter pins out (the data marks them `meter`), and then no climax or phase step may show within 600 frames, the patience of its wait; `--revisit <n>` goes back and forth between the last two scenes walked, and a move in place to a companion's position must show her only the two steps' states on the way, with no new grab; `--race-grab 1|2` (with `--data`) makes a scene key on the grab's one tick from inside the driver (into a companion's step: it must summon first and grab within 90 frames; out of one: it must reset first, no companion out at the grab), `--no-race-fix` its negative control; `--pick-companion` picks a companion's entry in the picker (its receivers with its step counts, its scene column only its steps) and shows its second step; `--dwell <ms>` stays on each scene and fails one that spent under 40% of it in its own states - a step that shows for a moment and drifts; a re-grab of a step of the running grab counts against it only when an in-place switch missed, not when the scene had ended by itself or `from` sent it back; `--shots <ms>,<ms>,...` takes each scene's screenshots at those times after it shows, for a scene that plays its phases in one state of hers - the log gives her animation as it changes in a companion's step, `her anim <a>`). No gamepad reaches the page (`navigator.getGamepads` gives none): headless Chrome reads the machine's pads, and a pad in use on the owner's PC pressed P1's buttons on the active giver in the middle of a walk (his y got Bao off her, his b moved it on a position). The controls are played there too: `-hgallerylog` prints each fighter's held raw input when it changes (`input P<n> <keys>`, the character's own `inputTime`), a receiver standing in her own walk, jump, crouch or run state (`MOVED P<n>`), and the controls as the gallery leaves them (`left remap=`). The walks change pairs with Page Down / Page Up, hold P2's Left from a new pair's reset until her scene shows (the action happens - the previous position - and she reads nothing), check that P1's keys reach only the active giver (with DongHwan as pair 2, a held Up moves him to his position 2 while pair 1 plays on), that no receiver read a key in the whole run, and, with the fight paused by the Pause key, that Insert takes the overlay area and every marker-colored pixel away and brings them back, across a reload too (H, with the picker open, too). A receiver's helper's steps log the action she is drawn with each time one shows (`helper art: her anim <a>`), and the run fails one outside her art (the data's `receiver.helper.art`: the bridge's targets; a number of her root's own is the root's body on her), and fails if her root is ever grabbed (`ROOT TAKEN`); between the shows her watch logs every change of her action, its sprite group and how many of the explods the hook removes on her are up (`helper watch: her anim <a> group <g> hidden explods <n>`; `spriteVar` gives the engine's raw nil for a sprite-less action, which `tostring` cannot take outside a pcall), and the run fails an action outside her art and her own states' (`receiver.helper.own`) or any such explod up - `--no-hide` (with `--data`) is its negative control, the hook's +1 removal lines shut, where DongHwan's 43434 is up on her through every intro; `--no-badge` (with `--data` and a pair whose giver the gallery gives her badge) shuts the hook's badge lines: her own immunity holds, as in a real fight, and his throw must never catch her (asserted from the log: grabs made at her, no show, no ROOT TAKEN; the scenes' own checks are the control's); `--orig <folder>/<file>` swaps that file of a scratch character copy for its `.orig`, and `--orig dr_kira_update/k-2.cns` with `--data` and her pair is the negative control of both art checks (her bridge gone: every show and the watch give Kira's own numbers, the screenshots a double-size Kira); `--picker-shot` opens the picker on the walked pair and saves it (its rows are the positions of the entry it opens on: a companion's, after `--pick-companion`). A step with a re-roll logs his state and hers, each with the one before it, whenever they change (`reroll watch: his <state> prev <state> her <state> prev <state>`): a re-roll shows as the drawing state entered from the one the hook took him out of, her in the step's state entered from the branch's (his 6005 prev 70002, her 6205 prev 72002: set back before she ran, so never drawn). `--p2-live` (with `--hand` or `--data`) is the negative control: the same gallery with the receivers' input left on, where the watch must see her take the held Left and walk. The harness hides the machine's gamepads from the page (`navigator.getGamepads` returns none): a pad on the test PC fed P1 button noise into the runs at AILevel 0, which closed the picker with an a press and completed Brian's AI_nn commands, turning his own AI grab on in the middle of a companion's summon. The desktop export's stock v1.0.0 engine runs the same hook and driver: `Ikemen_GO.exe -hgallery 1 -hgallerylog 1` prints the same log to stdout.

`test-gallery-run.js`, round 2: `--modes <id,...|none>` writes the other prototypes into the scratch roster's `modsOff` (and builds a `--hand` or `--data` gallery with the same modules), so a run plays only what it proves; `--mode-file <file.js>` adds a fixture mode to a hand-written gallery; `--control <scene,...>` marks negative-control scenes that must NOT show; a step counts as shown in what its last action waits for when that is more than its `states` (a KO after-the-match step's `herOn`).

## 4.10c Prototype modes: mob givers, characters that are galleries, KO scenes

Three kinds of giver play scenes the core gallery (§4.10b) has no way to play: givers who bring a mob of helpers that do the grabbing, characters whose files ARE a gallery (a pose menu, a director), and scenes that come only with her KO or after the match. Each is a PROTOTYPE MODE: one module in `gallerymodes/`, plugged into generic seams of gallerydata.js and gallery.js, with a Mods tab row of its own, ON by default, removable at any time (the owner's call, 2026-10-07). With every mode off the data is the core's byte for byte and the hook is the core's; the script differs only by the seam lines. With every mode on, over the 120 givers of §4.10b (best of R.Mika and Kung Fu Girl Z): steps 2,623 -> 3,247, real positions 370 -> 570, positions with speeds 359 -> 447, climaxes 409 -> 564, reached scenes 2,556 -> 2,869, givers with no pair 16 -> 10; 37 rows gain, none loses anything. Main: 35 KO steps (Kur0maru, Brian, Minotaur), nothing else changes. Every module's header comment has its rules in full; what follows is the map.

### The switch, and how to remove a prototype

- **In code**: `gallerymodes/index.js` lists them - ROWS (id, Mods add-on id `hgallery-<id>`, label, about, what turning it off loses) and LOAD (literal requires, so make-portable's require check follows them). A mode is `gallerymodes/<id>.js`; its helper files are `gallerymodes/<id>-<part>.js`, required by it (mob.js -> mob-rt.js; ko.js -> ko-data.js, ko-rt.js; self.js asks self-director.js when present). Ids match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,11}$/`, are no Lua keyword and no step field's name. make-portable.js and make-kit.js copy the folder whole.
- **Per bundle**: modmgr.js builds one row per ROWS entry right after the gallery's own (`hgallery-mob`, `hgallery-self`, `hgallery-ko`): hOnly, ON by default, `files` [] (a mode rides inside the gallery's two files), present only where the gallery's row is ("Only a build with the H gallery has it."), and off whenever that row is off, so the tab never names a mode in a bundle without the gallery (H stays hidden until found). Stored in `roster.modsOff` like any add-on. `gallerymodes.enabled(roster)` gives the modules whose rows are on; `idsOn(roster)` their ids; `load(ids)` serves the tests and `node gallerydata.js --modes <ids|all>`. `buildForRoster` hands the same modules to the data and to the files; a registry that throws means no mode, never no gallery.
- **Failure stays inside the mode.** Only a mode that is on is ever required, inside try/catch: a module that throws or names itself with another id is left out with a warning. A read or pair that throws leaves that mode out for that giver or pair (cached, so every build gives the same data). A mode whose trim, Lua or hook lines throw, or that the files cannot carry (not ASCII, not one `MODE.add`, a line break in a line, a gate the hook does not have), is left out and the files are built again without it - files identical to the build without that mode. At run time an error in a mode's hook switches that mode off for the session ("H gallery: mode <id> is off"); its steps stop with "its mode is off" and the gallery goes on.
- **To remove a prototype**: delete its file(s), its ROWS and LOAD lines and its tests. Nothing else names it: the shared suites (tools/test-mods.js, tools/test-gallery-modes-data.js) read the list from ROWS, and with each prototype removed in turn (a preload that drops its rows and makes its files unrequirable) both still pass, 135 and 45. The director alone: delete `gallerymodes/self-director.js` and its test (the hub stays, the summon's core step comes back).

### The seams: what a mode may do

**Data** (`buildGalleryData` opts.modes; gallerydata.js PROTOTYPE MODES). `read(base, ctx)` once per giver base (kept with it, so by his files' signature): ctx gives his base's readers (`base.fns`, not enumerable: his walker W, standingGrab, issuesCustom, issuesAtOnce, HIT_GATE, trigTxt, xMoves, helperReach), the mode's own memo and a library (gallerydata's exports, cnsexpr, scenelib, modlib). A null answer leaves him out of the mode. `pair(G, R, ctx)` answers null or { steps, claims?, counts?, setup? }, cached like a core pair; ctx adds what read answered, `walk()` (his walk for her), the pair's judging, `pairSteps` (walk-shaped steps judged for her, carrying `ext`, `withCtrl`, `noGrab` and `step[<id>]`) and `finishPair`. A mode's steps carry `ext: <id>` and its own fields under `step[<id>]`, and go AFTER the core steps of the pair, so core indices hold; CLAIMS put them in place of core steps instead, at the first claimed step's index (the claimed grab's position order is kept). A claim is a list of his grabs (honored only for a grab one of the mode's own steps enters by; never a companion's step) or a predicate; a mode never claims another mode's steps. Where the core has no pair for her, the mode's steps make one at the giver's place in the list. A mode's `counts` are added to the pair's (a scene it now reaches: +1 to its verdict, -1 to unreachable, never below 0). Mode steps never enter a receiver's-helper pair (Dr. Kira's Chichi). Givers only a mode understands but hScan does not detect are not added this round. **The gate**: `makeWalker` opts.gate { round, over, herAlive, herLife } reads RoundState, MatchOver/Win/WinKO (1 when `over`; Lose*, WinTime, WinPerfect stay 0), her alive and her life as the gate says; a gated walker never shares a cache. The KO mode walks with it; nothing KO-specific is in the core.

**Runtime** (gallery.js PROTOTYPE MODES). trimData keeps a step or action with `ext` only while its mode is on and hands it to the mode's `trimStep` / `trimAction`, which copy its fields runtime-ready into `out[<id>]` (or drop it with a reason). `zss(t, lib)` gives lines in the root's -4 block, blocks after the companions' and in [StateDef +1], each under `# ==== prototype mode <id> ...`, and GATES on four core lines - noKo (GlobalNoKO and its kin), refill (life < lifeMax / 2), cut (the intro cut) and recvInput (her NoInput) - a gated line runs only while every mode's condition holds (ANDed); the mode's own maps are `_gal_<id>_*`. `lua(t, lib)` gives one ASCII chunk, `MODE.add('<id>', function() local M = {} ... return M end)`, placed after every core local: it sees the driver's locals as upvalues and its own locals are its function's registers (no top-level local, ever). The `MODE` table (one top-level local after LEAN) runs every hook through a pcall. The hooks, each a no-op for a step of no mode: place, grab (in place of `changeState(entry)`), drive (its own phases `<id>:<name>`), inScene (may widen the scene test, never narrow it), act (for one of its actions; true hands the tick on to the command or jump), status (overlay words), tick, live (run outside round state 2), inPlace, reset, frame, match (before a match loads) and after (a match that ended by itself; `{ what = 'again' }` loads the same pairs again, kept). Per-pair state lives in `G.m` only. The overlay and the picker mark a mode's step with its id ("scene 3/9: [ko] ..."). Two step fields are the core's for any step: `withCtrl` (his commands act while he stands in a basic state with control: a command his -1 takes only on ctrl) and `noGrab` (no `changeState`: the path starts after the place; until her first scene shows, being out of one is where it starts, within its patience; never reached in place).

### Mob givers (`gallerymodes/mob.js` reads, `mob-rt.js` plays)

A mob giver brings his helpers on her, many of them and of several kinds, and they do the grabbing (towerofbloodyfight and tobf+, Gnoll Raid2, MR1_ProjectRose, ZHE's Futas, Colette's strikers, WrestlerX's heels, GoblinParty). The core walk saw each kind as one summon whose helper plays every scene at random; the mode gives each MEMBER TYPE steps of its own, position by position, with ONE member on her at a time (onlookers are not spawned).
- **MEMBER**: a helper id (never his companion's) that a Helper of his spawns by a ROUTE, that can be out more than once (`NumHelper(id) < N`, N >= 2, a count variable, or two Helpers of it in one state), and whose own states hold a GRAB. A member out only once is the mode's only where the core knows no summon of it and has no step of his at all (Colette's striker, GoblinParty, WrestlerX's Heel_inv); a dog or a god summoned one at a time stays the core's (Sanae's Suwako and Kanako).
- **ROUTES**: *press* - a Helper in his -1/-2/-3 that fires for a human root in his idle (AILevel 0, round state 2, his ctrl on, his helpers absent and their variables at 0, his variables at 0 or where the pair's setup holds them) on exactly one playable command and not without it (TOBF's a/b/c/x; a press that would also start a move of his is none); *press into a state* - a Helper in a state S of his that his negative states enter on one playable command, S's first tick reading the command (WrestlerX's Heel1 by zombieb); *present* - one is always out (Colette's striker); *state* - a Helper in a state a fight can enter (ZHE's summon state 100000), its first time atom its `after`. AI-only Helpers and those the pair's setup keeps shut are no route. A COUNT GATE a state route compares (`var(53) < 2`) is held in the step's setup.
- **TYPES, GRABS, FAMILIES**: a variable some member's idle writes that a hit's p1/p2stateno or a ChangeState reads, differing between the kinds that grab, is a TYPE PIN (TOBF's var(15): Zombie 0, Skeleton 2, Ghoul 4, Titan 3); a root variable that sends the member into its grab is a ROOT TYPE held on him (Colette's `root,var(40) = 3`). Its grab is a standingGrab HitDef its idle reaches (`affectteam = F`, a grab only his own side takes, is none); a variable the grab state draws at random that the hit or a later state goes on by gives a FAMILY per value, pinned (the Ghoul's fvar(1); GoblinParty's var(49): 324 / 350).
- **ITS MACHINE** per family, read with the walker from p1stateno, pins frozen: positions (p1stateno where it is a base, else what it goes on to; a draw that never comes back is the intro pick: the Zombie's 16667 -> 162998 or 164000), speeds (a loop's states), phases (meter rungs below the top, the meter at the rung's middle), climax (the top's states, the meter one past it; with no meter, a state the speeds go on to by time alone: ZHE's 7483 -> 7489). Animation-keyed members (the Bao clones 41401/41488) are read like a companion's play. A held state that leaves on `time >= N` (N >= 60) restarts at N - 1. Her states that change themselves on her grabber's state read off the hit are hers while the member is in it.
- **STEPS**: group = the Helper's name; "the grab (press a)" (one per family), then "pos k, intro", "pos k, speed i", "pos k, phase j", "pos k, climax"; the grab step waits for her first scene and those its grab state passes on to in its first ticks (ZHE's 7477 -> 7480), and holds its grab state. The mode CLAIMS the core's summon steps whose `clear` is a member id (TOBF's union "the grab", ZHE's 100000).
- **PLAYED** (mob-rt.js): his route made (the spawn command pressed on his root every PRESS_EVERY ticks once his state time reaches `after`, or the summon state entered); the newest instance of the member taken once one more is out than at the grab, after 2 ticks and its settle states; then THE JUMP - the hook stands it `gap` past her on her far side, facing her, and selfStates it into its grab state, so its AI's random, distance and life gates never decide and it never walks into another pair (not taken in 15 ticks: asked again, 3 times per grab). Every other instance of the member id goes (with its explods); the one that plays takes its pins every frame, its position and its hold. Member ids join the kill list, so a reset removes them. No member in SUMMON_MAX ticks: "his mob sent no <who>". Log: "mob: its <state> restarted at <time>".
- **THE CUT (a cut cleans what it cuts).** The hook's jump into a step's position (a change in place) and a hold's restart take the member out of the author's flow: his own way into position 2 passes 164000, whose RemoveExplod with no ID clears every layer, and the jump skips it. So in the same hook block, before the SelfState, the member's own explods go (RemoveExplod with no ID, which also takes Colette's no-ID pictures 7520-7524) and it sets its own `_gal_mob_cut`; its child helpers (made after it, so run after it) destroy themselves recursively with their explods on that frame (`time > 0` spares one the new state makes on that tick; `parentExist` comes first, because a parent redirect on a helper whose parent is gone writes the engine's console every frame); the member clears the mark on the next frame. Its -2 status explods come back the same frame, and the new state's time-0 layers are made after the cut. A change in place never replays the grab. Played: Bloody Tower x Yoko, five moves in place, no layer twice; the near-black share left of the pos 2 pair 39.60% -> 0.28%; Colette x R.Mika 7520, 7521, 7523, never two at once. The children half is unproven in the engine (no child was out during a move).
- **AN INTRO FREEZES.** A "pos k, intro" step (nav speed 0) plays once and holds its last frame instead of restarting its animation (which replayed the Zombie's 257-tick insertion forever and lost its time-0 layer 3343, removetime -2, from the second loop on: the Gnoll's head). Its hold carries `freeze` and `explods` (the Explods its state makes on an exact first tick that live at least as long as their animation; Gnoll's random line 905150, removetime 200, is not one): the member gets AssertSpecial animfreeze at animTime >= -2, its layers ModifyExplod animfreeze, and she is frozen through `_gal_mob_hz` on her root while the step shows. Any other step releases it; the cut removes the frozen layer. An intro with a time exit (ZHE/Colette's 7480, restart 242) still restarts: a freeze cannot stop the state's clock. Played: Bloody Tower x R.Mika and x Yoko (two late shots pixel-identical, 3343 still up past 257 ticks, speed 1 moving after END); Gnoll Raid2 x Jill keeps the Gnoll's head.
- **HE IS NEVER A TARGET** while a mob step plays: NotHitBy SCA in slot 7 every frame `_gal_mob_id` != 0. Colette's support HitDefs carry `affectteam = B` (the author's TODO) and took Colette herself, so every 7470-family grab read "did not start". Played: Colette x R.Mika, the grab in 1410, then speeds in place. (Only her support's Lv3, the purple lady, `root,var(40) = 3`, does H; the steps already hold var(40) = 3, so her intro menu's choice changes nothing in the gallery.)
- **HIS CAMERA CURSORS** (`cams`): helpers of his (no member, companion or summon) whose own state holds the camera with a ScreenBound whose movecamera x is nonzero on a trigger that always fires - TOBF's and ZHE's 22401 "Camera", the author's cursor his fwd/back walks, drawn as the floating Kuromaru head (in Bloody Tower a red-suited man at 1/256 alpha: the "invisible fighter" the camera chased). For a pair with them the driver sets `_gal_mob_cam` from the match's first frame (the round intro already pulled the view); in +1 the cursor is invisible and leaves the camera alone. Only one is kept (his -2 brings one back whenever none is out): his round state 1001 spawns another at its time 0, which every reset passes (Bloody Tower, Gnoll Raid2, Project Rose - "they keep multiplying"), and that newcomer goes on its first tick, before it is drawn. Played: Gnoll Raid2 x Jill, one cursor across three loads (before: 2, then 3), no heads, camera steady.
- **AN AWAY ROOT** (`away`): his idle is his state 0 plus the states it and his negative states reach with no command and no AI; where it PosSets him off the ground on a line that certainly fires (TOBF's 1000, Y = -999, and 1001 then off the stage), the root is held beside her in +1 through mob:out/enter/act/show - GAP behind her as the place stood him, on the ground, facing as placed, no player push, moving the camera only while `_gal_free` = 0 - so pairCenter, the markers and the side the member is stood on read a true place. Colette, WrestlerX and ZHE are not away; GoblinParty is not either (its state 0 hides P1 only on a name its attacher's target has: a HYPOTHESIS that it is away at run time). Played: one pair, the root at her - 36, camera 0; two pairs, each root 36 from its receiver, the zoom on pair 2 asked at 85 (before 361.5).
- **OWN ID.** A member's grab HitDefs, its reach walk and the grabbing filter are read with IsHelper(N) against the member's own helper id (cnsexpr `ctx.helperId`: IsHelper(N >= 0) is N = that id, as char.go; a negative N or IsHelper(N, index) stays unknown). A member with no grab that fires for its own id is no member: WrestlerX's Momo 47400 catches her only as his Royal Rumble copy (`isHelper(7442)`, p1stateno 27477) and for its own id is a plain hit, so its 16 "Momo2nd" steps (a hammer hitting the ground over and over) are gone. A member's name may start with a digit ("1stBruiser"); a name with "_" is still refused ("Bruiser_inv" stays "helper 27401").
- **THE SETTLED HOLD.** A hold names the animation its state settles on: the state's own ChangeAnim/ChangeAnim2 lines that fire on every tick under the pins (`anim = <a>` plus pinned variables, a literal value) are followed. Project Rose's Skeleton in 22303 holds 27231, not 7231 (the hook and the state swapped the animation every tick, both explod layers could be made). A speed that settles on another speed's animation is that speed (the Skeleton's pos 2: 3 speeds and 2 climaxes, not 6 and 4); a keyed animation the state never shows under the pins is another kind's.
- **BORROWED ART.** His PEERS are the characters beside him in the build's characters folder that ship, by name, every state file a member's idle and grab come from, and a sprite file of his sprite file's name. If he drew some member type anew (none of its idle/grab sprites matches a peer's), a member whose idle and grab sprites all match one peer's, pixel for pixel with the palette ignored, wears the base's art: its steps' labels start with "[base art]" (after a leading "(violent)" / "(experimental)"). Marked: Project Rose's Skeleton (tobf's yellow-and-pink thug 1110/1121/27230, with the new wolf 17220 in pos 1) and Gnoll Raid2's Titan (tobf's Titan). TOBF and TOBF+ mark nothing: neither redrew a member type, so they are versions of one character. +190 ms cold over the 9 mob givers, memoized per file signature; the mode's reading is cached on his own files' signature, so a peer's changed files show after a restart.
- **HER RELAYS.** Her states of his that change on her grabber's state (`PlayerID(GetHitVar(fall.envshake.ampl)),stateno = N`) are followed through the ones with no art of their own (GoblinParty's 334, her LAS initial, the one tick between its 324 and 325; 351 between 350 and 352). A state of the member where she is in a relay is one of its scenes (go.in, the in-place search), never a step's `until`. Before, the chain 4001 -> 334 -> 335 stopped at 4001 and GoblinParty read as one position.
- **ANIMATION BY OFFSET** (read before a family's other readings). A state P whose animation is `K + var(V)` (its header - 325: `551121019 + var(45)` - or a first-tick ChangeAnim on its own variables' values - 352: `551121045 + var(53)`), where her state keys her animation on his (her 335's ChangeAnim2 on `PlayerID(GetHitVar(...)),anim = 551121020..044`, or `enemy,anim`): each keyed N is an offset N - K. POSITIONS are the rows of the TABLE writing var(V) on one key `var(W) = k` in the machine state nearest before P (4000: "CHOOSES DOGGY TO PLAY" var(45) = 0 on var(51) = 1, then 5, 15, 10, 20), in key order, named by the rows' labels minus their shared words. SPEEDS: LAS, the row's value plus each pass of its RELAY's first-tick VarAdd (324 at `time = 1`), up to THE LADDER'S END: the value P's way back to its relay excludes (`anim != 551121024 && ...`) is the pass after which the pose leaves for good - its AFTERMATH ("AFTER CUM" in her 335) - the pass before it its CLIMAX ("CUM", where her -2 takes life), the passes before that its speeds ("SEC 1-3"). (Read at first as the climax: Space played the aftermath and the climax was "speed 4/4" - the owner's report.) HAS: the values a row draws (`random%4 + 6`) are its speeds; the climax is a row of the same key on a further condition ("CUMMING", `var(52) = 10`, held 0 on the speeds); ITS AFTERMATH is a first-tick ChangeAnim of P to a literal animation her state keys on, asking the row's key and a flag P raises on the climax's animation (352: `var(51) = 1 && var(54) = 1` -> 454541211; "AFTER CUM VARIABLE" var(54) = 1 on `anim = 551121049`), held with that key and flag and var(50) = 0. The aftermath is the climax's second picture: Space shows the climax, Delete / End step to "after the climax". Each step pins var(V) and the line's conditions, holds P at K + offset, restarts it before a time exit (325: 300), and goes to the relay. AN OFFSET POSE RE-ENTERS: its layers are Explods keyed on its animation, persistent 0, so another animation re-enters P after the cut. THE HEAD FIRST: the go acts from the states where her state follows the relay; elsewhere it first takes the member to the state hers follows from there (`via`: 4002 -> 4000 -> 324), the second jump a tick later (she sees his state of the tick before); read over every family's machine, never from the grab state. GoblinParty: 10 positions (LAS 1-5, HAS 6-10: doggy, front missionaire, bottom cowgirl, front missionaire var 2, blowjob); LAS 3 speeds, HAS 4; a climax and an aftermath each: 55 steps.
- **THE AUTHOR'S BIND.** Ikemen 1.0.0 drops an Explod's authored bindID when its postype is p1 (the Explod's Run applies `bindid`, then setPos's p1 branch binds it to its owner again: bytecode.go, char.go Explod.setPos). GoblinParty's 325/352 layers are `postype = p1`, `bindid = PlayerID(helper(4711 + var(22)),var(0)),id`, and the goblin parks itself at y 9999999999 on 4000/4002's first tick, so its body was drawn there (logged: bind = its own id, y 2147483648) - the owner's "no goblin sex sprites". Where every Explod of the pose state binds to another player by PlayerID, the hold carries `bind` and the hook gives every explod of the member her player id in +1 (`_gal_mob_her`); logged after: bind = her id, x 56, y 0. HYPOTHESIS: versus loses the body the same way on this engine (a fork carry-list candidate: keep an authored bindid after setPos).
  - **HER POSE'S CONTACT POINT** (the hold's `at`). Bound as written, his layers stand at their pos from her (`var(32) - 38`) while her pose (keyed on his) draws her at its first frame's x from her (65 in his .air; Ikemen does not scale a ChangeAnim2 frame offset by her xscale): the goblin sat 27 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 11 toward her head - the owner's "too far to the left on all positions" - in every engine reading (MUGEN 1.1's space = stage is its mirror; his own round-start nudges move it the same way). So the hold carries `at` = her pose's first-frame x less its layers' shared offset (65 - 38 = 27; missionary and cowgirl 20 - 14, blowjob 25 - 14), and in +1 the hook stands the member there (her x + `_gal_mob_at` along her facing), at her height plus THE AUTHOR'S ROUND-START HEIGHT (the hold's `aty`, `_gal_mob_aty`: his layers' y reads a variable of the helper they name - `helper(...),var(33)` doggy, var(35) missionary, var(37) cowgirl, var(39) blowjob - which his attacher's 520 sets at the round's start, `roundstate = [0,1]`, to -8 / -6 / 3 / 6 and back to 0 once the fight runs; the one nonzero round-start literal of that variable in his states is read), facing her, with no player push; its layers stay bound to it as the engine binds them. Without the height the goblin sat too low in doggy and missionary and too high in cowgirl and blowjob (the owner's report, 2026-10-08); her frame's own y offset (-30 / -17 / 20 / 25) was tried first and overshot every pose when played (doggy floating, blowjob at her chest). Played: Yoko and R.Mika, all four poses in contact. (This replaces round 2's ModifyExplod bindid line.) Played: R.Mika, Yoko, Mai, every position.
